reviews.text: bought these, have been skiing with them for  a month a they’re great, for tons of different conditions and different style of skiing they’re great for anything!

reviews.title: Sleeping Bags
reviews.text: I bought these for my kids for backpacking as they have outgrown or will soon outgrow more kid bags. While I would have liked to get down filling, that wasn't in the budget for a big family. These bags are the closest to down as you can get as far as weight, space, and warmth. They are a great budget option. I am actually glad we didn't get more expensive bags for them yet as I can let them take these wherever and I am not paranoid about keeping them in pristine condition. The bags fit in the bottom sleeping bag zip pocket of the kids deuter 40 backpacking pack. Very warm, but probably not long enough for a taller adult.
reviews.author: Evgeny Z

reviews.title: Great bag that keeps you warm
reviews.text: Our family needs sleeping bags that are built to last and this one seems to match this need. My partner feels the cold and this bag keeps her happy and pro ides a good night of warm sleep. Zipper seems solid and the storage bag is well made too
reviews.author: DJ E

reviews.text: Good for 15 degree temps while wearing a light layer. Can’t speak to durability and zipper performance over time.

reviews.title: High Quality..Great Value
reviews.text: My girls have really enjoyed this bag. I would definitely recommend it if you're looking for an affordable bag with quality written all over it.

reviews.title: Good if you like mummy bags
reviews.text: This sleeping bag provided good warmth even below its rated temperature (08 degrees f) but it was too constrictive for our use (that wasn't the bags fault, just personal preference).
reviews.author: John W

reviews.title: Warm, Cozy Bag
reviews.text: Love my BA Anthracite bag. It has kept me warm as I transition into winter camping and is pretty lightweight to pack. Love that I can zip connect it to my boyfriend's BA bag too!
reviews.author: Etta P

reviews.title: Good stuff
reviews.text: My partner wanted a double bag, but I got this to zip up with my anthracite. Its a little bulkier than the male version, but in sure there's science behind that. I usually carry this one in my bag. Im jealous that they get the better colour.

reviews.title: Warm and great for shorter people
reviews.text: This was the perfect size for me (5'2“). Have only used car camping at around 40 degrees so far but was very comfortably warm. I also love the purple color
reviews.author: Elizabeth G

reviews.title: Keeps me warm all night.
reviews.text: This was a much needed upgrade. I find myself camping in high elevation all the time, mainly in the summer and needed something that would keep me warm enough but not too warm. Temperature in this bag is perfect. Keeps me warm but still with enough room to move a bit. I have never been a fan of the tight mummy bags but this provides just enough space for comfort. Definitely would recommend this for car camping, backpacking, or tent camping.

reviews.title: Great beginner backpacking bag
reviews.text: Bought for my wife for a 4 day backpacking trip in the White River NF. Lightweight and packs down small enough to fit in her bag!
reviews.author: Gabriel H

reviews.title: Womens Anthracite 20F
reviews.text:
I bought both the men's and women's Big Agnes Anthracite 20°F sleeping bags, and they've been excellent for three-season camping. The lining is soft and comfortable, not slick like some synthetic bags, and the FireLine Pro Eco insulation keeps warmth even around freezing temps. I've found the men's bag comfortable into the high 20s, and the women's version with extra insulation in the hood and footbox works great for anyone who runs cold.

The design details really stand out: the draft collar, cinchable hood, and smooth zippers make the bag feel more premium than its price tag suggests. You can also zip them together for a roomy double setup, which pairs perfectly with a double pad.

They are a bit bulky and heavier than ultralight down options, but that's expected with synthetic bags. Overall, the Anthracite 20°F is a warm, durable, and budget-friendly choice for reliable comfort outdoors.
reviews.author: Justin W

reviews.title: New England life saver
reviews.text: We purchased this for our New England adventure. Let me tell you it was a game changer. In New York in 32 degree weather we were cozy. In New Hampshire in the flood we were dry warm and out of the wind. We camped New England for 10 days and were cozy each night and it rained and was flooding for three nights. Easy set up even at night. Buy Big Agnes. They know what they are doing. And as a bonus go with the vestibule it was a game changer for sure.
reviews.author: CampingBunny

reviews.title: excellent
reviews.text: great view of the stars and incredibly weather proof.

reviews.title: Best tent ever!  Double vestibule!
reviews.text: We used this tent camping at the lake with the captain comfort double pad and the double sleeping bag, and it is fantastic.  You can see the stars without the mesh and easily pull back the rain fly, and leave attached. There's so much space!  We love the addition of the vestibule and just ordered another one for the other side!  We didn't realize both sides have the potential for adding vestibule, which adds such nice space, it's like two extra rooms!

reviews.title: Love our Big House 6!
reviews.text: Big Agnes pays attention to ALL the details, and I am really glad we invested in this tent. Easy to set up, plenty of room to stand and move about, plenty of storage pockets, and kept us dry in a three-hour rain shower.  Bought the tent footprint separately (glad we did), and look forward to purchasing the "foyer" aka vestibule.  Great product.
reviews.author: Meredith A

reviews.title: Great Family Tent!
reviews.text: I use this tent for camping with my wife and three kids (all under 11), plus our dog. We are able to use our sleeping pads and have space for our pup plus some gear. I'm 5'10" and can easy stand up in the tent with room spare. The corner gear storage is handy. I plan to buy the additional vestibule for added storage space and so I don't have to bring our shoes inside the tent. Overall happy with this purchase.
reviews.author: Chad H

reviews.title: Best tent
reviews.text: Easy setup and lightweight.
reviews.author: Kimberly C

reviews.title: Big Agnes - Big House 6
reviews.text:
This is my first Big Agnes product and they exceeded my expectations. The tent is very well built. Reinforced in all the right places. Plenty of thought went into this design. Getting my wife into camping for her first time. This tent makes it more of a “glamping“ experience so we can both enjoy ourselves. 
Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Big house 6 has been good to us
reviews.text: Bought the big house 6 and vestibule for three people and two dogs(black lab and pointer) this tent has always been more than enough room for us and has been through a lot of rain. We have always been dry and comfortable.

reviews.title: easy set up, spacious, weatherproof car camper
reviews.text: We went camping in Northern NM and when we arrived it was storming pretty good. Ended up putting the tent up in hard rain/small hail easily and quickly. Good design in keeping it simple when it comes to erection. Spacious enough for 2 folks, a double size air mattress, 2 storage boxes full of camp gear, and a couple of duffel bags and still be comfortable. I'm 5'10" and was able to stand up no problem. Kept the weather out and had decent enough airflow to help prevent condensation. Big plus for carrying bag being big enough to store the tent, rainfly, and footprint no problem.  No struggle getting it back in the bag.

reviews.title: Big House 6 for roomy comfort
reviews.text: I used the previous year's version (2024) last  fall at 9500' in the Uintah range. It set up fast and easily as my backpack tents. The  footprint size worked well in small areas and steep wall design kept me upright while inside.
reviews.author: Rhonda

reviews.title: Great Family Tent
reviews.text: We've used this tent several times with our 1-year-old and it is perfect. It has enough room for a chair, a pack-and-play, and our queen air mattress. The good rain protection kept things dry in a severe rainstorm.  I would recommend this tent to a first-time camping family or to seasoned outdoors people looking for a family-sized tent. I would caution anyone using this tent with a pack-and-play to ensure the feet on it have some kind of protection as ours ripped the base of the tent when it was dragged.
reviews.author: paul G

reviews.title: Overall a good tent
reviews.text: Pleased with this tent, overall.  Only complaint is that the zipper tends to get caught in the fabric quite easily.
Great quality, easy to setup and breakdown and pack away.
reviews.author: Nicholas T

reviews.title: Overall great tent
reviews.text: First use of this tent was over 4th of July week in Northern California when temps were well over 100. This tent has great ventilation and cooled down at night with the weather. I also happened to place it on an ant hill that didn't expose itself until nighttime. The tent was covered with ants but not a single one inside. The only reason for four stars is the zippers snag really easily.

reviews.title: Almost Perfect
reviews.text: I used this tent for 14 days straight at Philmont, changing camp every day, plus multiple other trips since. The material held up well through rainy days, and setup took minimal effort each time. The fabric was nice and very light, and the interior space was good and easy for anyone to use. Highly recommend, it was nearly perfect. The only downside was that the poles sometimes had trouble staking compared to previous tents I've used from REI.
reviews.author: Michal O

reviews.title: Solid UL tent
reviews.text: Well built and very packable. Passed all the tests on my latest 4 night river trip.
reviews.author: Michael H

reviews.title: Perfect Tent
reviews.text: I absolutely love this tent.  I've taken it on over 10 backpacking trips, including a 12 day trek at Philmont in the back country of New Mexico, and it always performed like a champ.  It held up to everything from downpours to hail storms and always stayed dry.  The features are incredibly well thought out, making it my favorite tent.  I wouldn't change a thing.
reviews.author: Tim W

reviews.title: A canoe trippers best friend!
reviews.text:
My trip-partner and I each used our Copper Spur UL tents on a remote backcountry canoe trip in Canada and they both performed flawlessly!  We saw varying types of weather, including several extended downpours and enough wind to keep us wind-bound at a campsite for an extra day.  We were both very impressed at their ability to hold up to the elements, yet still incredibly lightweight and surprisingly durable.  What a great feeling to jump into my tent each evening, regardless of the weather.   
I won't hesitate to take my Copper Spur on any future trips.
reviews.author: northbound

reviews.title: Big Agnes Copper Spur UL2
reviews.text:
It's a great tent. In my opinion it has a couple stand out features that I think sets it apart from other tents and make it AMAZING. Now these couple features might be on other tents but none I have seen. 
Firstly, there are loops on the inside that can easily have caribeeners attached or other items. something so small but makes a difference when drying or trying to save space. 
Secondly, speaking of saving space at both ends the above your head and feet respectively is a space that can expand very easily for gear storage. I quite commonly use it to store my stuff sacks, dehydrated food, battery packs, and any other small items. 
Thirdly, the tapered design is perfect for 1 person and a dog comfortably with gear.

Lastly of course the weight of the tent is crazy how much can be so light. This was tested in the backcountry on several weekend and week trips in Idaho. from weather of sun shine and hot to rain and snow.
reviews.author: Liam S

reviews.title: Easypeasy
reviews.text: Nice tent, cool and cozy color!  It doesn't get dark inside the tent when camping near other tents with lights. Though set up and packing is easy and fast. When the tent is wet it dries fast, that's nice too.  Material feels breakable, but it's can handel a lot! Cords could be more visible in daytime, tripped a couple of time due to clumsiness :).  Would not recommend sleeping with 2 persons (im 170cm 68kg female, another me would be too tight and no room for two-person backpaking gear to keep dry in rain. Very comfy as a 1p tent though (reason I bought it).
reviews.author: Kir

reviews.title: The best for most people
reviews.text: The 2 person variant of this tent is perfect for backpacking trips with your dog. The tent has a tapered foot box, so fitting two people in it will require some coordination with sleeping pads, I prefer to keep my pack inside the tent, and there was plenty of room for my sleep system, my dog's sleeping bag, plus my pack/gear. It even kept us dry in a surprise snow storm at elevation. I've also woken up to a soggy rain fly during foggy alpine evenings where the day/night temps vary a lot but the interior has always stayed dry. The footprint is sold separately and is a must have (or make your own). Easy to set up and guy out, good ventilation, roomy and lots of storage.
reviews.author: Max Planck

reviews.title: Excellent backpacking tent
reviews.text: I have owned a Copper Spur UL2 for 9 years now and used it on multiple backpacking trips each summer in the mountains of Colorado. My husband and I find it to be very easy to set up, durable, and lightweight. A couple years ago we noticed some minor wear to the tent and had it repaired by Big Agnes. We thought we might lighten our load a little and try out the Fly Creek but found it did not have high enough sides to protect us from the sudden rain and hail storms at high elevation. We are still using our original Copper Spur to this day and are very happy! I see there are some newer updates to the tent like increased storage inside and the option to convert the vestibule into an awning. I think anyone looking to enjoy the great outdoors would be well served by this tent.
reviews.author: Sierra

reviews.title: Copper Spur UL2 For Bike Tour
reviews.text: I purchased this tent ahead of my 4 month 4000+ mile bike tour through Europe. The combination of low weight / packing size while remaining highly waterproof and robost was a huge win. I prefer free standing tents and think there may not be a better choice. The only time I was nervous about performance was camping in some exposed fields in the UK where the winds were regularly quite high. No issues when using all of the guy lines, although if extreme weather were to roll in without cover it may be a different story.  Love the fly material, waterproof, light, and dries out fast.
reviews.author: Elliot B

reviews.title: Perfect for me & my dog!
reviews.text: This tent has been great for me!  I've used it in snow camping (even though it is not 4 season) and the size is perfect for me and my dog for backpacking trips. The freestanding set up is nice and easy.

It has always kept me warm and dry through wind, rain, snow, and the dark of night.  One small hole created by a wind blown branch was easily repaired, and the tent continues to impress.   I will always buy, recomment Big Agnes products!

I like it so much, I got the three person version for car camping, especially because the two-person is a bit tight for two adults. Very durable, stood up to30-40 mph winds on the beach. But sand was able to make it under the fly eventually and we slept in sand which was not good. There is ventilation features but if the sun hits the tent in the morning, unobstructed, it's like an oven in there. The newer versions look a little better in this respect. After 10 years, the seam tape is coming off I re-glued them but it didn't work perfectly. I also popped a hole in the fly stretching it over the pole for the awning over the vestibule. I will patch it and keep trucking. 10 years and hundreds of nights out in the elements, I'd say I got my money's worth.

reviews.title: Lightweight, easy to setup...still getting used to it.

I do love this tent - it's a great size, weight is fine for backpacking, the fly has great coverage, but I am SO paranoid about destroying the bottom. It feels thin, though I know that is the idea given the tent's purpose. If you are on any kind of hill, the floor is also quite slippery, letting your mat slide and pull the floor at the staked corners. I was adjusting the tent all night for fear I'd rip it. On a flatter grassy ground, it was fine without slipping. Maybe it's the tent, maybe it's me, but hopefully I get over the fear and it's as sturdy as it claims!

reviews.title: Great quiver of one tent
reviews.text:
I bought this because I needed a lightweight tent for alone climbing and mountaineering objectives in the PNW. I considered a single wall, 4-season tent, but realized that the condensation issues inherent in single wall tents would far outweigh the potential pros (light, better protection form the elements, easier setup). A solid 3-season tent is preferable for 95% of what I plan to use it for, and after much research, I opted for the Big Agnes Copper Spur UL2. I would estimate about 50% of the people I climb with also use some Copper Spur variant.

Pros: lightweight (3lb 5oz including footprint, 8 stakes, guylines, and stuff sack), sturdy, comfortable in a variety of conditions. it has a lot of little details that I've come to appreciate, like little loops to quickly stuff the door in to hold it open. The zippers rarely catch. They've only caught in the rain fly, but the material is so silken that it just sort of slips out of the zipper rather than getting stuck. Ample interior area and vestibule. 

Cons: it's a double wall tent, so setup is never going to be as simple as a single wall tent. you set it up like any other double wall tent. That's no big deal until you find yourself pitching it in wet or windy weather. Fortunately, I haven't had to do that yet, but I imagine that keeping things from getting wet or blowing away will be a struggle unless you have a buddy or two to help.
the other con, and this is a minor gripe, is the guylines. They've got near little adjustable clips, and the cord itself is great, but the way it comes from the factory is just tied to the loops on the fly exterior. The guy lines are long, maybe 4-6 feet, and the little adjustors allow you to adjust from full length to half of full length. Going smaller than that, you need to get creative. I ended up getting the guylines to the tent with an adjustable taut line hitch, so if I need to use less than half of the line, I can adjust the hitch to make a smaller loop to the necessary size.
reviews.author: Jacob W

reviews.title: Awful. Stay away.
reviews.text: Hole in the bottom of the tent, only after using this tent twice, with a footprint and being super careful about the placement. Reached out to Big Agnes, they refused to replace the tent, blamed it on the tent being "ultralight" which is a poor excuse. No piece of gear should fail after 2 uses. I've used their tents before, and have had no issues with previous ultralight tents despite 30+ uses. This clearly has a defect or overall poor quality. Do not spend your money on this tent or on any of their products.

reviews.title: Great 2 person tent
reviews.text: Big Agnes tents perform exceptionally well. Rain, high winds, setting up on rough terrain..the Copper Spur 2 held up very nicely on an alpine climbing trip for 3 days. Barely notice the extra few lbs in my pack..Fits two people just fine. (5’10 190lbs + 5’4 120lbs) Was able to keep all my gear covered under the fly + my wife’s. We sleep on a double exped pad and it fits very snug inside. Material is light/durable. Pretty close to an “ultralight” set up without the dyneema price point. Only thing I don’t like is the packing bag for the tent it’s long and odd- I’d rather bundle it all up into a stuff sack personally. Very impressed. Highly recommend.

reviews.text: Super nice tent, the stuff sack is kind of like a burrito instead of a sack. It fits everything well especially if you strap the poles on the outside which is what I do. I kind of wish it was a stuff style because when everything is dirty or wet it gets tricky to get everything in without getting mud on the tent mesh. The tent stakes also are a little hard to secure to the tent at times but similar to many modern tents. It is spacious for one person but with a 25” sleeping pad there is not quite enough space for another person. With something smaller it will be cozy but doable. The tents zippers are really nice and the poles are easy to use. I do find that the rainfly zippers get stuck occasionally but it’s not too bad.

reviews.title: Best Outdoors Pants
reviews.text:
I picked these pants up towards the end of Summer/Fall 2023 and they have been a staple in my outdoor activities ever since. They are without a doubt my go-to pair of pants for a variety of activities, not just for biking.

Some features that I really appreciate:
1. They are lightweight, perfect for those warmer days (65° and above). I haven't tested them in the heat of summer yet, but they held up great on a hot 90° day while backpacking in the Grand Canyon. I have put long underwear on while wearing these, but I don’t love doing high cardio activities in long underwear, so I switch to my Dharco MTB pants for colder weather. 
2. The side vents are a game changer for me. While I wish they were a bit bigger, they still provide a nice breeze while riding or hiking if the wind is blowing. (Hey Backcountry, maybe consider making bigger side vents in the future?) I love using the vent slits to store my phone when biking with chamois that have a side pocket (Dharco makes the best chamois that have this feature).
3. These pants are incredibly comfortable. I can easily wear knee pads underneath, squat, pedal, hike, and even lounge around. They have been my go-to on hot days for just hanging out. Especially as someone who is obsessed with sun protection. 
4. They offer great rain resistance and dry super fast when soaked. I put them to the test on a five-day backpacking trip on the Lost Coast during two days of straight rain. They got soaked where my rain skirt didn't cover, but dried out quickly.
5. Sun protection. I am pretty principled about my sun protection and I won’t ride in shorts or short sleeves. So these have been the best option for my sun protection obsession. 
6. They have not stretched out. I wore these on a backpacking trip for 6 days straight. With soaking rain. Not once did they stretch out. To this day they still fit great. 

A few downsides to note:
1. I struggle to access my knee pads while wearing these pants, but I have the same issue with all my MTB pants.
2. The belt strap doesn't stay in place very well. So it won’t help if they are large around the waist. 
3. The front pockets aren't very practical while riding, as they are in an awkward position for storage. 

I am 5’6” and fluctuate between 115 and 120 pounds and I am quite slim. My pants size is between a 24-25 or 0-4 and the small fits wonderful, with and without chamois. (In Lululemon I wear a size 2 or 4 in their pants)
reviews.author: Laura B
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: My favorite MTB pant hands down.
reviews.text:
I get compliments any time I wear these pants on the trails! I live in texas and we have some pretty rugged terrain and brush usually around the trails so having a super breathable and light weight pant to help keep the sun off my legs and also provide protection against some branches and prickly plants is awesome! I bought a size small, I'm 5'4" and fluxuate from 128 - 132lbs since having my little boy last year. 

I ABSOLUTELY love the fit, theres enough room in the waist so they dont cut you in half when leaning over I wear a padded short with these and you can hardly tell but fit seamlessly together. The only gripe i have with these pants is where the vent zips are on the outter thigh there is a part of the zipper fabric that itches me if I dont wear a shammie/ padded shorts. Its quiet irritating but I'm super sensitive to itchy fabrics so it may just be me or I might of gotten a faulty pair. Regardless, I wear these 9/10 any time I'm getting on my MTB. I love them so much and will be buying more colors in these and will also try the 5" shorts this summer as well because im not a long short gal. Hope to see you out on the trails!
reviews.author: kmulder
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: Awesome design & fit!
reviews.text:
I first purchased the Slickrock bike short and was so in love, I just had to try the pants… skeptically though, a pant for mountain biking???
After one sunny, but still chilly spring ride, I am in love with the pants as much as I am with the shorts!
Perfectly designed with the features you’d want from a pant and a great fit! I am 5’10” / 190 lbs, up 15# heavier/curvier than I normally am, (but still taller than wider by a long shot) and typically a size 14, the XL fits very well. The waist doesn’t cut in at all (yay, who likes to feel like they are being squeezed in 2 by their waistband or have unattractive rolls above your pants???), they fall at my ankle and were large enough in the leg that I never felt a frustrating pull or stretch in the material, but they aren’t loose enough where I was worried about the chain, I know… they sound like magic pants and they may be!
If you want a pant that can work for mountain biking, jogging, hiking, grocery shopping, whatever… on a day with a brisk wind where you want protection, but not insulation, and a quick drying pant, this is the pant for you.

reviews.title: Slickrock pants!

reviews.title: Just right
reviews.text:
I have tried on so many bike pants since my favorite pair wore out and now cost over 200$, I’ve tried Patagonia, shredly, OR, and fox. I have big calves and so many end up fitting like leggings. The slick rock has the right fit and are super lightweight. 

I sized up from my usual medium, usually I’m 8/10, but backcountry’s sizing tends to run small. I’m glad I went with the large because it leaves room for chamois. I also love the zipper vents on the sides.

My one and only gripe is the ankle zipper could go up a little higher to make knee pads easier to put on.

The rise is perfect, they're soft, the silhouette is HOT, the army green is HOT. I'm in love. Was not expecting the Backcountry brand to take the cake over all the dedicated MTB pant brands.

reviews.text: These are honestly the best mountain biking pants I’ve ever owned—they’re super stretchy, and the tailored athletic fit just feels awesome whether I’m riding, hiking, or even trail running. The waist is really secure so I never have to tug at them mid-ride. I also love that the fabric moves with me but still gives plenty of protection and comfort on the trail (even when you crash). They’ve become my go-to for just about any adventure outdoors. They are legend.

reviews.title: Great Pants; Pain in the B Service
reviews.text: I bought two pairs of these pants to try on at home and kept one. The overall quality is great. I used these to hike the Tour du Mont Blanc earlier this summer and they were comfortable to wear at night and on cooler, wetter days. They dry fast and shed dirt. The side vents are a great addition to reduce heat. Customer service for the return was a pain. I tried on both pants at home, kept them on my table, and returned the one with all the original tags and packaging within the return window. They claim it came back in "used" condition. Backcountry's bar for "used" is extremely low. They also will not provide photos to validate what they based this on so you may be out more money than you expected. I won't purchase from Backcountry again, knowing this. It's not worth the risk.

reviews.title: Great Addition to my Kit
reviews.text:
The Slickrock is an awesome multisport pant to round out any outdoor sports closet. I love the material, they are light, stretchy, and wind and water resistant. I've only used them for winter sports so far and they have served really well. I've enjoyed them for running, hiking, Nordic skiing, and Fat Biking.  

They've played nicely from a 30F run with just spandex shorts underneath, to a -13F day of Fat Biking with fleece lined leggings and a chamois. 

The waist and overall shape is really flattering, I look good and feel good in these! The generously high waist in the back is ideal for riding, without feeling awkward for foot sports. 

Reasons I didn't give 5/5: 
> The only pockets are right at my hip crease, great for my keys when I am loading the car but useless when I need to start pedaling. 
> They could have a more generous ankle zipper and cut in the knee, I was able to put kneepads on without taking my pants off but it was a struggle. 
> The thigh zippers seem unnecessary? I could see them being helpful if I was wearing cargo bibs and needed to access something in my thigh pocket but I'd rather just have properly placed pockets on my pants. 
> The material is a little 'flimsy'... not sure how they will hold up to a proper MTB crash. At half the price of most MTB pants I can give a little grace on that though.

reviews.text:

They can be combined with a baselayer or tight and feel pretty comfortable too.
They're not going to be the best option if you're too exposed or in the wind.  Save these for when you're in the trees or on hotter days. 

Sizing:  waists on the slickrock garments are bigger than the traditional running short, but you can size up and lock it down with the nylon belt.  Alternatively, the website size chart is accurate if you want to be precise.

reviews.title: Good shoe for specific use cases.
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Here's my over all feeling on the BD Momentum shoes: 
Pros:
Comfortable fit after short break-in period
Great performance on slabs and small footholds
Secure, ergonomic velcro closure
Durable rubber
Affordable and beginner-friendly

Cons:
Lacks stickiness out of the box, a bit slippery to start
Not ideal for overhangs
Sizing runs large so size down 1 whole size
reviews.author: Pablo S

reviews.title: Comfy and Great for Beginners, but Sizing Was Tricky
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Black Diamond Momentum climbing shoes are super comfortable and make for a great introduction to climbing footwear. The breathability and soft upper materials were really nice, especially for longer sessions at the gym. The rubber seems fairly sticky and thick enough to last with my somewhat sloppy footwork. (I used to climb a lot but took a hiatus and my skills are definitely not what they were)

However, the sizing threw me off—I had to size down 1.5 sizes from my street shoes, whereas I usually only go down one size. (I wear a 10 iand usually a 9 in climbing shoes but had to trade for 8.5s) Interestingly, I saw other reviews suggesting they run small, but in my case they felt too big, especially in the heel, which had a bit too much volume for a secure fit. I might try the women’s version next time for a better fit. That said, for a beginner-friendly shoe with great comfort and ease of use, they’re a solid choice.
reviews.author: Joseph D

reviews.title: Great neutral shoe for all day comfort or beginners.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Shoe has all day comfort combined with a great Velcro strap. Plenty of rubber to last you a while as well as a spacious toe box for people with wider feet. Tends to run a little large. Anywhere from half to a full size.
reviews.author: Jesus C

reviews.title: BD Momentum Velcro honest review
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Initial impression was a nice comfortable fit, although they did seem to fit a bit big compared to other brands (i wear a 41.5 in La Sportiva and it’s a tight fit). The construction of the velcro system makes it easy to slip on and off as well as really crank down on the mid foot for a secure feeling on the wall. Toe rubber has held up nicely and performs pretty good on slab and more technical overhanging problems. Grip has not been an issue so far, pretty much performs as expected for a flat comfortable shoe. Very comfortable even after long days outside and in the gym!! Great shoe option for someone looking for a well-rounded and good performing shoe on all terrain.
reviews.author: Alexsander K

reviews.title: Beginners with wider feet rejoice!
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I love the fitment of the shoe. I have wider feet and having tried other brands of shoes I've felt how narrow and tight the sides of my feet are. I definitely recommend  getting sized up for the EU sizing as it is a better guide for fitment than US sizing. I went with a size EU 42/US 9 for my shoe and I typically wear a US 9.5 because of my wider feet. As for the sole of the shoe, it was stiff in the toes where it needs to be and flexable in the arch when doing some moves. As a beginner myself, having tried rental shoes for some time and feeling how much longer I can wear these shoes as compared to other brands as made climbing a much more enjoyable activity to do. I do want to let people reading my review know that I received a pair for free to test and write a review on. I've tried other shoes from different brands and I want to say that this shoe is the most comfortable for me and others with wider feet
reviews.author: Brandon Q

reviews.title: Momentum Climbing Shoe
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Black Diamond’s momentum climbing shoe has become my new go-to for indoor climbing. I love the breathable knit upper, the velcro that makes putting them on and off easy. They’re replacing a set of laced shoes that I wore for a year. Would recommend these to a climber who is just getting into the sport for comfort throughout the entire session. 

I typically wear a US Size 9/9.5 or EU Size 42, and would recommend sizing down one size in this shoe. 

Black Diamond gave me this free product to try.
reviews.author: Jeremy F

reviews.title: Really solid and durable shoe
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] So I tested these shoes both indoors and outdoors as apart of a product testing. These shoes are intermediate first of all, the price is very nice for intermediate there aren’t many shoes this nice for the price. The rubber edge of the shoe held up better than any shoe I’ve owned on sharp granite and it did fantastic. I absolutely love the fit and feel of these shoes along with a really snug heel box. I am a 11 street shoe and 42 fit great but I do like my shoes pretty snug and without socks. I also found that with the reinforced toe making toe hooks was very comfortable. I will say one thing and that is the rubber is not impressively “sticky”. I found that indoors while trying to smear and do more friction footwork they would sometimes slip. I don’t do a lot of footwork like that and I don’t think most do but if you do a lot then you may want to consider that. Other than that small thing I encountered I really liked the shoes and will continue wearing them. If you are a beginner wanting an upgrade at a really nice cost or you are an intermediate/advanced climber who wants a shoe that won’t lose its edge quick this is a really solid, surprisingly comfortable option. 


Black Diamond gave me this free product to try.

I am eager to see how the rubber holds up to regular use.

reviews.title: Great Neutral Climbing Shoe
reviews.text: Sizing on climbing shoes can be difficult but here’s what I found. If you want a performance fit then stick with you original shoe size, for a somewhat comfort fit then go a half size up. Now if you were socks I’d go a full size or a full size and a half up depending on thickness of the socks you wear. Overall this shoe is a great neutral climbing shoe with start that sinch down but are not constricting to the point you lose circulation. The shoe surprisingly ventilates well and and the split tongue makes it easier to slip on and off. Great shoe for climbers who are new to the sport or hobby of climbing. It does have a little dead space in the heel but the most important rule is that all toes should be touching the front of the shoe.

reviews.text: When it comes to the fit of the shoes, treat yourself like Cinderella and find a pair that fits well. I'm not sure if they need a break-in period, but it didn't provide me the stretch and comfort I needed while I was bouldering in the gym. On the upside, the NEO Friction performed well and was sticky on slab routes. Although the Momentum and I were incompatible, I would still recommend this product to a friend to test and see if the shoes fit comfortably for them.
reviews.author: iheartfilms

reviews.title: Amazing Gym Shoe at the Price Point
reviews.text: Black Diamond has put out a shoe at the level of excellence you expect from the company.  I have climbed hard in these shoes about 10 times in three different gyms, and they have been a joy to wear.  The first thing I noticed was the light weight.  These feel very comfortable and minimal, especially considering how well they perform.  My favorite aspect is the rubber and edging, which I did not expect from an entry level shoe made for comfort.  They edge onto tiny holds like glue, smear on walls with a solid feel, and have not shown any wear after about 20 hours of hard climbing.  As advertised, the shoes have not started smelling bad thus far.  The mesh vents well and does in fact hold up to abuse.  They seem true to size, but definitely try them on before buying.  The only thing these shoes did not do well was heel hooking.  The heels are just not made for aggressive bouldering problems or long overhanging walls.  That being said, in the slab and vertical world, these are both comfy slippers and beasts.  I look forward to seeing how they perform at Seneca soon!  Got my first 12a in these, thanks BD!

Bought size 5 for my 11 year old. At first there was a worry that they were too tight, but then it all seemed to work out once an indoor climbing session happened. After that, my son kept giving positive feedback about these.

To be fair this is our first purchase of shoes, as up until now we were using the bouldering gym's loaners.

reviews.title: Perfect sun hoody!
reviews.text: I own it in multiple colors and the fit is perfect! I ran an Ultra in Moab this past March and it kept me cool/dry and warm/comfortable when needed. I love the longer length, lightweight breathable fabric, elastic around the hood to keep it from blowing off your head. Excellent quality!! I can’t wait to add more colors to my collection.
reviews.author: Angie V.

reviews.title: woo!
reviews.text: so great, i wear it all the time!! lightweight and sturdy!
reviews.author: Alaina K.

reviews.title: My Favorite Wear
reviews.text: This has definitely become my new problem shirt in that I wear it every day! It’s breathable and easy to layer over and under things. Size fits accurately. I love the hidden pocket too!
reviews.author: Kat H.

reviews.title: FAVORITE sun hoody
reviews.text: I love these. They fit great and are lightweight. I wear them on hot summer days and never feel like im sweating. I have multiple colors and cannot wait to collect more
reviews.author: Kc H.

reviews.title: Excellent product for hiking
reviews.text: I purchased this for my wife and we went to Banff national park hiking Johnston Canyon, Moraine Lake, and Lake Louise. Best quality and airy but has good sun protection. She loved the air ventilation but protecting winds too.
reviews.author: Dipanjan N.

reviews.title: Perfect hoody on those sunny days
reviews.text: I just had a full day climb in the sun and wore this hoody. It kept me protected by the sun without feeling too warm. I used the hood over my helmet to keep the hot sun away and actually felt cooler. Light and comfortable it’s perfect layer for hot summer days or windy weather. I am loving it!
reviews.author: Erica F.

reviews.title: Nice Hoody
reviews.text: I love the bright red/orange color. The fit is decent, it feels heavier than most sun hoodies and I wear it in cooler weather. The zippered pocket is annoying and conflicts/rubs with my pack waistbelt. I'm not sure what I could put in the tiny pocket, keys or a phone would sag and rattle too much, it would be cleaner without it.
reviews.author: Michele N.

reviews.title: Cute sun hoody!
reviews.text: Fits a little large but I still love it. The pocket is nice and convenient. My only complaint is no thumb holes or ponytail hole.
reviews.author: Kendra A.

reviews.title: Sun protection for high altitude adventures
reviews.text: One of the best sun protection layers you can own; lightweight, cooling, protective, and genuinely comfortable.
reviews.author: Megan M.

reviews.title: Love!
reviews.text: So breathable, comfortable amd effective. Deep hood, long enough arms and body. Have been looking for a great sun hoody for so long and am thrilled I went with this one after a lot of research. We live in Arizona and this has held up in heat and sun exposure. I am 5’9” and often bought men’s sun hoodies for the longer arms but this one is perfect!
reviews.author: Alissa

reviews.title: Definitely recommend
reviews.text: I haven’t bought a sunshirt before, but wow, this one is great. Fabric is really nice and it fits perfect. The rose/fig color is way cuter in person too.
reviews.author: taylor l
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Love these hoodies
reviews.text: These sun hoodies are PERFECT for exposed desert adventures. Perfect combination of lightweight and airy, yet a protective layer for just about any scenario.
reviews.author: Kristin S.

reviews.title: It has a POCKET!
reviews.text: Since my husband love's the men's version I decided to start getting the women's. It's virtually the same, just cut for a woman and has a pocket-total score! These wear/wash/pack well and last long as well.
reviews.author: Nicole S.

reviews.title: Pectoral fin pockets are a nope
reviews.text:
What the He** pockets?

After spraying on about how much I love my alpenglow hoodies to my wife, I bought two of these for my her for an upcoming adventure where all day sun pro will be paramount. Well, she hates them simply for the bulky pockets that protrude off the side like some sort of pectoral fin. I said "what pockets" only to find the women's has the aforementioned pectoral pockets for some unknown reason. Now we are scrambling for an alternative. Do women need pockets? Why mess with perfect?
reviews.author: steve

reviews.title: Perfect hiking sun hoody. I
reviews.text: Perfect hiking sun hoody. I am tall, 5'10", and this hoody is long enough to cover my entire torso and down to my wrists.
reviews.author: Amalia T.

reviews.title: Lightweight and Comfortable
reviews.text: This hoody is perfect for active days outside. It’s lightweight yet provides great sun protection, breathable enough for warm weather, and layers easily when it cools down. The fit is flattering and comfortable, and the fabric feels high quality. Definitely a new favorite for hiking and everyday wear!
reviews.author: Ryan H.

reviews.text: The best!
reviews.author: Drew F

reviews.title: Perfect for the Longs Peak Trail
reviews.text: I wore this hoody recently on the Longs Peak trail, and it was exactly what I needed. Lightweight and breathable on the climb, but still gave enough coverage and sun protection at higher elevation. The fit is comfortable, layers easily, and the fabric held up great through a long, demanding day. Highly recommend it for serious hikes and mountain adventures.
reviews.author: Ryan H.

reviews.title: Amazing quality, great odor repellence
reviews.text:
I wore this hoody, went climbing for hours in early August, went out with friends afterwards for drinks and it still has no smell on it. 
Dries super fast, and is great for all things outdoor
reviews.author: Alborz Z.

reviews.title: Top-tier Sun Hoody
reviews.text:
I love this Alpenglow hoody with all my heart and own 4 of them now in varying colors!

The fit is perfect for tall, athletic builds with long enough arms and not baggy chest fit. The hood perfectly accommodates a climbing helmet and does not choke you or restrict movement when up!

The material is straight-up magical - it protects you but is woven in such a way that it really does keep you very cool in hot environments. I've used it in the hot and dry Rockies, hot and humid Florida, hot and muggy Virginia, and hot Texas and it performs incredibly well. I never feel muggy or sweaty in it as it's always venting and providing the perfect layer. I've also used this in colder weather and it works great there too - it's like the adobe of clothing, keeps you cool in the summer and warm in the winter.

I've used it rock climbing, mountaineering, skiing, backpacking, and general outdoor use! You will not find me outside without it!
reviews.author: Cody C.

reviews.title: Awesome Everyday Sun Hoody
reviews.text: I have used this hoody as my daily driver for the past year, taken it around the world to climb and ski in, and it still looks great! The material is lightweight, breathable, and very stretchy making it great for rock climbing. My main use case for the hoody is for sun protect, since I hate wearing sunscreen, and this product works great for that. The biggest drawback is that I wear it so often, I look the same in all my pictures!
reviews.author: Paul R

reviews.title: Best Sun Hoodie out there
reviews.text: This is the third one I've owned, just keep coming back for more! I wear them for rock climbing primarily, pretty durable considering the fabric is relatively thin and what I put them through, climbing chimneys, hiking through tight trees, etc. The hood fits perfectly over a helmet. Fits true to size, I'm 5'10" 165 lbs, size Medium
reviews.author: Chris W.

reviews.title: Sweetness
reviews.text: Where have you been my whole life, or more like, where have I been? Hello black diamond really love your hoodie. Thanks for your existence. I’ll be back.
reviews.author: LaCoy P.

reviews.title: My favorite sun hoodie
reviews.text:
I've used the Alpenglow Pro for a few seasons now, and I'm a big fan. It's perfect for climbing, with a nice stretchy hood that fits perfectly over a helmet. The material isn't superlight, but it's reasonably light, and the extra features really make this hoody shine.

It's not as light and airy as something like the OR Echo, but that's a benefit as well - you can get a bit of insulation from this sun shirt, while it also dumps heat using mesh panels at the armpits. The front zip allows for some ventilation, making it a decent shirt for running if it isn't too hot out.

The only downside to the Alpenglow Pro is that the material doesn't perform very well in humid environments. But here in Colorado, it's just about as perfect as a sun hoodie can get. That's why I also bought one for my girlfriend!
reviews.author: Taylor S

reviews.title: Solid All Around Shirt
reviews.text: Light weight to wear for sun protection, but also has kept me warm if the sun goes away and a chilly wind picks up on the multi. Comfy material and I like the colors.
reviews.author: Eric J.

reviews.title: Alpenglow Pro Shines like the Alpenglow on your Summit Approach
reviews.text: I have purchased two of these for the past year of guiding, and have been thoroughly impressed. I developed a tear that worried me due to the stretchy nature of the fabric, and I did not think that it would hold a patch well. However, after a year of abuse, the small tear has not grown any larger! The only con that another expert has mentioned is that this fabric is quite hot and heavy when soaked in a humid/rainy environment.
reviews.author: Finn B

reviews.title: Great long sleeve for any activity
reviews.text: Love my Black Diamond hoodies. I wear for hiking and backcountry skiing and typically do not wear any layering underneath and I live in the Fraser Valley of Colorado.
reviews.author: Edmund R.

reviews.title: The perfect shirt
reviews.text: This is the greatest shirt/hoodie I’ve ever owned. Whether it’s the East Couloir on Mt. Whitney, or a 109° canyon hike in Death Valley this is the shirt I’m wearing. If I could only own one shirt, this would be it. The fit is great, the fabric is soft but durable and it never really gets stinky.
reviews.author: Dustin G

reviews.title: Super breathable, trim fit
reviews.text:
Great base layer for snowshoeing/ winter running… and I expect it to be great as a sole layer for fall and spring runs. Very well made, great color. 

5’10” 185lbs size M fits trim.
reviews.author: Robert R.

reviews.title: Awesome Sun hoody
reviews.text: Just bought one for my trip to Palm Springs to hike the Cactus to Clouds trail (hardest hike I’ve ever done btw highly recommend) I’ve never actually worn a sun hoody before this but all my friends said it’s the best way to go in the desert and wow we’re they right. It kept the sun off and evaporated my sweat insanely quickly as well as crazy soft and comfortable. The only downside is I got tons of mosquito bites through it but that’s more on me for assuming the desert didn’t have mosquitoes and not doing enough research to bring repellents.  This will definitely become a staple in my hiking attire as I like how quickly it wicks the sweat and I sunburn pretty easily.
reviews.author: Kenny M

reviews.title: My favorite sun shirt, but could it be better?
reviews.text: Love these shirts. Have 3 now and wear them constantly, hiking, climbing, paddling, working, whatever. The material is really durable compared to other sun shirts I’ve owned, but with that it feels hotter. Would be amazing to have some perforated areas or something to allow more air flow. My only other gripe is one of the shirts I ordered was a lot shorter than the others and almost unwearable for me. Overall a key part of my gear. Nice work BD
reviews.author: Jason B.

reviews.title: “Just do it” - Shia LaBeouf
reviews.text:
If you’re here you made the right call, skip the Long Sleeve Crew and skip the Pro Hoodie and buy this instead (unless you have to have thumb holes). 

I couldn’t be happier with this sun shirt/hoodie. I work outside in the sun and humidity all day with very fair skin, and my two Alpenglow Hoodies are part of my everyday wardrobe. They are breathable, lightweight, and most importantly to me boast an SPF 50 rating to keep me safe in the sun. 

I have worn my Alpenglow shirt and hoodies on multiple hikes and while tubing in mountain creeks and they have held up perfectly despite branches, rocks, and the various other hazards that would rip into most other shirts/hoodies. 

I will be stocking up on more of these in the near future. It’s worth every penny, go ahead and add it to your cart.
reviews.author: Maverick H.

reviews.title: The perfect sun hoody
reviews.text: Just fantastic- simple and rugged. It does not have thumb holes though- not a concern for me, but i know it’s a dealbreaker for some. The pewter color is nice and cool and the UV resistance makes for a nice alternative to sunscreen. Fits a little slim, but not bad. This is my go to now- the material is rugged enough for mountaineering yet cool enough for hot days on the trail.
reviews.author: Johnny D

reviews.title: Best sun shirt I’ve worn
reviews.text: Best Sun hoodie on the market. I’m a multi pitch climbing guide at Seneca Rocks, and I wear one of these shirts pretty much every day I’m on the rock. The chest zip and armpit vents are perfect for venting heat on warm days, and it’s a great base layer to wear in colder temps, plus the material is comfortable and durable. It also comes in some pretty cool colors. %100 worth the price.
reviews.author: Arthur B

reviews.title: Best Sun Hoody Available
reviews.text:
The Black Diamond Alpenglow Hoody is an essential part of every backpacking, hiking, and camping trip I take. It's extremely lightweight and breathable which helps to keep me cool, even on hot summer days. With the hood up and the UPF 50+ fabric, I've never had a sun burn while wearing this hoody. After two years of use, my original two hoodies are still going strong and I will continue to recommend them to friends and family. Heck, I even proposed to my now wife wearing one of these while camping outside Yellowstone. If you're looking for a sun hoodie, this is the one to go for.
For sizing, I'm 6'2" 180lbs and wear a size large which gives a slightly loose but well fit shirt.
My only wish is that the hoody had thumb holes but the sleeves are long enough to cover some of the backs of my hands.
reviews.author: Alex W

reviews.title: Absolutely love this hoody
reviews.text: I own three of these now. They are my go-to shirts for day hiking, backpacking trips, and mountain climbing. They keep me cool even when the sun is beating down, and they look great to boot. I'm 5'9" and about 180 lbs, and the size medium fits me perfectly. Super stretchy and super comfortable. Black Diamond, you guys nailed it with this one.
reviews.author: Brian F

reviews.text: Super comfortable and durable, vents well.  Doesn’t smell after days of backpacking (or I just smelt bad enough I didn’t notice)
reviews.author: Jordan R

reviews.title: Excellent for an alpine clime.
reviews.text: Comfortable all day with sun hoody protection
reviews.author: Garth J.

reviews.title: Great addition to my Alpenglow Hoodie horde
reviews.text: The Alpenglow Pro is an improvement over the original Alpenglow. It is lighter weight and wicks better. The neck zipper allows easy ventilation. I'm a fan of Napoleon pockets en general. It's a nice addition. The top stays cool in the heat and warm as a base layer. Lastly: YELLOW!
reviews.author: CHARLES B

reviews.title: Sun Shirts Rule!
reviews.text: I have used this from snow climbs to climbing to hiking and for travel. The fit is great! I am 6’ 2” and weigh 195 lbs. It is loose where you want it but still athletic fitting. Love the hood.
reviews.author: Walt P

reviews.title: Do-it all hoody.
reviews.text: I have used this hoodie as a base layer for skiing in and out of bounds. Then on trips to southern Utah Mtn biking. Now as a protective layer against the sun. Seriously thank you for this all season crusher. I couldn’t ask for more. My go to hoodie for any season!
reviews.author: Kevin B.

reviews.title: Outdoor everything sun shirt!
reviews.text:
I picked one of these up in the raging sea color about a year ago in size L and it quickly became my favorite sun shirt. I use it paddle boarding, climbing, hiking and backpacking, it's simply the best. Breathes well, is flowy and comfortable, the hood has good depth to snug over my head, hat or helmet. I swear a fair bit so after a long day it'll smell a bit, but that's normal. Compared to a few other name brand sun hoody's I've tried this is my favorite. So far despite some velcro attacks and rock scraping from climbing it's holding up very well!

I'm 6'2" and 195lbs, athletic build (bigger shoulders 34" waist) the large fits snuggly so I went with the XL which is loose on me with a comfortable amount of room for movement with full sleeve coverage, the hem staying tucked in a harness, and the hood over a helmet without any significant tugging at the neck. XL hood also works well with a hat or by itself.

Weird thing is the size L I got a year ago fits exactly like a new XL I just got in Tundra green...no clue why, but maybe they changed the sizing or I got a mislabeled L shirt. Either way, I'm happy with the XL as I found in current sizing.
reviews.author: Alexander S.

reviews.title: Best Shirt in the World
reviews.text: Perfect shirt for early morning ascents, days at the beach, or wearing in town. I've got every color and I wear them all the time. The absolute best.
reviews.author: Kevin M.

reviews.title: Great buy, excellent quality and performance
reviews.text: I bought this about a month ago, the idea was to get something lite with long sleeves and a hood for sun protection, that would keep me cool in a hot day and dry fast. This fits all the above, I have used it for 4 climbs (top rope) and works great, material is light on the skin and performs well. I am 5'11" at 175 lb and got a size L that fits loose, perfect fit for what I need. Because worked so good for climbing I decided to give it a try for running as well (considering all the keeping cool and go easy on the skin attributes), so I run a few times in it, both trail run (6-8 miles) and on the road, in warm weather (75-85F). It worked as a charm, so much so that I will uses it for both climbing and running and get another color, when will become available on BD site.
reviews.author: tcc2020

reviews.title: Light, well fitted and clutch for exposed days
reviews.text: I burn looking outside at the sun so I've been hunting for a long sleeve hoody that's loose enough to be able to handle on a hot day hiking up a snow field or into the back country. Landed on the Alpenglow and it's become one of my go-to baselayers for long days out. It fits well, dig the color but most of all, it's just nice and light. Even without the hood up, I like the protection for the back of my neck and while it's a little snug to roll the sleeves up, I've been able to tolerate it on a hot day out before hitting camp.
reviews.author: Traveler Ted

reviews.title: Awesome!
reviews.text: Great sun protecting piece and also feels great as a base layer, spent days in one of these and am super glad I had it out on glaciers and for long hikes
reviews.author: Fastestknowntyler

reviews.title: Nice, but different colors than advertised
reviews.text: Very comfortable. However, the blue is not as baby blue as the picture would have you believe. Also, the white/tan one is more grey. Still kept them as they are high quality, but wish they were the same color as advertised.
reviews.author: Justanormalguy

reviews.title: IR treatment is plain to see...
reviews.text:
With a FLIR. Each day is different so sometimes it's a bit hard to say, "am I cooler, am I warmer, is this shirt any different?". I was curious whether I could observe the effect of the treatment, so I pulled out my IR camera. I compared the old version of this hoody to the new version with the IR treatment. Both were fresh out of the closet & the same temperature. See for yourself- plain as day, it's the real deal.

(If you're not familiar with thermal images, they measure IR as a proxy for temperature. So in the photo the new hoody looks "hot". But in this case it's actually the sun's IR reflecting off the garment like a mirror)
reviews.author: pshyvers

reviews.title: Poor quality
reviews.text: Production shipped with fabric string already falling apart. The bag had a 20” thread dangling out from the arm stitched area. The fabric feels soft and nice, but also fragile. i bought this shirt in grey and black. They are comfortable and look nice. but I’m afraid to do anything athletic in them.
reviews.author: Climber

reviews.title: Comfortable fit
reviews.text: I've only had a chance to wear it once while kayaking but it was comfortable and allowed full range of motion of my arms. It is probably true to size. Mine is a little large but I recently lost some weight. I ordered an XL but probably could have gone with a large. Not a fault of the product. I will definitely be wearing it more.
reviews.author: Peter W.

reviews.title: Still one of the best
reviews.text: I have 1 of the original ones from black diamonds first season with this product. I still use the original (one of the last remaining). they can last through a lot of expeditions so it was natural to return and restock the ones I wore out over the years
reviews.author: Maxwell K.

reviews.title: AMAZING
reviews.text: I exclusively wore this shirt for 10 days hiking the Tour Du Mont Blanc in late August. I was so glad I chose this hoodie. I normally find myself between a medium and large in most apparel items and I am glad I went with the large this time. It was a bit flowy and perfect for the super steep muggy climbs.
reviews.author: Anthony S.

reviews.title: Just so right
reviews.text: Super comfortable, lightweight hoody for just about anything - trail running, fishing, climbing, hanging. New fave.
reviews.author: Peter D.

reviews.title: Straight up
reviews.text: This is one of the best pieces of gear I own. I only need to purchase another because I burnt a huge hole in the shirt with a chainsaw, if it weren’t for that mishap the shirt would still be impeccable. I’ve worn this shirt more frequently and in more varied conditions than any other the last several years. It stays cooler and dries faster than any other shirt, and it does not hold odor. Black Diamond- Please do NOT change this shirt and keep a neutral earth-tone such as the Tundra color available at all times and I will keep coming back. Funny colors are great if you do recreation sports in Utah or Colorado but natural people living natural lives in natural settings like to wear natural colors. If you want to feel one with the nature, dress like the nature.
reviews.author: Baron

reviews.title: I liked the men’s colors
reviews.text: I liked the men’s colors much more and had heard bad reviews about the pocket on the women’s so I went for the men’s and overall I like it but it fits strangely across the chest. It feels like the shoulders aren’t wide enough which is strange for a men’s fit.
reviews.author: Callie D.

reviews.title: Great sun shirt. Sun protection
reviews.text: Great sun shirt. Sun protection without the need to reapply sunscreen. Comfortable fit and big hood that still protects your face and neck even with a hat on.
reviews.author: M C.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text:
This is a fantastic hoody. It is light, cool, and acts like air conditioning in the sun. I'm a ginger and keeping my skin out of the sun is critical.

I would ask the next model have looser sleeves. These are a bit tight but not in an uncomfortable way.
reviews.author: Herrick J.

reviews.title: Good midweight sun hoody
reviews.text:
Usage: I primarily use this item for outdoor climbing. I wear this when it's sunny to block the sun during cool weather. The hood was intended to fit under the helmet but I put the hood over the helmet. The underarm gusset helps with mobility and helps it from riding up from my harness. The fabric is medium weight (thicker than the Alpenglow Pro Hoody). I also use this as a mid-layer on colder days. For me, this is too thick for hot days (70 degrees F or hotter) and I recommend the Alpenglow Pro Hoody for hotter days.
Fit: I'm 5'7" around 160 lbs, athletic build and medium fits well.
reviews.author: Jay Y

reviews.title: Great Hoodie!
reviews.text: Have bought this hoodie in two different colors and am very happy with it!
reviews.author: Camilla M.

questions.text: Does this product have thumbholes?

answers.text: No — the Men's Black Diamond Alpenglow Hooded Shirt doesn't have thumbholes; the sleeves are just long enough to cover part of your hands without them.
answers.author: Alex C.

reviews.title: Lightweight and super-comfortable
reviews.text: I'm very pleased with the fit and feel of this helmet. I bought it to be used mainly on more technical scramble sections while peak bagging. It fits well over my light balaclava on colder days and the headlamp clips are nice for those alpine starts.
reviews.author: Nathan S.

reviews.title: Durable Shell
reviews.text: Up until recently was only using my BD Vapor which is an incredibly light helmet but extremely soft and dents easily. Was starting to look like an old avocado so decided to upgrade. This one take dings like a champ and has a bungee on the back to hold goggles if needed. Has become my standard winter climbing helmet.
reviews.author: brian k

reviews.title: Black Diamond Vision Helmet
reviews.text:
The Black Diamond Vision Helmet truly goes the distance. I have an oval shaped head, medium size, and wanted a very comfortable, lightweight helmet that met the current safety standards.

Sure, I climb the local crags, but I wanted a helmet that I could wear for 10+ hours on big objectives like the Tetons Cathedral Traverse or the Cirque of Towers Traverse. I’ve put this helmet through both, wore it for 15+ hours at a stretch and never thought about it. It’s that Comfortable!
reviews.author: Kevin C

reviews.title: Light with all day comfort
reviews.text: This helmet is lite and comfortable. II can fit the helmet snug so there is zero wiggle or shifting and wear this helmet all day. I do not get hot or sore spots. Also for you parents, I got the S/M and they fit my 6 yr old daughter and 7 yr old son. They wear them all day around the crag with zero complaints.
reviews.author: BRIAN C

reviews.title: Great fit
reviews.text: Very comfortable, light weight, intuitive adjustments! Love my new dome.
reviews.author: Ruth B.

reviews.title: Like a Dream
reviews.text: This helmet is very light, comfortable,  and finds a good ballance between lightweight & durability. Just enough hard protection for some falling rocks and me tossing it around, but lightweight construction to let you forget you have it on.
reviews.author: Cody T

reviews.title: Lightweight and comfy
reviews.text: I love this helmet, fits my noggin p It so comfy and light, I hardly notice I’m wearing it.
reviews.author: Helena M.

reviews.title: Comfortable
reviews.text: Adjustable sizing makes it easy to get tight. resistant to damage as well in a stuffed bag
reviews.author: Kesrith B.

reviews.title: Perfect
reviews.text: Fits great and forget it is on my head, what more is there to say.
reviews.author: Scott A.

reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text:
I like the helmet. It’s an upgrade from a
similar helmet that broke in pretty significant fall (it did it’s job!). It’s really lightweight and sits well on the head. My only initial critique is adjusting the head fitting is a little finicky (no spin dial) and there isn’t an adjustable chin strap. This was really off putting at first as my old helmet had thea, but honestly, after climbing two or three times with it I haven’t even noticed it. It surely saves a few ounces too. You’ll forget it’s on your head.
reviews.author: Greg
reviews.familiarity: I've used it once or twice and have initial impressions

reviews.title: Nice helmet but runs small
reviews.text: Bought the same size as my old BD helmet and could barely fit it on my head. Significantly smaller -- might want to try this exact model on at a store before purchasing.
reviews.author: Brittany Z.

reviews.title: lower quality
reviews.text: had this helmet before hence i reordered. was much better quality before including the plastic insert part that adjust diameter which is kinda jank now. the foam pieces in helmet where contact points were fell out of helmet so i had to guess where they went which wasn’t difficult but is kinda lot idea for safety equipment. overall i didn’t return but prob would have if they didn’t destroy returned helmets (or per folklore they do)
reviews.author: rock toucher
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Helmet Review
reviews.text: The helmet was amazing used it immediately for multiple trips in the Grand Teton National Park climbing mountains and for a Black Diamond photo shoot find it on instagram @shotbyzarth, @731. noah_h
reviews.author: Noah H.

reviews.title: Lightweight & comfortable
reviews.text: Cheaper and easier to travel with (less fragile). Fits well over hoods and visor.
reviews.author: Anna K.

reviews.title: I got this helmet because
reviews.text: I got this helmet because it was supposed to be comfortable. I have been very happy with how adjustable and comfortable it has been.

reviews.title: Vision Helmet

reviews.title: Top features, poor build quality
reviews.text:
I've been using BD headlamps for near twenty years now. They have only gotten better; lighter, brighter, more efficient. I was so psyched for this rechargeable and lightweight model. I have gone through a village's share of batteries before this moment. I have a habit of using dim mode or red mode to sustain battery life. So for me one full charge lasts weeks.
Here is the rub. With new tech gains, BD has overlooked the actual build. Less than six months of use, the hinge no longer stays fixed in upright position. The headlamp body, though not heavy, flops downward for every time I tip my chin down. This totally sucks for all downhill activity. 
Like much of my beloved gear, my BD headlamp now sports a piece of climbing tape.
Dear BD designers, please fix this analog glitch. Thanks.

reviews.title: Superb light
reviews.text: Very bright, good settings, long battery. Sometimes I wish I bought the battery one.

I been using the STORM light for years - it's been my go-to morning run light for years. But I am quite impressed with this Spot. Not quite as bright as the STORM, but it has all the feature I need - rechargeable, long battery life, AND the all-important red light for reading in the tent! Good investment.

Battery life is great and lasts a while for my needs. The headband is comfortable and stays in place even during movement. This headlamp is reliable and I’ll continue bringing it on camping or hiking trips.

reviews.title: Bad rechargeable Integration
reviews.text: Works well with AAA batteries, but does not integrate/fit the rechargeable battery well. It is very tight with so much tension on the terminals that it fails to retain the battery without carefully guiding the battery door closed; immediately falls out when opened. Lighting options and brightness are good with diverse color options.
reviews.author: Marc D.

reviews.title: Storm 450 Azul
reviews.text: Placed order of 3 Storm 450 headlamps on Aug 31, 2023 and received them. December 12, 2023 the plastic battery cover latch broke after replacing the batteries for the first time. I am very disappointed as these headlamps are supposed to be very reliable. This renders the performance of the headlamp useless. I am hoping the latch does not fail on my other 2 headlamps I purchased.
reviews.author: John B.

reviews.title: Bought Storm 450 Dual fuel headlamp…
reviews.text:
I chose the Storm 450 headlamp and over the past weeks it has definitely performed beyond my expectations. 450 lumens is more than I need daily but the fact the lumens are there allows for a secure feeling especially when they are but a tap of a finger away. I especially like the way the controls very easily allows for a gradual reduction of lumens to your desired level and the memory function is a joy to adjust and immediately goes into turbo with a touch of your finger, a beautiful feature well thought out. 
Access to the batteries is easier than I anticipated and now I am in the process of getting the rechargeable lithium battery and spare along with the the charger. 
With this kind of performance I definitely will get another Black Diamond headlamp as a backup being partial to the dual fuel option. Thank you Black Diamond for an excellent headlamp.
reviews.author: James S.

reviews.title: Broke instantly
reviews.text: The battery clasp broke the first time I tried to use it.
reviews.author: Thomas C.

reviews.title: I loved the storm 450
reviews.text:
I loved the storm 450 headlamp. Feels really smooth when you tilt it. The button to set it to max is really great and reliable. The light is very bright and the headlamp very light. 
BUT
I am giving it a 1 star review because I also bought a rechargeable battery with it and when I went to charge the battery for the first time after draining it, the hook that holds the battery compartment closed, broke when I was opening it. It used to be very easy to open and close when I first put the battery in so it was not because of me forcing it. I can not close the headlamp with tape for the time being either because it would go over the light source, so it is completely useless now. 
I also want to add that this happened when I was without electricity for 11 days, after hurricane fiona hit us, so I was disappointed, to say the least, especially for the price. 

I bought the astro 250 at the same time and the cheap option has been better than the expensive one. I'm glad that I bought that backup.

reviews.title: Amazing Headlamp

reviews.title: Fussy and Prone to Failure.
reviews.text: I had high hopes for my Storm 450, but almost immediately it started exhibiting frustratingly strange behavior. The "Power Touch" sensor on the side of the light was difficult to actuate when wanted. However, it was prone to activating on and off continuously for no reason when it was not wanted. Eventually the light itself would not operate correctly at all. When I put new batteries in, only the small white and RGB lights would operate for a few seconds then die completely. I definitely did not get my money's worth and now own a very expensive bit of toxic landfill.
reviews.author: T. S.

reviews.title: Good, but turns on in your pack
reviews.text:
This headlamp has been amazing for me, with one decent issue. 
I have opened my pack just find it turned on, or other times I've pulled it out to use just to find the battery life depleted or dead. (From turning itself on in the pack). I am a little surprised/disappointed it happens as much as it has regarding the size and nature of its power button. 
I highly recommend any potential buyers pack ample extra batteries alongside this headlamp, especially if you will rely on it. 

In all other regards, I have been very satisfied with it. It's performance and brightness is very good, it shines bright and seems to have amazing battery life. (When not being on inside a pack) The different modes are great. I personally like the battery cover latch, I have an older black diamond headlamp with the older style latch which I didn't care for. The latch is much easier and faster to change out batteries, which did simplify battery changes.

reviews.text: This light is nice . . . . but I think maybe trying too hard to be 'all things to all people. ' It's rechargeable AND lasts a long time — and who doesn't want that, right? Thing is, it accomplishes it by having a big, heavy battery. So you have this heavy thing on your forehead and don't get nearly as much brightness as you'd hope for. Personally I'd rather just use old-school batteries, which would give me much longer battery life for less size/weight. Maybe that's just me. But where this guy just fails is that it can't point at your hands! If you want to shine the light on your hands you have to put your chin on your chest and look out the top of your eye sockets. It's terrible! All they have to do is increase the angle on the pivot socket. Ugghhhh. This is why you never buy the first model year of something. Please - Black Diamond - take this thing away from me and send me next year's model!

reviews.title: bulky and heavy

Perhaps would be better for just hiking or camping, but for something with a higher impact, it does not stay put. I ended up switching to my much lighter weight biolite headlamp for the last hours of the race.

reviews.title: Shoes are fine, Sizing is off
reviews.text:
These shoes perform absolutely fine given their intended use/demographic, but it seems to me that Evolv is dealing with some sizing discrepancies that I would like to see sorted out.

The TL;DR here: I wear a Men's 11 in virtually all street shoes, but in this shoe I wear a size Men's 13 (out of the box, toes touching the ends but not quite curled over). If you are looking for shoes that fit similarly, my suggestions are as follows:
For your size in Women's street shoes, go with the same size or 1/2 a size up from what is listed as the Men's size on the Evolv Defy.
For your size in Men's street shoes, go 1.5 to 2 sizes bigger than what is listed as the Men's size on the Evolv Defy.
COMPLETELY ignore the EU and UK sizes.

Compared to the Evolv Titan, this shoe is exactly 1.5 sizes smaller (the typical men's to women's size conversion for most shoe brands) than what's listed on this website in Men's. It seems to me that what's listed on this shoe as the men's size should actually be the Women's size, and that the true Men's size is actually 1.5 sizes larger. Personally, I size up by 0.5 from my street shoe in the Evolv Titan, so I had to up 2 full sizes in the Defy.

Evolv, please fix your sizing! Try these shoes on and give us some logical numbers to go off of!

My street shoe is a 8.5M so per Evolv instruction I should order one size larger than street for a intermediate climber, which agrees with the 9.5M I have in La Sportiva. I ordered the 9.5M Evolv...  I could manage to get my foot in them but my toes were completely closed in a ball. Long story short, if you order these be aware their sizing is MUCH smaller than other bands.
reviews.author: Matthew
reviews.familiarity: I returned this product before using it

reviews.title: Great beginner shoe
reviews.text: There is nothing wrong about these shoes. They are priced right, perform well, and have been durable. They aren’t full of features, but they work perfectly for figuring out what you want In A climbing shoe. I started in these and both my kids started in these as well. The only way I wouldn’t recommend these would be if they were a veteran climber that specifically wanted something like a more aggressive sole edge.
reviews.author: Allen H

reviews.title: Good first shoe
reviews.text:
First pair of climbing shoes, bought them mainly because of the price. They get the job done; smears, toe/heel hooks, tiny foot holds, etc. all work. 

I'm a street 11 and matches with these, which is the "performance fit". They were tight, but I was able to sit/walk around the house in them for about thirty minutes before I felt the need to take them off while breaking them in. At the gym, I was fine wearing them for an hour and a half and didn't feel impeded while climbing.
reviews.author: Lupe R
reviews.familiarity: I've used it once or twice and have initial impressions

reviews.text: Great shoe. Super sticky rubber. Comfy enough.
reviews.author: Miles G

reviews.title: Keep shopping
reviews.text: These fit 2 sizes too small.  They are too wide.  They are not comfortable, and the bottom rubber bottoms don’t grip well.
reviews.author: LRRNola

reviews.title: First climbing shoe
reviews.text: I have enjoyed the shoe I am new to rock climbing and I do indoor climbing. The shoe feels well made and does great out of the box on getting a grip on foot holds. It will be uncomfortable when you first get it just let the shoe break in. I am a beginner rock climbing and I feel that this shoes are a great beginner shoe. Make sure not to wear socks (if your gym allows it) I feel that without socks the shoe is more comfortable.
reviews.author: Nicholas M

reviews.title: Favorite shoe so far!
reviews.text: Great grip! Pointed, flat bottom toe makes it easy to get into crevices. Heel is great, can easily hang from most holds. Used on indoor bouldering mostly.
