questions.text: I'm currently wearing the blue and orange rental shoes in a size 14. They are pretty stretched out and fit perfectly. Should I order a size 15? Is the defy shoes the best for a beginner with really wide feet?

answers.text:
Hey RJay,

The recommended size for Defy is your street shoe size. A half up would also suffice for more comfort. It may be uncomfortable at first right out of the box, however all climbing shoes do stretch about a half size more. Rental sizing is slightly different compared to performance models. Rentals are regularly much bigger due to over use and to compensate for socks. Generally, you want to have a snug shoe so your foot does not slide or move inside the shoe while climbing.
answers.author: Salewa

questions.text: I'm a size 12 in Saucony. What size climbing shoe do you recommend?

reviews.title: Broke when first trying it on. Twice.
reviews.text: Got these shoes as I wanted something more aggressive and blue. When they arrived I was putting them on for the first time and the right shoe's tongue ripped out as I was pulling on it to put my foot in. The shoes fit fine otherwise, and I figured it was simply a fluke. I returned the first pair and ordered another. And wouldn't ya know, the exact same thing happened the second time around. It seems odd that an aggressive shoe, which must be pulled very tight, has such weak material in the tongue. Very disappointed.
reviews.author: Joseph W
reviews.familiarity: I've used it once or twice and have initial impressions

reviews.title: Mid
reviews.text: It’s a fine shoe if on sale but it is sooooo stiff. I’ve been climbing in them for about 1.5 months and still the stiffest shoe I’ve worn. Not the most sensitive.
reviews.author: Dave
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: wide and supportive
reviews.text: Got these on sale and love them in the gym. They are super stiff/ supportive, which is not my usual preference, but I have come to like them in the gym a lot. Now that they are broken in they do flex where I can smear and stem, but are still super supportive which has allowed me to power off my feet more than before. They are still a very stiff shoe overall though, I wouldn't choose these for a slab boulder for example. I have bunions so wide towards the toes and a narrow heel (I think) and these are an amazing fit for me. No foot pain after long gym sessions. I don't like them outside as I can't feel what my foot is on well enough to trust and feel confident, but that might just be my preference to feel more outside. Might actually buy another pair at this price. In regards to the tongue issue, I have not had a problem but I also don't pull on the tongue very hard. I sized them so my toes are straight and not cramped so I'm not cramming my feet in and needing to pull them on too hard. I love that I can wear them at this comfortable size and still get a great performance out of them. I'm a size 7.5 or 8 in women's shoes, have these and two other pairs of Evolv's in 41.5 and that's a comfort fit. Have Scarpa Instinct (lace up orange and black) in a 40. I've had them for awhile now and there is still plenty of rubber left.
reviews.author: nihau
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: Never refunded my return
reviews.text: I ordered and these were wayyy too small. Submitting a return seemed easy enough but I was never refunded nor credited for the return. I reached out via email, never got a response. Talked to a gear head and they said they would issue a refund, it’s been weeks now and still no refund
reviews.author: Christian M
reviews.familiarity: I returned this product before using it

reviews.title: Do NOT buy these shoes
reviews.text: I bought these shoes after being assured by an Evolv rep that the known issues with the tongue ripping out had been fixed. They have not. The tongue ripped out of my shoe the third time wearing them. I contacted Evolv and they denied me a refund and instead offered an exchange. Personally I don’t want to go through the process of breaking in the shoes for this to happen all over again. Evolv should do the right thing and stop selling these or at the very least stop telling people that the issues has been fixed when it hasn’t. Feels kind of scummy to sell a shoe they know is defective while assuring people that it isn’t. Personally I won’t be buying Evolv again.
reviews.author: Adam H

reviews.title: Awful
reviews.text: The tongues on the shoes literally just ripped right off when I was putting them on. I've NEVER seen such awful, shoddy craftsmanship before. Absolutely terrible design.
reviews.author: PETER K
reviews.familiarity: I returned this product before using it

reviews.title: Far too wide but great for edging
reviews.text: I've been using them for almost a year on a lot of small footholds and it works like charm, very precise and great support for the foot, also the heel works amazing though a little insensitive. The one BIG problem it has is that the ball of the foot is gigantic, I can place my little finger on the side even though the toes are very crammed (but not excessively as I still wanted flexibility for smearing on credit card-like edges in less than vertical terrain); although the foot stays stable enough, is annoying that the foot moves side by side and if I wanted a tighter fit I would went with a more downturned slipper or velcro shoe for easier remove.
reviews.author: Arsenio

reviews.title: pretty dang good, just some small issues
reviews.text: This is a really stiff-toed shoe so it's really good on vertical climbs with small edges. but since it's so stiff, it makes smears (especially high feet smears) really sketchy. toe hooks felt really nice but I would have preferred a slightly softer heel to feel them better. I wear size 14 street shoes and got a size 13.5 but I really should have gone half a size smaller; I say this because when my feet start to sweat, my toes wouldn't stay right at the tip of the shoe. I blame part of that also on the felt that lines the inside of the shoe, it's comfortable but becomes really slippery when you sweat. The only other complaint would be that on my second session, the tongue of the left shoe fell off; most of the stitches on the tongue weren't actually connected (this didn't affect performance but it did look goofy). besides the tongue falling out, the looks of the whole shoe were superb. I got six months before the toe right above the sole rubbed away (mostly due to the smears that I was doing which are not what it's made for). overall, these shoes are really good for outdoor vertical walls and not for smears (still work, just not as well as a softer shoe). for future shoes, I would like an inside lining that's more focused on performance instead of comfort and a touch more rubber just above the toe of the shoe.
reviews.author: lemon_toes

reviews.title: Breaks in nice!
reviews.text: Love the fit and feel of the shoe. Heal fit is really good.  Tried them at a demo and got the size right.  They broke in and are just what I was looking for.  A comfortable but snug and high performance shoe I can wear even on long routes.  Leather upper feels good and stretched a little which is great as I went a 1/2 size down from my street shoe.  Love it on granite and sandstone, not so much on plastic and slick limestone.

Leather upper melted to my foot shape pretty quickly and it's really comfy but still high performance a shoe.

Shaman Lace LV: Same as regular Shaman Lace but narrower for low-volume (slimmer) feet.

The camo oil green is very subtle and looks good with all types of pants or sweats. I’m 6’2” 215 and XL which is my usual size fits perfect. Get one you’ll be glad you did.

reviews.title: My new go-to hardshell. It's perfect, I love it.
reviews.text: I bought this jacket in early January, ahead of a splitboarding trip in the French Alps. I'm 53, 5'10" and a bit overweight these days - circa 97Kg. My previous jacket is the top jacket by a well-known Canadian company, which has been disappointing in its waterproofing, and I'm afraid i am now a little large for! When choosing the Bergtagen (I've worn Fjallraven for many years, very interested to see them offering GoreTex) I deliberated over the size a great deal. I actually went for the XL, and I have to say I'm delighted with it. The fit is longer than my previous jacket, but not too long, and my main fear on the sleeves being gorilla-like was unfounded. They are perfect, and I really like the velcro cuffs, very substantial. The cut is roomy enough for me to comfortably wear a thick down jacket underneath on the cold days, but still looks great with just a first and mid-layer only. Waterproofing has been immaculate, and the fabric is much lighter than my previous jacket - it seems to breathe much better, I'm not soaking wet inside regardless due to perspiration - light enough I could wear it on wet walking days in summer months. It was a big investment at this price bracket, but I'm delighted with it and hope it will be my staple go-to for several years to come. Oh, and I LOVE the colour!
reviews.author: PadstowWhis

reviews.title: Great but need improvement
reviews.text: Everything is perfect, details and how it fit. I'm 176cm and 68kg, size S fit me well, have more room compare with Bergtagen Eco-shell one. I like the hammerhead zipper like the eco shell version instead of the new paracord, it's easier to grip when you wear thick gloves. I don't know if this is a design intention or a major flaw, customer will have to consider that this GTX version doesn't have a RECCO reflectors.
reviews.author: Saphire Louis

reviews.title: Excellent fall jacket, but strange sizing!
reviews.text: I have been searching for the perfect fall jacket for Ottawa, and this one fits the bill for exactly what I was looking for. The fleece is cozy, while the G-1000 is durable and breathable so you don’t get too warm when the sun is shining. I love that there is no velcro on the whole jacket. The sleeves cinch with metal snap buttons, and there is a storm flap with more metal snap buttons. The zipper works flawlessly, too. My only warning is to try it on because it is really oversized! I wear a Skogso Padded in size Large and a Nuuk parka in size Large, from before the recent sizing change. My jackets have the 40.9 inch chest. This one, even the Medium was way too big for me! I ended up buying the size Small, even though my chest and waist measurements are 41 inches and 37 inches. It fits me exceptionally, even with a t-shirt and cotton hoodie on underneath, especially because the raglan sleeves provide room for my broad shoulders. And the sleeves are also a perfect length. I am 179cm and weigh 88kg.

reviews.title: Do Not Buy: Inconsistent quality
reviews.text: I've been wearing hiangles for 4 years now. I tried the Team Blacks once, and went back to the Hiangle for what was, at the time, an ideal shoe for all kinds of climbing. I've bought 4 pairs since the redesign. The first were great, but a season of heavy use inside and out wore them down. After that, every pair has worn down the toe or delaminated the heel rubber too quickly, even as my climbing volume has noticeably depreciated in the past year and a half. I've hit a breaking point. I took my new shoes out for a session, and after one try on a heel hook intensive boulder, the heel completely separated. In an attempt to save my session, I tried a toe hooking boulder, only to have that rubber separate from the cloth upper. I've stuck with fiveten for as long as I can, but I'm not wasting any more money on their new, low-quality shoes, nor can I recommend them in good conscience to anyone else.

reviews.title: Light & Packable
reviews.text:
I unfortunately had to order two jackets as the US M/EU L was too big. I finally got to try out the smaller size on a recent ride. I am gutted Gore has now closed as I have been looking for years for a light, packable Gortex road cycling fit jacket that fits me. I haven't worn it in a big downpour but recently had a 2 hour ride in dense fog, the type you end up soaked. I was impressed how well it breaths plus it's very light & packable. reviews.text:
I did numerous searches for suggestions on a quality down sleeping bag that was light enough for backpacking but still very affordable.  There were many suggestions, but the one mentioned over and over again was the Kelty Cosmic Down 20, so I bought it.  Overall I am very impressed.  It came with a stuff sack that was fairly small already, but I put my new bag into a 10 liter compression sack which turned out to be a bigger sack than needed.  I'm guessing the final compressed size was in the 7 to 8 liter range.  The Kelty is new so I don't have a lot of field testing done yet but so far I think it was an excellent choice.  I'm 6'2" so the Long has plenty of room for me.  My son who is 6'5" tall also fit well in the bag which says it is good for people up to 6'6".  

Product comparison note:  I have an REI Radiant 20 and this new Kelty Cosmic 20 Down.  I bought the Kelty on sale for $150 (size long) and the Radiant 20 cost $200.  If they were the same price, I would buy the Radiant because it's just a little more fluffy and comfy.  But for the occasional backpacker who doesn't want to break the bank, the Kelty on sale is hard to beat.

Fit: 
--My roommate, like me, is probably considered plus sized by outdoor gear standards, so she also wanted a sleeping bag that fit her hips and wasn't claustrophobic to sleep in. 

--I gave her the gift and she got inside the sleeping bag. She felt like there was enough room to layer while not losing warmth, but she had enough room to roll around every night. 


Visual appeal:
--We both really liked the colors of the Mediterranean bag. It's eye-catching and won't get mixed up with other sleeping bags.


Value:
--Roomie didn't need a crazy expensive bag, but wanted something that she could use casually for years. This seems to fit the bill! (And my birthday present budget.)


Caveat:

reviews.title: Game-Changer for Beginners: My Experience
reviews.text:
**Review of Tarantulaces Climbing Shoes**

I purchased a pair of Tarantulaces about a month ago, and I couldn’t be happier with my decision! As a beginner who started bouldering just two months ago, transitioning from rental shoes to my own pair has been a game-changer.

Right from the first climb, I noticed an incredible difference in performance and comfort. The Tarantulaces provide excellent support and fit snugly without being too constrictive. This has allowed me to tackle more difficult routes with greater confidence and precision. I appreciate how the rubber sole offers fantastic grip, making it easier to maintain my footing on challenging holds.

One of the standout features for me has been the balance between comfort and performance. I can wear these shoes for longer sessions without discomfort, which is crucial for someone still getting used to the sport. They’ve truly elevated my climbing experience, enabling me to push my limits and improve my skills.

Overall, I love these shoes and highly recommend them to anyone looking for a reliable and effective climbing shoe, especially beginners. The Tarantulaces have made a significant difference in my bouldering journey, and I can’t wait to see how much more I can achieve with them!

reviews.title: Uncompromising All-Arounder
reviews.text:
My favorite shoes are often the ones I find myself most hesitant to wear... I want them to last forever! The new Solution Comp's are in that special category. Is this go worth the rubber?? Because out of the box these shoes have been a sticky edging precision tool that absolutely crushes granite of all angles and has already been surprised me with slick granite redpoints. The original Solution was a breakthrough in its ability to grab holds on steep boulders as effectively as it would surprisingly walk up technical vert climbing. Some downturned shoes are great on 30 degree overhangs but "pick" unexpectedly on vert and slab. The Solution can turn the lip of the cave and still tick-tack up the runout slab headwall. 

The toe hooking rubber is the stickiest I've felt in any shoe, and the heel has zero deadspace on my foot. I've always liked a more structured heel over an extremely soft heel (I like to feel like I'm "edging" when heel hooking) and the Comp is the perfect balance of feel and support.

I sized them a half size down as I do my Skwamas (39 instead of 39.5 for Muiras, TC Pros etc) and they were a pain to put on initially. Now that the neoprene sleeve and heel cup has broken in a little, I'm happy with the downsize. 

If you're having trouble getting them on, work your toes as deep into the toe box as possible before trying to pull the heel on. That way you can get the big toe all the way forward before trying to fit the shoe on.
reviews.author: EB

reviews.title: Precision and Power!
reviews.text: I've worn more pairs of Solutions in my 13 years of climbing than any other shoe, probably more than 20 pair. The Solution Comp is a great variation with some tweaks that change the fit and feel slightly. The toe box feels different with the new rubber patch for hooking/scumming/jamming. This takes a little time to get used to, but breaks in great. The heel is more shallow and much softer. I think it pushes the foot forward more aggressively and makes the shoe feel smaller / lower volume. The power feels the same, very snappy and precise. A great variation that will be sure to please all the folks who didn't like the molded heel on the OG solution. A great shoe for hard climbing anywhere. Inside or out.

reviews.title: Absolutely Awesome
reviews.text: My new shoe of choice for overhanging and foot-intensive routes. I am in love with the feel of this shoe and the softness of the shoe allows a maximum feeling of your footholds. Might I add that the heel is quite literally perfection. I've used this shoe on nearly all of my overhanging hard sends and will continue to do so.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: This is my shoe of choice for indoor climbing, outdoor bouldering and is the best pair of soft shoes I have ever owned. They are great for smearing but still perform well on small edges given how soft they are, especially if you get them really tight. They are very downturned so great for overhangs. The heel is really skinny which fits my heel perfectly but definitely something to bear in mind if your heels are a bit bigger. This makes them excellent for heel hooking and the toe hooks are excellent too. They are designed for lead/sport climbing, so the toe of the shoe is quite a bit further forward then the toe of your foot, which I like but I know some people don't so if that's you I wouldn't recommend this shoe. A shoe like the Theory has the toe closer so that might be a better option. Overall, a really really good and surprisingly versatile shoe.
reviews.author: Wile E. Coyote

reviews.title: So far so good...
reviews.text: Still breaking them in but impressed with both how they feel and perform. So far, I've used them only indoors. I'm effectively a 9.25 (US Women's) in street shoes and have long toes and fairly narrow, bony, arthritic feet. I wear a 41 in La Sportiva trail runner, approach, and mountaineering shoes/boots and a 41.5 (US 9.25) in Zamberlan trekking boots. I sized down to 40.5 (Women's 9) in the women's La Sportiva Solution Comps and the fit is perfect for me. I could probably have gone down to 40 without too much pain but nah: with these long toes and bony toe knuckles already scraping the upper, I'm good at 40.5.

To zip two sleeping bags together, one of your bags will need to have a right zip, and the second bag will have to have a left zip. It is important that the two bags are the same model. For a mummy bag, you must have one right hand zipping bag and one left hand zipping bag.They must be placed side-by-side, not one on top of the other to be zipped together.

reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve really been loving my Marmot tent! It also held up really well in cold, rainy weather and kept me dry and comfortable. I was honestly impressed with how well it handled the conditions. Definitely a great tent for outdoor adventures!

reviews.title: Amazing Free-standing Solo Tent
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I replaced my old 1-person tent with the Tungsten about 2 years ago and have used the Tungsten mainly in the winter months, but also a few times in the spring and autumn (I'm not a big summer camper). I've used it on both the east and west coasts and in dry and wet conditions. So far, I think the tent is perfectly fine ... sets up easily and is modern in color-coding the poles to clips, etc. The specs on the tent are perfectly reasonable for my purposes, but I have withheld a single star from the ratings as the fit of the rain-fly to the tent itself is a bit wonky, as is the placement of the tab for keeping the tent "door" rolled up and out of the way. The fly clips to attachment points on the tent itself, and the tent poles go through grommets in both the tent and the footprint. These clips, no matter how tight, are slightly off-spec enough that the fly was unable to be tightened up enough to prevent snow from accumulating in heavy patches on some parts of the tent. Of less concern, but a minor annoyance, is the way the door to the tent rolls up for stowage - the loop and tab are so far off point that there is always a drape of tent-door hanging out unless I fold the rolled door. Otherwise, the tent is spectacular for the price and the weight is negligible unless you're an ultralight fanatic (in which case there is a UL version). With just a little more attention to detail, this could very nearly be a contender for best overall freestanding 1-p tent out there.
reviews.author: T Rowe

reviews.title: Tough little tent in the wind.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Had this tent on a quick trip in the Winds. Per the namesake, the nights were exceptionally windy - 30 knots at least, with some rain. This tent held solid with no leaking. I like that it has more head clearance than many single person tents. Please include more stakes! I’m happy with this purchase, as the seams are tough. We’ll see how it does over the long haul.

I've taken it out a few times now and it has worked out great. The tent is very roomy, I had space ar my head and feet to store gear amd the vestibule had plany of room for my pack. This is a solid tent.

I laid down inside in this tent in the backyard and closed the zipper door to get a feel for the amount of space inside: I started to feel claustrophobic. Not sure if this will happen in another one person tent or I need a bigger tent. If I kept the tent I don’t feel it would last a few years given the material used. Disappointed.

reviews.title: Awesome Tent Purchase
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently completed the 20 mile Manistee River Loop Trail and spent two nights in this tent. I have absolutely no regrets about this purchase as the tent performed flawlessly. It is incredibly easy to set up/take down within minutes, had plenty of room for me inside and for my backpack in the vestibule, and there was adequate ventilation with no condensation despite the nights being cool. Best of all, the footprint is included so there is no additional expense for this important component to help protect the floor. All in all, I am extremely pleased with my Marmot 1p Tungsten Tent!
reviews.author: Cappiejoe

reviews.title: Excellent 3 Season Tent
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My first trip with my new Tungsten 1 Person tent was to Big Bend Ranch State Park last November. Temps ranged from lower 80’s during the day to lower 40’s at night. The tent weighed almost half what my previous one did. I was really happy about that. It also sets up in only a couple of minutes even when using the rain fly. On warmer nights the Tungsten was perfect without the fly. Great views of a star filled sky that way as well. On the coolest nights I was super comfortable with the fly on to help retain some heat. I was pleasantly surprised to find the air circulation was good enough to almost prevent all condensation from building up inside the fly. I am 6’2” and there was plenty of room for me and my long sleeping bag plus all of the gear that makes me happy to have close at hand. Don’t misunderstand though; it is definitely a one person tent. After those 4 nights I would definitely recommend this tent. It has all of the quality you would expect from a premium brand like Marmot. Get one for yourself without fear of disappointment.
reviews.author: Howie763

reviews.title: Roomy for 1 person
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Set up and take down was easy. I have not had a chance to us it yet. Only set up in the yard. It did get rained on and was dry inside. Lite weight for bike camping. Foot print is durable enough for protection. Looks to have good ventilation.
reviews.author: RJD1

reviews.title: Good balance between size/weight and quality
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This is a great tent for the solo traveler that finds a sweet spot between being lightweight but also durable.  The shorter tent poles allow it to be more compact which is a bonus when traveling light.  I also like that it doesn't feel small and make me claustrophobic when I'm inside it.  The door zips almost 360 degrees which allows for easy entry/exit.  The fly provides good protection and ample room and storage area by the door.  I also like it has a vent on the top to allow good airflow on hot days.  The included footprint is a nice bonus that some other tents make you buy separately.  The only area that was a slight letdown was it didn't include a tent gear loft.  Thankfully my wife is a skilled seamstress and will be making one out of mosquito netting so that issue will be resolved.  Overall, I'm very impressed with this tent finding a balance with being small and lightweight while still having quality to the materials.  I've had really good luck with Marmot tents over the years and I'm certain this will be a similar experience.
reviews.author: Adrenaline Junkie

It’s been solid for both mauka hikes and makai beach camping — definitely a good tent for island conditions.

reviews.title: Lesser quality than older Tungsten version
reviews.text:
My first tungsten 3p tent was purchased approximately 10 years ago and has been very well used (and well taken care of). I decided to purchase a new Tungsten tent because I just couldn't get the water to bead away after waterproofing many times over the years (Kiwi Camp Dry and Wood's silicone waterproof spray). Also, the velcro tabs kept coming off even though I I glued them back on... and the tent clips (that attach to the poles) were starting to tear away from the screening. Anyway, it had served me very well and I accepted that these are the things that slowly start to break down after many years of use.

In setting up my new Tungsten tent, I instantly noticed the quality of materials did not match up to my old version of this tent. Material is finer (feels thinner), all of the strapping and buckles are smaller and there is just an overall feeling of cheapness to the tent. 

I've only been on a 5 day trip so far and it kept me dry. And I do appreciate the improvement with moving from plastic to aluminum for the piece that ties the main poles together. I expect it will serve it's purpose but just disappointed in the loss of quality in materials. I also suspect that it will not last as long as my old version.

One last gripe, there are 8 points of tie down on the tent itself plus 4 more to secure the fly in high winds, for a total of 12 tent pegs required, so why does the tent only come with 6 pegs.

I weighed the tent and fly and there is only a 5 gram difference between the old and new, so cutting quality on the materials wasn't to reduce weight.

Very disappointed, I used to rave about this tent to everyone I knew but will no longer be recommending it unless the quality in materials is improved upon.

questions.text: What is the floor made out of? How thick is the fabric? How thick is the denier polyester taffeta?

answers.text:
Hello Vinnysea,
Thanks for your question. On the Marmot Tungsten 3-Person Tent, the floor is constructed from 68-denier polyester taffeta with a durable PU coating and fully taped seams to help protect against ground moisture and abrasion. Rather than being measured in millimeters, the “thickness” of this fabric is defined by its denier rating, which refers to the weight and durability of the yarn, so in this case, the floor fabric itself is 68D polyester taffeta. This denier level is intentionally chosen to balance toughness and packability, giving the Tungsten a floor that’s robust enough for repeated use on varied terrain while still keeping overall tent weight manageable.

reviews.title: Decent down jacket for moderate cold
reviews.text:
Overall I like this jacket. With just a 60gsm Alpha Direct hoodie underneath it I was just starting to get chilly at around 20F while sitting in the tent. The fit is good, though I wouldn’t want more than 1 light- and 1 mid-weight layer under it. At 798g/28oz for size XXL the weight and bulk aren’t bad in a winter pack. I knew I wasn’t getting anything UL when I ordered it.  Something pushes slightly against the middle of my back but I can’t feel anything obvious with the jacket off. Maybe it’s the structure provided by the Ceiba flower fibers (Kapok)? There’s no inside pocket as stated in the description, which is probably the worst thing about the jacket for me. I’ll have to see how it “handles moisture and movement” some time this winter. Though I doubt I’d actually be moving in temps low enough to require this jacket in order to be warm, but would instead set up the tent I always have in winter and hunker down. 

For the $82.50 I paid I think it’s a great buy, if I could go back and do it again I’d buy a few more as gifts. I doubt I’d spend the current price of $165, and no way would I pay the $275 regular price.

reviews.text:
I didn't feel a need to review this pad until I bought some cheaper pads for my garage climbing wall and saw how high quality this metolius is comparably.

It is worth the price for the size. Very useful size I don't see the point in these 36x48 pads that you need 2 of. 

This pad is very firm and I like that. I could knock the wind out of me if I fall flat on my back from a roof but that is not a typical fall for me.

This pad is not a great bed because it is too firm but it is a good couch.

the angled hinges, good fabric, tight fitting cover and firm foam put the madrock pads I bought to shame. It is fine because the madrock pads  were 25 percent off and were significantly cheaper, and I needed 4 of them for my garage.

 This pad is miles ahead in quality. I would recommend this to anyone. Don't be afraid of the size bigger is better. do cost per square foot analysis it is not that much more expensive than some cheaper options.

Great chest pockets and hand pockets on outside with a bonus pass pocket on the left arm.  Removable powder skirt which is nice because that's a rare need in PA.  Ample room for layering so I can adapt from sub zero temperatures to spring skiing with easy to use pit vents to cool off.  If I had one complaint and its a nit-pick, the inside drop pockets could be deeper and lower.  They are located in a spot that if I put my goggle lens in, I can't get it to a comfortable spot and the lens feels uncomfortable pressing on my torso.  No worries though, the large hand pockets are where they will reside and I definitely give the Boundary Ridge 5 stars regardless.

reviews.title: Good jacket, just can’t go the distance…
reviews.text: I’ve had this jacket for several years now and as much as I like it, it’s also a huge disappointment in the following ways:  delicate fabric (I have patched it numerous times) and hemorrhages feathers, especially on the arms, & no cinch feature in the hood. If you just think about coming in contact with a branch, or maybe some rocks, this thing develops a hole. And the same can be said for feathers - it started losing feather the first month I had it. It’s a shame we don’t see more welded seam construction because every place there is a stitch a feather finds its way out. I’m tempted to get  another one though because the fit is good and it’s a decent little lightweight down jacket. If you plan on casual town wear it probably will do just fine, I use my jackets for everything - hiking, walking, doing outside chores and so on - admittedly, I am probably pretty taxing on my clothes - I don’t worry about getting dirty if the need arises. This jacket looks like a patchwork piece - lots of tenacious tape and featherless baffles. I also think it could use a small pocket tucked inside - like a reverse napoleon pocket. FYI:  the zipper is a little brat.
reviews.author: larjam

reviews.title: Everything I had hoped for.
reviews.text: This jacket is everything I wanted in a lightweight down jacket. I have used it repeatedly for snowshoeing and hiking in the winter. It is a fantastic jacket as a standalone or with a layer underneath or on top. I highly recommend it.
reviews.author: G Blase

reviews.title: life time purchase
reviews.text:
So there I was, outdoor climbing on a dry November day in 2019, freezing as always. 
A buddy let me borrow his coat, which happened to be a men's Ghost Whisperer. I hadn’t known that a coat could leave you feeling warm, like really, truly cozy in the outdoor elements. 
I bought one that same day. It is now 2023 and I wear this coat most days in Fall, Winter, and Spring in the PNW. (Heavy usage)
I wear it backpacking, snowboarding, hiking, and when I am working at my barista job and while working my outdoor job as a rec guide. It somehow regulates temperature really well, I do not often sweat in it. Since it seems like it would tear easily, I typically wear it as an insulating layer, with something over it, and it has held up remarkably well. Just this year, I got my first tear in it and I put my first proud patch on it. Side note: in my 3+ years of owning it, I have washed it twice. It smells fine and it looks brand new. :) 

The only drawback I see in this coat is a personal one. I bought this coat in the bright orange color. (To be fair, the women’s colors were not as cool as the men’s). This is my only regret as it is made with such quality that I know this coat will last me at least 10 more years, if not my whole life. That means I unknowingly condemned myself to a life of bright orange. It was a bold choice, certainly a statement. Word of advice: Think about the quality and longevity of this item and really ask yourself, do you want to wear this color for the rest of your life??
For size reference, I am 5’4, 127 lb, and the women’s small size fits perfectly. I can wear a layering long sleeve underneath, but a sweatshirt underneath fits a little more snug than I prefer.
I did have to roll the sleeves up because they were approximately 2 inches too long. (Short arms for me, I guess.
Anyways, best coat. I love Mountain Hardware, and I am always trying to convince my friends to get a Ghost Whisperer. You should probably buy this coat.
reviews.author: Sav

reviews.title: Best Valued Light Down Jacket
reviews.text: This 2nd Gen GW/2 is our favorite, even though it’s only 800-fill RDS®-certified down insulation fill, as opposed to the 1000 fill of the latest GW/ UL.  The GW/2 also has the hem adjustable draw cord, which is absent in the newer UL.

reviews.title: So Light yet Super Warm!

It was just perfect for my most recent camper van road trip to Joshua Tree N.P., Mojave Desert and other parts of Southern California.  Good color.  One of the best purchases I’ve made for outdoor activities.  Prompt communication and delivery as well.

I just got this jacket for my trip to Iceland and was so excited, especially about the unique color (lantern). 

However, because the fabric is so thin and light, every single feather shows up behind the fabric and in all of the seams making it look like the jacket is dirty.

reviews.title: Favorite winter hiking jacket
reviews.text: I recently conquered my first 14er during a trip to Colorado, and brought this jacket while preparing for the big climb. As someone that get cold very easily, I thought this jacket layered with an outer shell and mid layer would help along the way. To my surprise, it kept me warmer than I could have expected and held its own against the high winds. Now, it’s officially my winter jacket. Looking forward to layering it with just a baselayer and taking it snowboard next seasons.
reviews.author: Yaz

reviews.title: Warm, but the feathers oh my!
reviews.text:
So I searched and searched for a jacket this season I live in northern Michigan and it gets pretty chilly. I went to multiple local shops but couldn't find this brand to try on for sizing so I winged it and ordered a small. For reference I am 5' tall and my weight bounces from 117-120 pounds and I'm a 36 D. This jacket fits like a glove when I'm just wearing a t-shirt or long sleeve. But also fits perfectly with a hoodie without making me look frumpy! I'm not sure how it does it to be honest lol. I was worried about the "garbage bag" looking material, but in person its perfectly fine. Its not super shiny but not like matte.It's a perfect in between. I am one to ALWAYS be cold. So this year I was really on the hunt for a good jacket I could take out steelhead fishing on the boat but also be versatile enough to wear everyday. Ladies if you are one to be cold all the time THIS IS YOUR JACKET! I have not complained about being cold once since I've bought it! It feels like it knows your body temp perfect to be quite honest. Not too hot but warm enough. Now I do really love this jacket and especially since I caught it at a good deal, but that doesn't mean it doesn't have a couple flaws.

CONS:
-I wish the logo was on the chest area and not the sleeve (but I guess that's just personal preference)
-I have had several threads/stitching come loose that I've had to cut. Just little ones but still at the price of this you expect the best quality.
-Theres no pocket on the inside. (again personal preference)
-NOW my BIGGEST pet peeve of all... the FEATHERS!! You wouldn't believe the amount of feathers I loose from this thing! I have black cloth seats in my 4runner, and when I get out there is ALWAYS at least a dozen feathers stuck to my seat. My husband also has a down jacket from a competitor brand and he doesn't have this problem so it does make me worry a smidge. 

OVERALL: I really hope this lasts me a while because I really do love the jacket and the warmth. I tried on quite a few and did tons of research before deciding on this one. But the warmth really is a huge important factor for me. I think I'm most impressed with that. I hope this helps someone else on the hunt :)
reviews.author: Chelsey0012

reviews.title: Compressible, Light, Stylish, but Not Durable
reviews.text:
I've owned this puffy for 2 years now, and I've really put it through the ringer (it's my only puffy). It's gone up many multipitch climbing routes, and has accompanied me while cragging, bouldering, skiing, biking, rafting, and camping. I even sleep with this thing on sometimes when I'm camping in really cold weather. The hood is really clutch and fits well over climbing helmets.

I love the compressibility and the weight-to-warmth ratio. I stuff it in a stuff sack instead of its own pocket because it's a really tight fit and takes a minute to zip up completely. It fits under a harness really well. Climbing in it is fine, but not ideal since it fits pretty snug. The zippers always zip and I've never had problems of it snagging.

I'm 135lbs, 5'8", and have broad shoulders. The medium has a performance fit and the shoulders are a smidge tight, but it's not too uncomfortable. The color is really pretty and vibrant. Overall, I do like the fit for belaying, camping, or chilling, but not the best for full-on activities like multipitch climbing since the shoulders feel a little restrictive for my body type.

I think it is a stylish, light, compressible, technical down jacket, but you have to give up durability which is unfortunate. 

At this point in its life, every time I go out to climb and pull it out of my pack, I find down precious coming out from a new micro-hole (see photos). It's mostly in the arms and near the hips where I think gets rubbed by harnesses a lot. I take care of my gear fairly well, but inevitably I will end up hiking through narrow canyons, hitting my arm on rock while bouldering or something, and be exposed to rocky elements in general. To that kind of use, I don't think this jacket holds up well, which is too bad because it's a nice technical piece of gear in most other aspects, especially for petite women.
reviews.author: Angela

reviews.title: Great, warm jacket - super shiny
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The jacket fits great and it warm. Unfortunately, the finish is super glossy. I've avoided buying many down jackets for the same reason, but the photo of this style didn't look shiny. I loved the olive, but with the gloss it looks a lot lighter in color than the photo. reviews.title: Beautiful ultralight garment, but broad-shouldered ladies beware!
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] For reference I am 5'10", 145 lbs with a slim/ athletic build and ordered size Medium.

The bad: I so desperately wanted this jacket to work as it would have rounded out my sub-10 lb base-weight so perfectly. But, alas, I also experienced that awkward tight-armpit phenomenon that others reference. I am puzzled by this fit, as the arm length was plentiful, and width (both in the arms and body) was generous- to the point of being borderline too large/boxy/busty. I understand that this width accommodates layering, but nothing accommodates layering when you're binding in the shoulders and armpits. Length in the body is just barely long enough, and I imagine that while sizing up to a large may improve the length/ armpits, it would render the jacket so loose, that it would drastically decrease the garment's thermal efficiency. 

The good: This jacket is light- as air and incredibly packable. The non- adjustable hood is perfectly designed to be snug and windproof, while also able to accommodate a hat or extra layer and not blind your peripheral vision. The lightweight elastic drawstring at the waist has a fantastic integrated toggle, and does exactly what it needs to do- simply and efficiently. If your build is slightly shorter with more narrow/average shoulders, look no further than this jacket!

Finally, this is an ULTRALIGHT jacket! Some reviewers have complained about the crinkle and shine of the fabric. If you want ultralight performance, you're going to have a crinkly, shiny jacket. It's just the nature of the technology at this point. I would advise you to not worry too much about style in the backcountry, and remind you that everyone will be crinkling away on their Neo-air sleeping pads anyway!

reviews.title: Innovative and Versitile 3 Season Staple
reviews.text:
Pros:
The Ghost Whisperer Jacket presents an impressive blend of weightlessness, breathability and durability. Its maintenance of loft when wet and low profile prepares it for an incredible variety of weather conditions. Butter fabric along the inner cuff resists pilling, is as soft as its name, and effectively seals in warmth. Many people fear the Ghost Whisperer fabric is flimsy and prone to tearing. I have yet to experience this and doubt I will. You can tell it was constructed with integrity, precision and attention to detail. Sewing work is clean throughout and notions are functional and sensibly colored. Clever design decisions such as loop for carabiner make this jacket highly user friendly.

Cons:
While the majority of the garment fits true to size, I find the arm holes of the jacket to be much too snug. It's a shame because everything else about this jacket lends itself to seamless layering and this feature is rather encumbering. I really appreciate the storage pouch-makes packing quite convenient. However, in the pocket that transforms into the pouch, there is an exposed serged seam allowance which is distracting when putting bare hands into pockets for warmth, especially since this seam allowance is absent from the other pocket. This is a minor issue and doesn't effect performance, but unfortunately apparent.

Overall a stellar product and highly recommended! If you are looking for a jacket you can throw over a t-shirt, tie around your waist and also pack for a friged alpine trip- look no further.

The Outdoor Research Helium Jacket is a great lightweight and packable option for cool-weather adventures. It offers a solid combination of performance, portability, and a reasonable price, making it an easy jacket to throw in a pack for changing conditions.

For me, it shines on cool fall mornings in the Boundary Waters or during late-season hikes. The biggest drawback is that it isn’t quite warm enough to be a standalone winter jacket, especially on colder days in the low 20s. I’d want to pair it with a sweater and vest for those conditions. I also found the fit to be a little tight across the back, particularly if you have a more muscular build. Overall, though, it’s a versatile, lightweight jacket that’s easy to pack and a great choice for fall and shoulder-season outdoor adventures.

reviews.title: Great jacket but....
reviews.text: Let me start by saying I love this jacket. It is my go to cool weather jacket and I have worn it for everything from casual winter dog walks to trekking in Nepal. It has a great fit and is super durable. I love the reinforced shoulders and arms, especially with a pack on. Saying this it has a couple cons. 1. It could be warmer. I read a lot of reviews about down jackets before I bought this one. Some said it was warm, and some said it was not as warm as they expected. I don't find that I can wear this jacket in weather cooler that -8-10C without needing a mid-layer or base layer. It could definitely benefit from some more down, even if it adds a bit of extra weight. There are lighter jackets out there if people are concerned about weight, so make it warmer. 2. The main zipper consistently puckers around the chest pocket, which, on its own, would make me reconsider purchasing it again. There's something about the way the chest pocket is sewn into the jacket that causes the zipper to pucker and fold over. This flaw seems like a relatively straightforward design fix, especially considering that none of my other jackets exhibit this issue. I am a big fan of OR product, but they have overlooked this aspect of the design. It's possible that they have addressed this in the new model year, as mine is a season or two old. However, I would strongly recommend trying it on before purchasing. If the chest pocket still feels tight and pulls on the zipper, it's worth questioning whether you can tolerate this issue, as it doesn't seem to improve with wear.

reviews.text: I was on the fence about buying this parka for a while. I needed something really warm to replace my mid-weight puffy for the cold snap(s) in the middle of January/February for both work and play. Boy did OR deliver, I love this jacket. The inside part of the zipper that touches your face is very soft and cozy to snuggle into and the whole jacket is surprisingly lightweight. I love all the pockets for my hands and they also prevent my phone from freezing and dying. The zippers can be a bit finicky as other reviewers said, and the sizing definitely runs big. I ordered the XL and found it nearly perfect. I find that most technical outdoor clothing fits slim around the hips and shoulders and OR is no exception. I have broad shoulders and hips and so the bottom part of this jacket is a bit tight. Not incredibly uncomfortable, but I would like to see something different in the future. I am also concerned about the zelcro on the sleeves tearing up the fabric around the pockets. Overall, a solid and warm jacket. I've used it for strenuous hiking from -10 to -30 C and it was perfect (not too warm), especially for someone who is always cold. Can't wait to test it out while ice fishing!

However, my only little critique would be for them to add in a waist cinch, so you can tighten it up in the middle to keep more draft down. I love the double zipper, very good feature (and hard to find now) for a long jacket! I would say it fits a bit bigger than actual size, since I also have a Helium down jacket in the same size that fits smaller (almost a whole size) than this one. For reference i am 5'6' (was)190 lbs, bought XL. I have since lost weight, am now 162lbs and can confirm a large would be sufficient. I hope this helps someone:)
reviews.author: Anyse

reviews.title: Excellent sizing for athletic/tall
reviews.text: I'm almost 6ft tall, and athletic/muscular, which can make it challenging to find ladies sizing in outdoor clothing that fits a woman's shape. This fits the bill! A miracle - it actually fits my hips/bootie, and goes all the way to upper hips, as an alpine parka should! Half star off, which is esthetic only - in the yellow, the fabric is rather see-thru, and the inside stuffing is multicolored, and looks a little odd. Very lightweight with a stuff sack. Taking this one mountaineering!

reviews.title: LOVE THIS JACKET!!!
reviews.text: I absolutely love this jacket!! It is so incredibly warm and comfortable, while still being lightweight enough to not feel like you can't move at all. Easily handling -10F temps, the hood also is nice and big with a wonderfully soft lining. The length is perfect as it covers your hips without making you feel trapped at any point - super easy to move around in without letting any cold air escape up the sides. My only comment is that I wish the front pockets (which are huge by the way!!!) were positioned just a little bit higher - I sometimes find myself having to reach down just a bit to fish out things that may have worked their way to the bottom. Regardless, I still absolutely love it and would highly recommend!!

reviews.title: Well-made, but not a cold weather jacket
reviews.text: First the pros: This jacket fits well and is very nicely constructed; it doesn't feel like any shortcuts were taken in the design and material and I would have kept the jacket if it were warmer. The cons: it is billed as a cold weather jacket. You can see from the photo I took as I held it up to the light that there are gaps where there is NO down. Even if it's filled with 800 down fill, it's not going to keep you warm in cold weather when you skimp on the down. This is a jacket for temps of no less than 40 degrees. I've added a comparison photo of the Rab Electron Pro Jacket - no gaps in the 800 down fill. It is a much warmer jacket.
reviews.author: Naomi

reviews.title: Warm, packs well, all around go to winter jacet
reviews.text: I wear the coat daily for casual wear and on the mountain. Alaska had an extremely cold start to this winter, with several weeks below zero. I spent several weeks skiing in negative temps, including -20F. This coat proved to be clutch on the skin track and while skiing down. It packs well, is warm but not too warm for activity, and looks great. With the cold temps, the snow has been light enough to just brush off and the coat has stayed dry. Like any down coat, it does get wet with heavy snow but the shoulders and hood are water proof, helping to keep me warm on those storm days. When the coat does get damp and wet from snow, it has dried quickly. This coat has become my go to puff. (I'd recommend a heavier puff for belaying or if you have to stand still for a long extended period of time in below zero temps.)
reviews.author: Heather

reviews.title: I love this coat so much!
reviews.text: I have nothing but praise for this coat! It's so durable. I have had it for 6 months and have already put it through the ringer and no snags or tears/holes, nothing. I even accidentally stepped on it with a crampons and not even a scratch! I love the bright greenish color too! I also love the length, adds more warmth and coverage for my backside.

reviews.text: Purple color is fantastic. Love the backpack shoulders. Small fits great (5'7, 36A, 135 lbs). I use as my main winter coat in Colorado. Packable and warm.

reviews.title: Perfect all around puffy
reviews.text: This is the warmest, most durable puffy I have purchased. I've already taken it climbing, backpacking, and on a scuba trip - it did great in all 3 environments. Great shell for the wind or rain or snow. I'll be taking it on all my adventures.
reviews.author: Mikayla

reviews.title: Truly abrasion-resistant and awesome!
reviews.text: Finally, a down jacket that withstands the rigors of my outdoor life! When OR introduced the Helium Down collection, I had to get one to try, because in my experience there is no such thing as a down jacket that is also durable. I usually take off the puffy to rock climb because previous jackets just can't take it. Every puffy I've owned has numerous patched holes from tree branches and snags. Well, I've put my Helium Hoodie through the wringer this fall, and it's truly as advertised! The Diamond-Fuse tech really works. I work as an outdoor guide, and I've worn my Helium as my outer layer on every trip October and November. I've led offwidth crack climbs wearing this jacket, I've bushwhacked, I've logged a lot of harness hours. There are no holes, no snags, no tears. No fuzzies from abrasion under my harness waist band. This jacket is amazing. Soft inside, warm and comfy. I haven't had a chance to really test the water repellency feature, but the hood and shoulder panel seem legit. Get this jacket; you'll love it!
reviews.author: Rebecca

reviews.title: I would definitely recommend to a friend!
reviews.text: Love this jacket! Love this color! I'm 5'5" and 140 lbs and I ordered a medium. I have a swimming background, so my shoulders are broad and I have long arms. I found the medium to be perfect for me! A large would have worked too if I had wanted something on the bigger side--just depends on the type of fit you want. Spending most of my time outside, this coat has been perfect for me. Its great for my technical adventures, as well as just going to and from class, or casual nights around town. Very happy with this purchase!

reviews.title: Great down puffy jacket, perfect for hiking
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Fit and Comfort
The jacket fits well, even with lots of layers underneath. It's close-fitting and well cut without being too tight. Nothing feels too tight or too oversized, even when moving around in the jacket. It is suitable for my activities. I recently hiked Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania and used this jacket as my inner layer puffy for most days of the trek. I've also worn it in more casual settings around town and to work, since it's a great looking jacket and functions well off the mountain too. It is very easy to adjust, with zipper pulls that are long enough to be usable with gloves on - a huge plus!


Warmth and Insulation
I've worn the jacket as part of a layering system down to 0 degrees Fahrenheit with 20-30mph winds so far, and was still warm enough. The insulation feels evenly distributed throughout the jacket and I did not notice any cold or hot spots. The warmth matches the jacket's intended use. 

Breathability and Moisture Management
The jacket did not trap moisture during activity. There were times I was a little warm, so I simply unzipped it to regulate. The jacket handled a minor amount of internal condensation and sweat well and did not feel wet. 

Weather Resistance
The jacket performed well in windy conditions. I did not notice any significant drafts or wind cutting through the jacket. 

Mobility and Use in Motion
I can freely move in the jacket while hiking. I did not feel restricted nor did I have issues with it bunching up. 

Packability and Travel
The jacket is fairly compact when packed. I had to look online at first to see how the jacket packed down, since there were not clear instructions printed inside the jacket or pocket that I could find. The jacket does fit easily into the left pocket that serves as its stuff sack. I have taken the jacket on longer trips and would do so again. 


Durability and Construction
The jacket held up very well after repeated use and washings, and shows no signs of wear. There are no issues with stitching, fabric wear, or insulation clumping, even after washing the jacket. All zippers and closures are working properly. 

Design and Usability
The elastic cuffs on the jacket are great for keeping wind out of the sleeves. The pockets are a good size but not too big. There are no standout or problematic design details that I noticed. I like the style and color. 

Overall Performance
I would recommend this jacket, and would buy it. It is best suited for hiking and other outdoor activities, along with wearing more casually day to day. It feels more durable than other similar puffy jackets I've owned in the past.
reviews.author: Claire G

reviews.title: Helium Down Hoodie in Thyme Green Rocks!!!
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Size Medium - Female 5'7" ~ 150lbs

I received this product for free in exchange for my honest review.

This jacket fits really well with baselayers or sweaters underneath. I can also put my medium shell ski coat over, and it fits well. The zippers are sturdy. The material is durable and didn't rip even when I was carrying bundles of firewood. The shoulders and the hood are sturdier in material, which helps with precip, although the jacket is not waterproof.

I have taken this jacket ski touring, Nordic skiing, snowmobiling, winter camping and hiking. As for warm rating, it is definitely not extreme warmth, but not a light layer either. It is right in the middle, which I believe is an essential layer to have year-round. This Hoodie packs down really small and is great for adventuring, especially when traveling up into the high alpine. 

I am super stoked on this jacket and would recommend it to all of my lady friends!! 

Outdoor Research gave me this free product to try.
reviews.author: Belle G

reviews.title: Armpits are very tight, while rest fit normal
reviews.text:
The material was shoved all the way up my armpits. I am a true medium, meaning never had an issue with OR products (5 foot 7 and ~135lbs). I felt like the material under my armpits was crazyyy tight and constricting. The rest of the jacket fit me perfectly though??  So disappointed.

The jacket color is gorgeous and jacket is high quality. I own an OR rain jacket that I love and was so excited about this jacket but had to return. My partner got the men's Medium, and that fit me better than this with zero armpit issue, but it's a bit longer and falls weird length on my thighs so probably won't buy the men's for myself either.

Other than that they are my favorite pants for the hot humid weather in South Carolina. They fit true to size, form fitting, but aren’t restricting.
reviews.author: BBPP

reviews.title: Best Pants Ever!
reviews.text: The Outdoor Research Ferrosi Pants are the best travel and hiking pants I’ve ever worn. They’re lightweight, quick-drying, and incredibly comfortable on the trail or on the go. The zippered side pocket is easy to access. They’re also surprisingly flattering thanks to the stretchy fabric, which allows for great freedom of movement. Another feature I love is the adjustable ankle design, they can be worn straight or use the cinch tie for a more tapered fit.
reviews.author: Best Pants Ever!
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: Durable and Stretchy for Thru Hikes
reviews.text:
I wore a pair of these pants for 5 months continuous hiking on various trails - rain, sun, snow, mud, you name it. They proved themselves over and over. The length was perfect and I often wore them with home-made ankle gaiters. Also as I lost weight on the trail (don't eat the local chicken!), I was able to use the string to cinch them in. Lightweight and quick-drying, they made washing on the trail easy, and the navy blue hid dirt and minor stains well.

The fabric was stretchy enough to handle climbs, scrambling, and long days with a pack, and while they faded in strong sun over time, that didn’t affect performance. The right thigh pocket is perfectly placed and no issues with the zip, and the back pockets are deep which is handy.

I never quite got the gist of the little elastic things and plastic pieces around the ankles, so wouldn't be disappointed if they disappeared.

I do wear another pair casually, and ended up buying Ferrosi shorts for hiking as well. For comfort, fit, durability etc. I can't say enough. Please don't change this product OR they rock!

reviews.title: Short
reviews.text: I wanted to love these, but the regular is too short and the tall is too long. They felt like heaven and were super stretchy. They would be perfect if you aren't 5'9" with a short torso. 32 would be a better length.

reviews.title: Are These The Perfect Pants
reviews.text:
I had a pair of these about 5 years ago when I walked the Camino in Spain. After walking, I backpackad throughout Europe for the next 12 months. These were my only pants. They are durable, lightweight, breathable, dry fast and I loved them for all of that plus the zippered pocket that kept my wallet and passport safe in Paris when two friends had theirs stolen. The majority of the time I hand washed them since an actual washing machine was wishful thinking. Fortunately, they don't hold onto sweat and stink like some man-made fabrics so a sink, some warm water, a little bit of soap, and some elbow grease kept me from being too socially unacceptable.
Did they pill? Yes, between the thighs. So what. The zippers held, no seams unraveled, the front button didn't pop when I first wore them and was too fat for them and the drawstring was a lifesaver when they were too loose when I finished. Ladies, these are a perfect pant. 
I just bought a new pair. It's the right time. Adventure awaits!
reviews.author: Robin

reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.text: It’s perfect for hiking. I got light gray from my husband size 2. I’m 5’3” average Asian women. A little long (regular) for me but very perfect to cover my ankles for me. And it’s very LIGHT AND BREATHABLE . I will buy another color too.
reviews.author: Fit Wahine

reviews.title: Crashed a dirtbike and they look new
reviews.text: I skidded on my side about 8 feet after crashing a dirtbike going way faster than I had any right to, and the pants look new. I don’t know if the current fabric is the same as these, but I bought them about seven years ago, wore them hiking, and then decided to take up dirt biking last Saturday (you are correct, these are not appropriate pants for that sport). The side of my leg that I landed on is covered in baseball-sized black and green bruises, and I do have broken skin. The pants are untouched. I have no idea how. OR you killed it
reviews.author: HaileyO

reviews.title: Best hiking pant
reviews.text: I bought two pair of these hiking pants after Whitewater rafting the Grand Canyon with my son who was wearing them. They repelled water well, were lightweight, and protected his legs from sunburn. After buying two pair, I was so in love with them that I bought two more. The fabric is nice enough that I can wear them to work as well as hiking in Colorado.
reviews.author: Mamafresh
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Lightweight Hiking Pants
reviews.text: I am in love with these pants, they are incredibly stretchy, durable, comfortable, and flattering. I took them on 3 day backpacking trip to test them and they held up beautifully. We ended up doing some boulder hopping which included me sliding on my butt quite a bit, and after the fabric looked good as new. They’re easy to roll up, clean up well after I spilled food on them, and fairly water resistant. I’m 5’7” 135 lbs with a 26” waist but bigger thighs and a size 2 fit great. I usually don’t like the drawstring in the waistband cause I normally wear a belt when serious hiking/ backpacking so I can carry. But even wearing these around town they are flattering to cinch the drawstring down. I loved these pants and bought a second pair after the trip!
reviews.author: Megan T
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Pilled and torn within the first week
reviews.text: After reading some reviews (e.g., "I'm an archeologist and these held up forever out in the field!") I had higher hopes for the Ferrosi pants than they bore out. I purchased them before a multi-day backpacking trip. I like the way they feel, though the material is thin enough that even keeping a hair tie in my pocket resulted in the outline of a circle on my thigh. I was disappointed to find a pull in the fabric on my first day wearing them (during which I rode a train--there was no major activity), but figured it was just bad luck. Then, a few days into the trip I realized that the material was pilling around the waist/fly. My backpack waist straps weren't hitting it, so it wasn't that--I still don't know what did that. And then I took a spill on the trail and tore a hole in the seat of the pants. (Not likely the pants fault, but thicker fabric would've held up better, I suspect.) In general I like these, but not enough to buy another.
reviews.author: BackpackerGal

reviews.title: Awesome waterproof pants
reviews.text: I've gone through a lot of outdoor/field pants, and these are my favorite so far. Today I submerged my legs in flowing water up to my knees for about half an hour, and the pants remained completely dry. I didn't buy these because of the waterproofness, however, these will definitively be my go-to pants for rainy/wet days. Other than that, they are very comfy and look nice. The only small downside I've found is that they seem to have stretched a bit after only a few days of use? I'm hoping they'll shrink in the wash.

reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Bought these pants for hiking. I used for the first time on an 11-mile hike with some climbing. The temp started in the 50's and ended in the 70's. These pants were perfect for the temperature change and I never sweated like in other bottoms. I will be buying another pair! I am 5'6", 134-136 lbs and bought a size 6.

The best part is how versatile these pants are, wear outdoors or wear into town for dinner. I love Pants that are dual purpose. Great job Outdoor Research!!!

The material is very lightweight and would not offer much abrasion resistance you would need for mountaineering. I wore them ~5 day for hiking and the material was already pilling. I miss the zip front pockets.  The back pockets are too small to be good for much. I love that you still offer them in a short inseam. I am usually a size 10 or 12.  I bought the size 12, they fit well, but we will see how much they stretch out.

They are light weight & pack small.   I am 5' 7", weigh 130lbs.  Size 6 regular fit perfectly.

reviews.author: bemikyla

reviews.title: Please make more colors for plus sizes!
reviews.text: I love these pants. Super comfortable for all sort of activities, especially when it's hot. I have a pair in navy blue that I've put through the wringer and continue to mend ripped seams and patch holes. These are the best fitting plus size hiking pants I have found, including specialty brands that make only plus sizes. Please, please, PLEASE make these pants in more colorways!! Or at least offer the ranger green in plus sizes. It's baffling that that the options are black, navy, and TWO shades of off-white, including one that is inexplicably called "dark sand"??? You've got to be kidding me. I will wear my navy pants until they disintegrate. With any luck, OR will be offering my size in new colors before that happens!

reviews.title: Great briefs
reviews.text: Used these to replace all my boxer briefs in the field and just about anywhere now. Tried many popular brands and these take the cake. I don’t  notice I’m wearing them and with boxers/briefs that’s the goal in my book. Keeps me feeling fresh in extreme heat and during long hikes. In the field I can go a couple days in these or even longer. Used them for everything from running to long range days.

reviews.text: Perfect fit and very breathable.  Wore it on a 7-mile hike up Quandary Peak and it was extremely comfortable.  My favorite hiking underwear.  I'll be buying more.

reviews.text:
Yes, I’ve only worn these on a handful of consecutive hikes, and yes I’ve noticed some pilling of the fabric even before their first wash. But they fit great and they are insanely comfortable, and feel very durable yet lightweight and tactical/technical. 

The deep jeans-style front pockets don’t bother me like other reviewers. And I thought maybe I’d miss the convertible pants/shorts these are replacing, but I could wear these all day. And I find the low-profile leg pouch and zippered back pocket to cover the bases. I don’t want to use my pants as a giant storage container anyway. 

They are very cooling and provide all-day UV protection. 

I can already say I’d buy these pants again and again.
reviews.author: timarmitag1451567
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Awful Durability
reviews.text:
I own a lot of OR gear that I love – two jackets, bucket hat, gloves, gaiters, etc., and I had been looking for a pair of nice looking hiking pants that I could wear to the office or business meeting or brewery and also hike in.  For 10 years a pair of Kuhl pants served that purpose but unfortunately the (excessive) stitching began to unravel and they no longer looked professional.  As I always do, I researched a lot of different pants and decided to go with the Ferrosi pants.  I have always been impressed with OR plus Outdoor Gearlab, which I usually trust, rated them very highly.
Living in Texas, I did not get to try them out for a while because it was too hot for pants.  I wore them inside and appreciated the fit, stretchability and features.  So I was very excited to finally get to hike in them during a recent trip to Santa Fe.
As expected, the pants performed well during my first hike.  However, taking a break half way through the hike I noticed two scrapes/runs in the material near my left pocket (see photo).  I could not believe it.  I had been hiking on well established trails, not bushwhacking and couldn’t even remember running across any brush that would have caused such damage.
Needless to say I am extremely disappointed with the durability of these pants.  The aforementioned Kuhls I had owned for 10 years, and backpacked, played disc golf (in Texas (meaning cactus, mesquite and other thorny things), hiked, bushwhacked and not once did they show a visible scrape, scratch or tear.  And all the while maintained a professional look
But the first time I wore the Ferrosis, they became damaged on a well-manicured trail, apparently with minimal contact.  Are they ruined?  No.  Of course I can still hike in them.
And I debated what rating to give the pants and decided that based on my purpose for buying them (hybrid office and hiking use) and the fact that they now look ragged (after one use!) it was only fair to rate them lowly because of their horrendous durability and easy tearability.  

So now I find myself again in the market for a pair of pants that I can hike and then go to a meeting in – I guess I’ll buy a new pair of Kuhls.
reviews.author: LMC12

reviews.title: Great for hiking, do not expect much for WR
reviews.text: Very comfortable hiking pants, great fit. Do not buy it for the “weather resistance”, 10 m waking in the rain and they will be soaked.
reviews.author: Onis

reviews.title: Great pants but fabric pills
reviews.text:
I have bought two pairs over the years. I like the style and fit but pretty quickly the fabric starts to "pill" especially over the upper thigh.
I have both the early one with the elastic draw-cord ankles, which I prefer, and later ones with the hemmed straight cuff.
reviews.author: Skier in Vermont

reviews.title: Great Features, Fit and Style, but...PILLING!
reviews.text: I purchased three pair 3+ yrs ago.  Love the style, fit, color options. stretch fabric, wicking, and comfort.  Like the flush pockets, including the spring-loaded zipper pocket on right front leg (and now in back as well).  After 3+ years I noticed heavy pilling of the fabric and some of the stitching coming lose, so just purchased four replacement pair. (If I find a good thing, I tend to stick with it!)   All the positives still stand, HOWEVER, after two washes I'm starting to see pilling of the fabric in the front pocket area; not a good sign of longevity!  I'll probably keep for the positive attributes mentioned, and just deal with the pilling via a disposable razor gently across the areas of pilling, but agree with another comment:  Stop always trying to "improve" something.
reviews.author: HGIII

reviews.title: Poor Durability
reviews.text: Stitching failing after 6 washings.  Stitching is failing on rear seam. Inseam and back pockets. Also pulling.
reviews.author: Stacey M
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: Best travel pants out there.
reviews.text: First off, probably the most comfortable travel pants out there. The stretch of the pant is perfect for travel, hiking, or working out. These really excel when doing starts or climbing activity where you need a lot of swing in your leg. The side zipper pocket is perfect for a wallet and passport when traveling and the front pockets fit all your normal items. The downside to such a great fabric is: 1) everything in your pockets shows through, so for pictures, maybe empty your pockets out or have weird shapes showing through. 2) After 4 days (two pairs) of my pants already started showing pilling on the sides from a seatbelt. Nothing about the belt was abrasive, but the quick of wear was a little disappointing. 3) The back pockets are a little worthless unless you have nothing more than an ultra thin wallet or piece of paper. It's not really the fabric, it's just not really comfortable with anything in the back pocket in pants that are so lightweight. Lastly, I also own OR rain pants. I didn't need to even put them on since these pants wicked away water so well. It takes quite a bit of water before they absorb anything. If you're moving around and sort of "snap" your pants all the water is instantly gone. Highly recommended for travel and outdoor activities. Go get a pair!
reviews.author: Christopher

reviews.title: I loved these pants until...
reviews.text: The comfort, style, fit, and look of these pants is outstanding. They are so comfortable and so versatile, and I could wear them in any setting. They are lightweight, but not too lightweight, and very breathable as well. However, and this is a big however, I have only had these for less than 6 months, almost exclusively casual wear, and the pilling is terrible. Not only that, random threads have popped out that I have had to cut off. I would therefore consider the durability and quality of these pants to be atrocious. I am so disappointed because up until they started falling apart, they were by far my favorite pants.
