reviews.author: Ray

reviews.title: Great all around pant
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Bought for a climbing road trip. Wore daily on my motorcycle (under mesh over pants), they were comfortable in all conditions. Put on lots of miles hiking and climbing, from the alpine to the desert, and in heavy forests. Theyve kept me cool and dry and no tears through it all. The cinch at the bottom is great for climbing - on a future model it would be great if the loops created when cinching were hidden inside the pant, definitely a small tripping potential. No other complaints to date. Love these pants.
reviews.author: Jay

reviews.title: Suitable for Everyday Wear
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My new favorite pant and the most comfortable pair I own. They are also very light, thin, highly breathable, and have drawcord cuffs so you can cinch them up higher on your calves if needed. All of these are great qualities in this Middle Tennessee hot humid weather.
reviews.author: Charles

reviews.title: Fantastic pants !
reviews.text: (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) My new Ferrosi pants arrived just 2 days before I departed for my hike to Albania. Hiking through the peaks of the Balkans, my Ferrosi pants saved my skin from the low lying bushes/branches and mud/snow. The breathable fabric also kept my legs from getting over heated from the sunny daytime humidity. The pockets were perfect for holding my phone for the quick snap shot and zipper pocket for carrying my personal valuables.
reviews.author: Razor

reviews.title: The BEST pants EVER!!!
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been rocking the Ferrosi pants since they first came out. The second generation were horrible (fit off, no rear zippered pocket). But, the latest gen is OUT OF THIS WORLD PERFECT!!! I have eight or nine pairs (every color that's been made). These pants are PERFECT for hot weather full length coverage with protection from the sun and nature. I use them exclusively while traveling (currently in Japan). The side pocket fits a US passport perfectly (I can fit three FYI). And, the new cuff cinch is flawless.
reviews.author: Matty from AK

reviews.title: Extremely baggy, longer than advertised inseam.
reviews.text: While these pants are light and breathable, they are ridiculously baggy. Looks nothing like the product photos unless the model has calves like tree trunks, and they're not visibly cinched. They're also longer than the advertised 30" inseam, causing them to bunch up significantly. I was hoping these would be a pair I could wear to the office and on the trails like my Zions, but they look like sweatpants, so I'll likely be returning them. For reference, I'm 5'10" and 150 lbs and ordered the 30x30 in Pewter.
reviews.author: Tim

reviews.title: Better than the old version
reviews.text: This is the third generation of Ferrosi Pants for me and by far the best. The new material is great so far, just as stretchy and light as the previous. The pockets are improved with a bigger hip pocket that is perfect for the current phones and the security of a back zippered pocket. The front pockets are slightly different and now more jean like and therefore deeper. I've seen other reviews complaining about fit. From my experience the fit is nearly identical to the previous version. I don't have issues with the waist and have compared directly. The new are a slightly different shape with a little more tapper into the waist. To me the legs are slightly less tapered in the way they fit which is a positive to me. I included a photo of the new (left) and previous (right) for comparison. I'm 5-10 and 185 lbs and ordered a 32x34. I prefer the longer length. After getting these I ordered the Crux Pants and I'm also very happy with them and just ordered the 12" Over Shorts. I think the Ferrosi line just got better.

reviews.title: Great jacket - 2 major flaws
reviews.text:
Great jacket but there are 2 major flaws that will probably get me switching back to my Helly Hansen Loke 2.0. 

1. Sleeves are 5-6 inches too long. Sleeves shouldn't go too much onto your hands. My fingers don't even make it to the end of the sleeves with my hands down at my side. Makes wearing it very uncomfortable when there is that much extra fabric flapping around your hands. Then it just bunches up on your arms. 

2. The cuffs on the sleeves are too large is you don't have thick cuffed gloves on. The opening is so large that your hand just swims in the opening. Must close all the way just the keep them on your wrists. 

Since these 2 things can't be tailored on a jacket like this, it makes me very disappointed in it since everything else is great. The stretch and fit in the shoulders and chest are great.

reviews.title: Amazing mountaineering softshell pants
reviews.text:
I bought this to use as a double weave softshell for alpine mountaineering and it's been perfect. It works as advertised and it's hard to find any fault with it.

It's flexible and breathes well so you don't get sweaty with it on. It's sufficiently and modestly wind resistant and water resistant. Light snowfall and sitting on snow didn't soak through and it held up fine against heavy winds (enough so that I didn't feel a need for a hardshell on top)

It's pretty durable and has taken accidental impalements with a crampon without falling apart,  likewise for catching it with an ice axe.

It's marketed as 3-season pants but I took it up Mt Fuji for a winter summit and it performed great. Great all around.
reviews.author: brownie123

reviews.title: Great pant for rough conditions
reviews.text:
Just received these pants 2 weeks ago. As soon I tried them on I knew they were special. I own the Cirque I pant in small, which are a bit short and tight @ the waist. These new model I bought in medium, and they seem just right. The pockets have changed, however, and for the better.
All are larger, and quite capacious.

reviews.text: Just received these and tried them on. They’re a comfortable fit and well-made. Tough material that looks like it will be warm even in high wind.

reviews.title: Great but!
reviews.text:
I love the features,color options, and the fact that they come in a short length which is not that usual in outdoor apparel.
   But as others have said, the fit is a little odd, with the crotch being really long and the hips and butt being too baggy,,and I have an ample rear and thighs.
reviews.author: Dave wave

reviews.title: Great bike pant
reviews.text: If you are looking for a great cold weather fat biking pants these are it. I’m on my second pair. Love the stretch material and the mobility in the knees.  The scuff guard is great for protecting from the chain and chain ring. All in all I recommend these pants.

reviews.text: Great pants bombproof!
reviews.author: Patrick

reviews.title: Great alpine climbing pants!

reviews.title: Maybe not as good as the Circ2

This was the first time I’ve used them and will give them another shot, but seems odd and might have to go back to the older version

reviews.text: I have 2 earlier pairs of Cirque pants and they are very well constructed.  I just received the Cirque 3 pants, and these are also well made except for the logos on the pants.  They are iron on and not embroidered.  It makes me more reluctant to buy future Outdoor Research products if they are going to start cutting costs on such high dollar items.
reviews.author: Ross

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: I've used these a few times now for climbing the Teton's and on Rainier.  Great fit, warm and very durable.  Highly recommend for those adventures in more rugged terrain.
reviews.author: Matthew W
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Weird Fit
reviews.text: Crushes my groin, but still have a lot of slack in the waist and thighs and some drape in the seat. Quite annoying considering I like most other things about the pant. Good flex, I like the leg opening and feature set there. I do prefer integrated belts over Velcro side tabs, although this buckle does bring concern over longevity with how slim and flimsy it feels.
reviews.author: Mack88

reviews.title: Strange fit, rise is too long.
reviews.text: Great that these are offered in short length. Thick high quality fabric and good stretch. However, I was disappointed by the fit through the crotch. The rise is way too long proportional to the leg length. This means that unless I pull the waist way up to 2-3” above my bellybutton, every time I lift my knees for a step, my movement is restricted by the crotch of the pants (which sits midway down my thighs). Not ideal, since I wanted these for ice climbing and will be high stepping regularly. Might have to try them with suspenders…
reviews.author: Ian G.

questions.text: A problem I often face while doing a long backpacking trips is the hip strap of my backpack will squeeze my belt and make the belt a nuisance on my pants. Has anyone ever had a problem hiking 16 miles plus with at least 60 pounds in their bag, while wearing these pants with the built in belt? Does the fabric belt and plastic buckle chafe your waist and make it sore??

answers.text: The Cirque III belts generally play pretty nice with a hipbelt. The Cirque III uses a low‑profile webbing belt and a flat plastic buckle that sits inside a brushed, lightly padded waistband with OR’s ActiveTemp treatment, so there isn’t a hard metal buckle for your pack hipbelt to mash into you.
answers.author: Keaton R.

reviews.title: Amazing features, breathability, and waterproofing
reviews.text: My Foray kept me bone dry during hours of rain and walking through wet brush even after the rain ended. The pit zips going all the way to the bottom hem makes it great for keeping coverage from the rain while being able to release body heat to ventilate, I used that when the rain had ended but every branch and leaf still was wet so it kept me dry still.
reviews.author: JACKSON M

reviews.title: Huge value for an awesome rain shell.
reviews.text:
I managed to snag this jacket on sale and I could not be more pleased not just with the jacket, but with the value as well. 

Bought this piece as part of my main system for my first attempt at submitting Mount Ranier. 

While the mountain may have stopped us at 8100 feet with 13 degree temps, 25mph winds, pounding snow…essentially a whiteout, I was still totally dry and cozy with this, a baselayer (in addition to gloves, a buff, and beanie). 

Can’t recommend enough! Outdoor Research will be the first place I look for pieces in the future.
reviews.author: Ihavenonickname
reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: Great Company and Gear!
reviews.text:
BLUF: Great brand that stands behind their products and make sure the customer is taken care of! 

I had bought an Outdoor Research rain jacket, the Men’s Foray II Jacket in May of 2023 and I loved the color, material/Durability, and breath ability but my jacket always seemed to be not very waterproofed and I ended up wearing it as a windbreaker or a light sprinkle. I was disappointed but figured I was just stuck with a defective item, until I saw an ad online about OR Warranty. I reached out that day and with in a week I had a new Men’s Foray 3L Rain Jacket in the mail. It came just in time for the rainy season in Hawaii and has done great through these last two Kona storms, I stayed bone dry and not a drop soaked through. I am happy with the product and even more happen to support a reputable company that is here for the outdoors and military and not just for fashion. Thank you! 

Shaun
reviews.author: Shaun

reviews.title: Great breathable outer layer that protects from rain and wind.
reviews.text: I’ve worn this a few times and one was in some moderate rain and I stayed completely dry. Definitely protects from the wind and I also do like that the arm pits have the zip option! Pros: lined zippers, armpit zippers, lightweight. Cons: haven’t found any yet.
reviews.author: Darian G

reviews.title: dont be fooled by its good looks
reviews.text: Good looking jacket more than anything else. Build is horrible. Even much cheaper jackets can hold the tension with the little band that tighten the jacket at the bottom. Also the little grommet broke off very easily. This jacket feels very fragile. I really dont know how it got so many awards. I literally only wore it once and noticed major flaw right away. Its really sad just how bad the quality is for things these days even when you pay an arm and leg. I am think i might just go with a waxed cotton jacket at this point. The quality and durability of synthetics is horrific.Its day and night obvious they did cost cutting on this jacket and yet charged crazy price for it.
reviews.author: Joey

reviews.title: Replaced same model that lasted 9 years.
reviews.text:
Still pricey for a heavier rain jacket that requires retreatment annually to not wet out.
Internal seams finally separated but still a solid choice for a one quiver jacket. Still haven’t improved the annoying collar unless it it’s totally up or way down mostly unzipped.
reviews.author: Ed B

reviews.title: No longer 3L Gore-Tex
reviews.text: I've had several 3L Foray Rain Jackets, and they've all performed perfectly. Always true to size, with a stretchy athletic fit. I was bit bummed to learn that the Foray is being longer constructed with Gore-Tex waterproofing. Still, a solid jacket made by a fantastic manufacturer with an unbeatable "infinite" guarantee.

reviews.title: Low quality

reviews.title: It keeps you dry !
reviews.text: Finally... A jacket that does what it says its going to do -  so happy I purchased this. Excellent rain protection I experienced over 2 hours in medium rain on walk.  No wet out, no leakage - water just ran off and kept me dry the whole time.  Highly recommend this jacket for sure !

reviews.text: Great product. Stood out in rain for an hour, heavy rain, and was completely dry.

reviews.text: its a very good pretty durable rain jacket. i went on an artic ocean trip on hte coppermine river with it and it held up through all of the things i threw at it even falling off a clif while getting chased by 4 bears. its a great jacket at a good price so anyone can use it and it will work for everyone

reviews.title: Rain jacket
reviews.text: I have not been in an extended downpour yet, so can't say for sure.  I did buy it as my friend's held up better than my BD in a recent extended rain.  Nice features - only one available now with Napoleon pocket.  A bit crinkly.  Vanity sizing of late has led me to wear mediums for most things nowadays, but I needed to get a large for this jacket.
reviews.author: bobo

reviews.title: Bought twice cried thrice
reviews.text: First one was stolen but I didn't skip a beat in buying again. Fantastic rain jacket. Ultimate 2 layer solution when paired with a lightweight technical hoodie for wet cold windy days. Only option on the market with full side zippers which is especially helpful for proper fit on shorter torsos. Price is high but expertvoice helps.
reviews.author: Gram P

reviews.title: Perfect for PNW outdoors
reviews.text: This is the ultimate rain jacket! I put it to good use out in Washington state. It packs down well but more importantly it keeps rain out. It never gets saturated and always keeps me dry underneath. It does a decent job breathing and keeping me from overheating. The zippers are sealed and never leak! This one is a keeper and a must have if you're going to be out in the wet!
reviews.author: Tristan S

reviews.title: Great Jacket
reviews.text:
Great jacket, has kept me dry in everything from a drizzle to a solid downpour. Good fit and style. I would recommend this to friends. 
The hood is oversized for helmets, which I don’t need, so that would be the only complaint.
reviews.author: Ryan D

reviews.title: Great All Around
reviews.text:
The Foray is a great rain jacket. OR never disappoints, I’ve had this as a rain check for two years now and it’s great in warmer climates with lots of rain to moderately cold temps. I’ve worn this near the Arctic Circle to the coast of southern Alaska in the summer and it’s held up well. It’s flexible enough that it doesn’t present as a Hard Shell but light enough that if I need to layer I can. 

My main gripe is it’s a bit straight fitting, not athletic or tactical. So it tends to “swish” on me and annoys me slightly when hiking. This isn’t a huge issue as nothing catches to cause gear issues, but an odd feeling at first. 

Plenty of use on extreme terrain in the mountains. This can definitely take the punishment of a family man with kids in tow.
reviews.author: David D

reviews.title: Side zipper vents 100% awesome!
reviews.text: My all time favorite jacket.  The side zipper vents are a real game changer! They have made great upgrades in durability with the waterproofing fabric over the years.
reviews.author: SFlynn

reviews.title: Poor Performance When it Matters
reviews.text: I bought this jacket on Boxing Day 2025. Since then I’ve only used it in the city or in light rain and it has performed, which is to be expected. I work as a biologist and finally got caught in some heavy rain while out in the field near Attawapiskat. Very disappointed with the inadequate waterproofing on this shell. After the heavier rain had passed, I decided to throw on a layer under the shell as I was getting cold. When I removed the shell, my arms were soaked through to my elbows and my upper torso was also soaked through. This was the first real test for this jacket and for me, it failed immensely. My previous Columbia jacket was half the price, and still doesn’t soak through after 6 years of use in the field. And that jacket has been up close and personal with many sticks and branches during those years. Considering this shell is double the price, I am incredibly disappointed in its waterproof performance. I wonder if it has anything to do with the PFAS free nature of the jacket. Do yourself a favour and buy something else that will keep you dry when it matters most.
reviews.author: Jonny

reviews.title: Always  great products!
reviews.text: As always, OR makes everything top notch - good zippers on legs, seam is covered well.  Easy as heck to get on with boots and fits well without feeling stuffy.  Light rain so far - will update when I get drenched one of these trips.
reviews.author: Nathan J

reviews.title: Excellent pants
reviews.text: Excellent pants. Easy on/off, perform well. Easy to clean.
reviews.author: trevor e

reviews.title: Top notch rain pant
reviews.text: These pants have a nice feel against the skin (not clammy) as a result of the third layer and feel like they’ll be durable.   Love the 3/4 sealed zippers and the zipped back pocket.  I’m 6’2 and usually wear a 34x34 pant.  I bought medium regular length and they fit perfect with enough room in the waist to allow for a thick fabric underlayer.
reviews.author: Kyle F

reviews.text: Really nice rain pants. Pack down fairly small with a carabiner clip to hold ‘em on your bag. Honestly I didn’t notice much of a difference between their weight and my previous REI pants weight. They do seem to be a little bit larger than the size that is advertised. I’ve seen other peoples reviews and they mention the same thing, so though you may be fine with your normal size, I would try a size down. Overall, it’s a great quality product that should keep you dry from rain.
reviews.author: Colby J

reviews.title: sizing is completely off
reviews.text: Based on the sizing chart, I should be a S regular. But when it arrived, it looked like I was wearing parachute pants. I likely should be wearing one or two sizes smaller, but for whatever reason, Backcountry doesn't sell OR size XS.
reviews.author: Junshien L
reviews.familiarity: I returned this product before using it

reviews.title: Check sizing before buying
reviews.text: I went of the sizing chart, and the the large regular pants are too long, and the large top is a little too big as well. Try on in a store first if you can.
reviews.author: Ryan C

reviews.title: Same great material as the jacket and those leg zips!
reviews.text:
I recently purchased the Foray 3L pants, and I couldn't be more pleased with their performance. The standout feature for me has to be the full-length leg zippers, which make them incredibly easy to put on and take off, even over bulky footwear. This feature also provides excellent ventilation when needed.

The material is top-notch, identical to the jacket, which I also own and love. It’s exceptionally effective at repelling water, making it perfect for handling the sudden, intense downpours common in Florida. Despite its waterproof capabilities, the fabric feels comfortable and breathable, ensuring I stay dry without overheating.

Overall, the Foray 3L pants are a fantastic investment for anyone who needs reliable, high-quality rain protection. Highly recommended for tackling unpredictable weather with ease!
reviews.author: Lewis B

reviews.title: 32 waist, small the better fit
reviews.text:
Feather light and durable, rain proof yet vented
For hiking and low drag thru brush, small works for me (6' 180 lbs) over uninsulated pants.
That matches the profile of the medium jacket
If doing ballet on the rocks, medium pants will give more room
But for most other activities, it'd be too baggy
reviews.author: Metin L
reviews.familiarity: I've used it once or twice and have initial impressions

reviews.title: Tall is too tall
reviews.text: My issue isn't with the pants which are great,  BUT with the sizing chart - I am 6'3" and 36" waist and a large size works for me but I have an 34" inseam and the chart recommendation is to get a tall size however I think regular would have been much better.  The pant legs bunch up at the bottom when I have mid waterproof hiking shoes on.  The OR pro deal is great but unfortunately they don't allow exchanges or returns.  I would liked to have swapped this pair for a large regular.
reviews.author: Andy P

reviews.title: Great rain pants!
reviews.text: I've had several pairs of rain pants from other manufacturers over the years and these are the best so far.  They don't restrict my leg movements, don't leak, and are easy to get on and off.  The rise is high, so you have good overlap with your top and the waist drawstring seems sturdy enough, although I pair them with suspenders also.  Rain and wet brush are expected if you are outside much of the year here in the PNW, so you need some good rain pants.
reviews.author: Livetohike

reviews.title: Definitely Keeps You Dry
reviews.text: I purchased this Aspire 3L rain jacket for a recent 10 day trip to Alaska as my previous rain jacket (not OR brand) was 10 years old and NOT rain resistant anymore.  The weather for the trip was more or less misty/foggy with some moderate rain at times and the temperatures were low 50's.  The jacket, layered with a puffy jacket, was very comfortable and kept me dry.  There is a previous review where a person stated the jacket "pockmarked" when it got wet.  Yes this jacket did that too BUT the "pockmarks" did not stay as it rained and they also disappeared when the jacket dried.  We did several hikes with the jacket on with just a t-shirt underneath and got a tad warm but cooled down fairly quickly upon opening the pit zips.  I appreciate the ability to unzip the sides of the jacket for this purpose but also unzip the jacket from the bottom sides as well, should I need to access pockets and what have you.  Now the not so good....During our trip I wore a small Camelbak Pak for carrying small things like gloves, hat, etc and I noticed that the pack has actually chaffed the jacket and caused some unsightly pilling and this is in just the first week of owning the jacket.  Now I don't expect to have to wear this jacket every time I hike, but I do worry that over time, wearing a pack with this jacket will eventually wear holes in the material.  I guess I expected better quality in this aspect. (Excuse the color variation in the photos as this is from the camera and lighting)  Hopefully OR can come up with some type of fix for their materials in the future.  Overall, I love this jacket as it was comfortable, kept me dry in all rain conditions and packs well when not needed.
reviews.author: BGTraveller

reviews.title: Perfect for rainy hikes
reviews.text: If I didn’t have this jacket, I would’ve been miserable on vacation. It rained almost every day, but I was dry the whole time. The hood is kind of big for me as is, so I folded it back and the problem was solved. It was perfect when I wore my hair up. I never overheated even though I was doing hours long hikes and was very easy to clean all the mud off. The pockets are spacious and the zippers are really good quality, so I didn’t need to bother with any other bags most of the time. It also fit easily into a small backpack when I wasn’t using it. It quickly became my favorite jacket.
reviews.author: Gavvy

reviews.text: I’ve always told people Outdoor Research rain jackets are the biggest bang for your buck. They’re great pieces.
reviews.author: Andrew C

reviews.title: Well made but not your average XL
reviews.text: Cut too small and with a shorter back than most other comparable rain coats. Fits much different than an XL Patagonia- also- zero returns allowed.
reviews.author: Kevin R

reviews.title: Great jacket.  Pretty color, too!
reviews.text: I’ve only owned it for a few weeks, but I did get outside in the rain on a weeklong hike.  It was great as an extra wind-breaking layer when it wasn’t raining, too..  This is my second Aspire jacket.  I bought it the first time in 2015 for the side zips and pit zips and general performance.   The major upgrade was the wrists.  They were previously elastic and Velcro.  Hated them.  The new model dropped the elastic, so you can wear them looser when you want to and Velcro them tight as well.  Much better!!  This one seems to fit better all around, and the color Winterberry is gorgeous.  It’s great on and off the trail.  I’m 5’4” and 135 lbs, ordered a small.

reviews.text: Comfortable and true to size. Fairy light and easy to pack in overnight bags

reviews.text: I’ve tested this jacket in the rainiest of commute and work days hip deep in muddy wetlands, along with snow/wind skiing. It exceeds all expectations for cutting wind and keeping dry while still being stylish. Great value! Love the color options too.
reviews.author: ItsJ

reviews.title: Works as expected!
reviews.text:
Haven't had the chance to wear in the rain yet, but I stayed super dry in a wet snowfall yesterday! The hood is a little larger than I like, but it'll be great for helmets, and it stayed out of my face and kept its form pretty well.
The jacket seems to run a little big. I'm typically a women's large, but I've got a lot of extra room, even when wearing a down jacket beneath. Love the winterberry color!
reviews.author: Cheyenne D

reviews.title: Not waterproof!
reviews.text: I've had this jacket for a little less than two years now so I've been able to really test it. The main activity I use this for is skiing: works great as a shell because it's lightweight and you can zipper down the sides when you get warm. HOWEVER, this jacket DOES NOT hold up to downpours or even light rain. If you need a jacket to quickly run outside and do something for less than 20 minutes, this jacket is fine. But if you are backpacking or need to be outside for some time and it's raining or snowing, this jacket will soak through. I have even waterproofed it recently and still no luck (that might be saying more to the waterproofing product as well). Please don't get this jacket if you actually need one for being outside in the rain-your money is best spent elsewhere.

reviews.title: Well-made, waterproof, excellent pockets

reviews.title: Hard wearing and great Handling.
reviews.text: For most, we don?t think of a 9.2mm rope as hard wearing. However, I?m genuinely impressed in how well the Volta has held up after nearly a year of use. I initially purchased it for long multipitch ice and rock routes where I didn?t want dental floss, but also didn?t want to lug up a 10mm rope that would weigh as much as a ship anchor after a day of climbing on wet snow and ice. The 9.2 Volta struck a nice balance between weight, handling, and durability. It has survived terrain belays, sharp choss, sea cliff edges and dozens of late night dripping wet ice. I highly recommend this rope and I can assure you you don?t need to baby it. Petzl really outdid themselves with this rope

reviews.title: Strong light; USB-C; easy to control
reviews.text: My title says it:  certainly enough light for my purposes or relative to comparable headlamps.  I really appreciate they have moved beyond USB-B -- one less cable to carry, and not many others carry "B" if yours going missing; and for a set of buttons, it's pretty comprehensible.

reviews.title: No looking switch
reviews.text: The Petzl Swift RL headlamp is a good headlamp if you are looking for brightness. The 1100 lumens is great to have for a headlamp. But if you have this down in your pack there is a possibility that the power button could be turned on and that could cause the battery run down.  On the Petzl Swift RL 900 lumens it has locking switch so the battery will not run down when in your pack. This way the Petzl 1100 is a good headlamp not a great headlamp.
reviews.author: Josh

reviews.title: Petzl 1200 Lumen Light
reviews.text:
I have used Petzl headlights for many years.  I exchanged the Petzl 1100 lumen headlight I had just purchased online for the 1200 when I found out that the 1100 was discontinued in a phone call with a Petzl Rep.  The 1100 was an excellent light, but would not rotate down enough to allow me to see through my bifocals.  This is a significant issue for anyone over the age of 45.  The new 1200 lumen light  rotates 360 degrees vertically and is lighter than the 1100.  Otherwise, the same features ( reactive  and constant lighting, red light, and a lock feature) are unchanged.  I will use it for hiking, camping, night mountain bike rides, and nighttime paddle boarding.
I am very pleased with the light and the excellent help I received from the staff in the BC store.  
 I
reviews.author: Utah Bob

reviews.title: Terrible Feature
reviews.text:
Terrible idea for anything serious like climbing. Petzl’s Reactive Lighting is the worst feature to put on a professional headlamp. It barely saves any battery—maybe a few minutes—yet it constantly changes brightness, which is the last thing you want on a climb when you need consistent, predictable light.

To test it, we set the lamp to high in our restroom and shut the door. In one minute, the brightness changed nineteen times—without anyone touching it or moving in the room.

That feature doesn’t make the headlamp better. It just makes it more expensive. Choose wiser.

reviews.author: Royness

reviews.title: Excellent fit and feel
reviews.text:
It is hard to find the perfect down jacket. I know because I bought 3 or 4 different ones before settling on this one. I am a big Outdoor Research guy and my go-to option in this price range was the Helium. I really liked the features and tougher material on that jacket but the fit was just so odd for me. The medium fit perfect from the torso up but the waist was squeezing me when zipped and was very short. The large was gigantic on me. Tried some Mountain Hardwear - medium fit too loose and boxy and the large was a trash sack on me. 
Then I got to this Rab! The cut and fit of these is so well thought out. I actually could not decide between the medium or large because they both fit decently and would both work in different situations (layers under or over). I settled on the medium and it is just perfect. It is every-so slightly tight in the armpit/shoulder area which is further motivation to lose the excess 15 pounds I've been carrying on me for the last couple of years. The length is what makes this stand out for me. It fits snug in the torso but also has a slight tail that is sure to keep your waist and belly covered when reaching or bending over. I also love the stitching layout for the neck area when it is zipped all the way. 
As far as performance goes, I have taken it out for a couple of hikes and a couple of bike rides in drizzly/misting conditions at around 40 degrees. It is no surprise that it is plenty warm for 40 degree weather, but it also stands up well to the wet and even moving quickly on a bike on an open road the wind doesn't make it through to the skin at all. About 80% of the jacket has shed the moisture and only a few spots where water hung on soaked through, but I certainly never felt like the insulation was losing any of its performance. 
The stuff sack is a little weird when everything else on the market can stuff into a pocket, but I actually really like it because the shape it stuffs into is nicer than the usual pocket-shaped thing. I just keep it in the chest pocket so its out of the way of my hands and it isn't even noticeable because the stuff sack material is so light and soft. 
My final note is the feel of the jacket. Compared to the other brands I have tried, I would say this has an extra level of "plushness" to it. The outer and inner material is just really soft and less stiff or rigid than some down jackets.
reviews.author: Collin T
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Light weight W/style!

reviews.title: The Rab Microlight Alpine Jacket
reviews.text:
The Rab Microlight Alpine Jacket hits that rare sweet spot between true warmth and remarkable lightness. 
For a 700‑fill down jacket, it feels almost weightless when you put it on—easy to pack, easy to layer, and never bulky. Despite that low weight, the warmth-to-weight ratio is excellent. It traps heat quickly, cuts wind effectively, and stays comfortable across a wide range of shoulder‑season and winter conditions.

The fit is athletic without being restrictive, and the recycled down insulation lofts beautifully.
Whether I'm walking around town, hiking in cold weather, or using it as a midlayer under a shell, the Microlight Alpine delivers reliable warmth without ever feeling heavy.

If you want a jacket that’s light enough to forget you’re wearing it but warm enough to trust on cold days, this one nails it.

reviews.title: Lightweight but Mountain Ready
reviews.text:
I wore the Rab Microlight Alpine Jacket on the Mardi Himal Trail, and it completely exceeded my expectations. It’s incredibly lightweight, but when incorporated into a proper layering system, it kept me impressively warm and dry.

We hiked for six hours at a time, climbing and descending in changing conditions, and this jacket never retained moisture. While others were wearing thick, heavy down coats that became soaked with sweat and took forever to dry, my Microlight stayed breathable and comfortable. When they peeled their layers off, they were damp. I was dry.

It was so effective at retaining warmth that I often had to remove layers because I was getting too warm — which is exactly what you want in performance gear. And because it’s so thin and compressible, packing it away was effortless.

I hadn’t heard of Rab before this trip, but after researching and choosing this jacket, I’m genuinely impressed. It kept me dry, warm, and comfortable the entire trek. A fantastic piece of gear I would absolutely recommend for serious mountain conditions.

It also gets me through a majority of the winter and I actually wear it skiing with a rain jacket on top of it and I'm super comfortable. Also RAB's customer service is amazing! I ripped the pocket of the first jacket (totally my fault) and they patched and sewed it by hand and send it back to me for only $40. I've tested a lot gear in the last 20 years and I would not think twice about this jacket. It's honestly the best down jacket I've ever owned.

reviews.title: Road and Trail Slayer!
reviews.text:
After 20 miles, the Aero Glide 4 GRVL has exceeded my expectations. It feels smooth and responsive on pavement, then transitions effortlessly onto gravel roads and mellow singletrack without skipping a beat.

The cushioning is plush without feeling unstable, the fit is secure with plenty of comfort for longer miles, and the outsole provides dependable grip on mixed terrain. This is the kind of shoe you can lace up without worrying where your run will take you.

I’m holding back the fifth star until I’ve logged more miles and can evaluate long-term durability, but after 20 miles, I’d confidently recommend the Aero Glide 4 GRVL to anyone looking for a true road-to-trail shoe. This is my favorite shoe lately!

The shoe is extremely comfortable on gravel and road, but my favourite thing is how they perform when running downhill, this is where other shoes usually fail me, but felt like I could run down hill all day. The cushioning is incredible here.
They feel rather warm, however I did purchase the all black, worn with black socks (just my style). So perhaps go for lighter colour if wearing in hot weather.

reviews.title: My New Favourite Trail Shoe
reviews.text:
(This review was collected as part of a promotion.) After a month in the Aero Glide 4 GRVL, I can confidently say this shoe has earned a permanent spot in my rotation. Whether I’m cruising gravel roads, running dirt trails, or tackling technical sections, it feels right at home on every surface.

I already loved the Aero Glide 3 for road and treadmill miles, but the Aero Glide 4 GRVL takes that same lightweight, cushioned comfort and adds versatility for off-road adventures. It’s comfortable enough for long easy miles but still feels stable and capable when the trails get more challenging.

I never thought I’d say this, but I’m officially sold on the Quicklace system too. I wasn’t a fan in previous models, but this setup feels secure and effortless.

Light, cushioned, comfortable, and incredibly versatile — if you’re into gravel roads, mixed terrain, or trail running, this shoe is the real deal.

reviews.title: Max Versatility and Cushioning
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After using the Aero Glide 4 GRVL on a variety of different terrains including road, light to moderate dirt & grass trails and at the beach, I can say these are very versatile. They have a “cloud-like” cushion across mediums, are lightweight and have a responsive feel without being bulky. 

The lacing system is easy to get use to and very convenient - tighten and tuck.  

It only happen a a few times but one thing I did notice while walking in a neighborhood is that the inside arch area had a bit of side to side roll since it is narrower.  

Overall the cushion and surface to surface transitions are so seamless and adaptable that this is easily a daily wearer and ready to go if you decide at the last minute to blaze a trail.  

Highly recommend picking up a pair.

p.s. - they also look great!

reviews.title: Max Versatility and Cushioning
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After using the Aero Glide 4 GRVL on a variety of different terrains including road, light to moderate dirt & grass trails and at the beach, I can say these are very versatile. They have a “cloud-like” cushion across mediums, are lightweight and have a responsive feel without feeling bulky. 

The lacing system is easy to get use to and very convenient - tighten and tuck.  

It only happen a a few times but one thing I did notice while walking in a neighborhood is that the inside arch area had a bit of side to side roll since it is narrower.  

Overall the cushion and surface to surface transitions are so seamless and adaptable that this is easily a daily wearer and ready to go if you decide at the last minute to blaze a trail.  

Highly recommend picking up a pair.

p.s. - they also look great!
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.title: Awesome shoes for Trail/Beach running
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I was impressed with these shoes right out of the box. Light weight, true to size, with a cool lacing system. These shoes have great energy return with every stride, while still being stable. Most running shoes with a tall stack lack stability to push your speed, but not these. Also, the design is great for preventing dirt and sand from getting into the shoe with a trade-off being breathability. After about 25miles or so, I don't really notice any wear, even the tread is holding up. I'll definitely be shopping Salomon again for my footwear needs.

reviews.title: Awesome shoes
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] These running shoes are fantastic. They fit perfectly, and the adjustable laces make it easy to get a secure, customized feel. I’ve used them on sugar sand, gravel, dirt trails, and pavement, and they’ve performed great on every surface. They’re incredibly comfortable and lightweight, even on longer runs. I highly recommend them to anyone looking for a versatile, reliable running shoe.

reviews.title: Great support and great cushioning.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] These shoes look great! Very comfortable and maximum cushioning yet still supportive while jogging a mixed terrain hiking trail. Like my other Salomon shoes, these have a quick lacing system that holds tight and is quick to put on and take off. At first I was worried about having enough stability because of how much cushion these have but somehow these shoes provided great lateral support while taking them out for a jog on a moderate hiking trail. Love these shoes so far!
reviews.author: Jason27

reviews.title: The only shoe I reach for
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After logging approximately 60 miles in the Salomon Aero Glide 4 GRVL, I’ve come away impressed by its versatility and overall performance across multiple surfaces.
Fit & Comfort
The shoe fits true to size and strikes an excellent balance for runners with slightly wider feet. While not marketed as a wide shoe, it provides enough room to remain comfortable even as feet expand during longer runs. The toe box volume is particularly well-executed—spacious without being loose—eliminating any issues with rubbing or bunching.
Midsole Performance
The Optifoam 2 midsole delivers a soft, cushioned ride while maintaining a stable and responsive feel. This combination makes the shoe especially well-suited for longer distances, helping to reduce fatigue in both legs and feet.
Upper & Lockdown
The upper material wraps the foot in a sock-like fit that feels breathable, lightweight, and secure. The gusseted tongue adds to the overall comfort and stays in place throughout runs, while providing just the right amount of padding. The lacing system is equally effective, offering a strong lockdown without creating pressure points or discomfort across the top of the foot.
Outsole & Versatility
Equipped with a durable Contagrip outsole, the shoe performs reliably across road, gravel, and light trail conditions. After 60 miles of varied use, traction and durability remain strong, reinforcing its all-terrain capability.
Minor Drawback
If there’s one improvement to be made, it would be the addition of a heel pull tab or back strap to make putting the shoe on easier.
Overall Impression
The Salomon Aero Glide 4 GRVL stands out as a highly versatile and capable running shoe. Whether you’re transitioning between road and gravel or mixing in light trails, it handles each environment with ease while maintaining comfort and performance over longer distances.

reviews.author: m2fresh

reviews.title: Surprisingly rugged
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] On first look and feel, these shoes are super lightweight and squishy. The interior fabric and tongue is nice and flexible and I didn't feel any pressure points when walking or running. The new quicklace system took an extra second to figure out but is intuitive. I had issues with the laces loosening on the first run, but after a dusting of dirt they are staying in place well. Once running, they are surprisingly rugged for how light they are! They faired very well on dry and wet gravel running conditions, and even dry/rocky more technical trails. A more technical trail under rainy conditions caused mud to get stuck in the bottom gap of cushion but I popped it out with a stick and kept going. Overall, these are really comfortable shoes for gravel and dryer trail conditions. I would like to see a lower drop in the future but will keep wearing them as is.
reviews.author: Melissa

reviews.title: Awesome Running Shoes with the BEST Sole
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I previously bought 3 pairs of the Aero Glide 3 GRVL and now the Aero Glide 4 GRVL. I've been wearing these shoes for road running and track work for about the past month. (I wore the Aero Glide 3 on some light trail runs and they were as awesome as you'd expect from Salomon.) It has the same sole as the Aero Glide 3 but it has made a significant improvement with the toe box. The toebox on this shoe is nice and roomy (but not uncomfortably big) and not at all tapered like the Aero Glide 3 GRVL was. This shoe is also back to having the Quicklace system. I actually did not mind having regular laces on the Aero Glide 3 but you can get a very precise fit (that doesn't budge) with the Quicklace system. One change I found puzzling is that the lace just past the toggle is physically attached to the top of the tongue. I find this awkward because I can't open up the laces as wide as possible when putting on the shoes. I've debated snipping the piece of black fabric to free the laces but it does not detract from the shoe (it's more of a minor inconvenience). But the best part of these shoes is the sole. Salomon describes it as foam but to me it feels like running on ridiculously bouncy rubber, in the best possible way. They are very stable shoes but you do feel the energy return. My middle-aged knees appreciate the cushion and the bounce. SALOMON: please continue to release new versions of this shoe like you do for Speedcross and XA Pro 3D!
reviews.author: Erika

reviews.title: Best hybrid shoe on the market!
reviews.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve been a dedicated trail runner and Salomon loyalist for about 8 years now, racing competitively in 50K to 100-mile mountain events. I picked up the Aero Blaze Gravel last year as a workout shoe for gravel threshold/VO2 sessions and the occasional track workout (I’ve always been hesitant to fully switch to a road shoe). They were solid, but these are on a completely different level.

The foam feels incredibly supportive with just the right amount of bounce. I feel noticeably faster and stronger in them, especially during workouts. At first I thought they were a super shoe!! I’ve used them for road runs, gravel sessions, and long runs up to 3 hours, and they’ve handled everything really well.

Where I live, runs are rarely just road or just trail. It’s usually a mix of pavement, gravel, and sometimes wet or messy conditions. These are perfect for that. They strike a great balance between performance and versatility.

Fit is spot on, grip is great, and the quicklace system feels secure and premium. The upper material is high quality, and overall, the shoe just looks great too.

Only minor note: on chunkier gravel, small rocks can occasionally get caught in the midsole, but it’s rare and hasn’t been a real issue. Overall, this feels like a major upgrade; easily one of my favorite non-trail shoes I’ve run in.

reviews.title: Comfort, Speed, and Grip in One Package
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Salomon Aero Glide 4 delivers a lightweight, responsive ride with excellent cushioning and support. The fit is true to size with generous internal volume, allowing room for thicker cushioned socks without sacrificing lockdown. A breathable upper and well‑designed lacing system provide comfort and security, while the slightly pointy, propulsive toe geometry promotes efficient toe‑off and speed. The bouncy midsole offers strong energy return, and the full rubber‑covered outsole protects the foam while delivering reliable grip across multiple terrains. Reflective details enhance visibility for low‑light runs, making this a versatile and confidence‑inspiring daily trainer.

These are also super lightweight, I've compered them to my old road shoes Phantasm 2's and these are so much lighter, while also having a great level of cushioning and spring so they are great for runs of all length and pace. I've done recovery runs, base runs and sprint sessions in them, Perfect for training. 

My only concern is over durability, I think I will be lucky to get 500km out of these shoes, I would prefer to get 600+, but I suspect the main sole will wear incredibly quickly once the tougher rubber outer is worn through, I'm currently approaching the halfway mark with mine now, I do have a very specific wear pattern on my shoes though so it may just be me and my odd running gait.

My only complaint is the lack of creative colorways (so far). I loved my Aero Glide 3 proto pack!

reviews.title: Exceeded my expectations
reviews.text: I am not a "professional" runner by any means and I usually dread the moments before, during, and after runs.  I am getting to the age where I am looking to stay fit and introduce more cardio activities into my workouts so here we are.  I have previously been using an older pair of running shoes which always left my knees hurting after short runs (3-4 miles).  The Aero Glide 4's are the first pair of running shoes I have owned with the insane amount of cushion on the sole.  To be honest I have always thought these types of shoes looked stupid and were unnecessary.  That being said, I am now a believer in their benefit.....though I still think the massive sole looks stupid.  I have only put about 20-30 miles on these bad boys however I noticed a big different in how I feel during and after my runs.  My legs, specifically knees, feel fresh and not abused after 5k runs.  I wouldn't say I'm excited to go running however I do find it more enjoyable with these shoes.  We will see how they hold up over time however I can't see myself going back to "normal shoes" so I will just buy another pair when needed.

reviews.title: Sizing changes from last model
reviews.text: I ordered the same size I wore in the previous model, 46.5 with 47 street shoe. The old model fit me perfectly and I loved them despite the blue dye and the thinner rubber so I wanted to try with the new model since I’m wearing into the midsole. The rubber is thicker, 4mm vs 3.5mm, so they will last longer but the fit and feel is very different. Almost like a different shoe. I would return them for another half size down, 46, if I hadn’t thrown the box away already. They felt ok at home but immediately became loose outside on a 70 degree day. After comparing these side by side with last years well broken-in shoe, these new ones are at least a half size bigger at the same size. The toe box feels more roomy and the fit in the heel is pretty loose. The soles feel stiffer than the previous. Definitely reduces some sensitivity from the last model with the thicker rubber too but it’s a trade off. I’m really hoping the leather will shrink after some handwashing and wear so the fit will improve because I like the added durability and no blue feet. Decent for volume and multipitch at a half size down from street but I’d want to go at least a full size down from street for redpointing.

- Roomy toe box = comfortable for all day wear

reviews.title: My go-to shoe
reviews.text: I've owned eight pairs of scarpa veloce, it suits me very well as a light, sensitive climber. I don't think there's a better shoe for slab. For overhang some don't appreciate the lack of toe rubber and oversized heel. For me it's not really a problem. Pair this with a VSR and you we'll have virtually any indoor bouldering terrain covered. They last a long time compared to how soft they are, the main replacement reason is always smell and eventually holes in the toe.

reviews.familiarity: I've put it through the wringer

reviews.title: Soft shoes
reviews.text:
Like others have already written, these shoes are soft and comfy.  That's the only pro for me.

I have only climbed for a couple of years, and gyms only, so perhaps I need the reassurance of a stiffer shoe on smaller foot chips?  I am def not a fan of how soft they are.

I have only worn the Arpia, Miura, Skwama, and these.  I wear street shoe size.

I plan to keep these as my "backup" shoes
reviews.author: D L45
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Ready For Action Right Out Of The Box
reviews.text: I?ve been climbing for 46+ years. I?ve owned EBs, RRs, PAs, & my first pair of sticky rubber shoes were Boreal Fires bought from Ray in Joshua Tree in 1984. I bought these specifically for gym climbing along with a pair of La Sportiva Skwama?s. I bought these because I have a wide (EE) forefoot and these shoes are known to have a wide forefoot. I bought my street shoe size. They were snug out of the box but after 10 minutes of climbing, they molded to my feet and are spectacularly comfortable while climbing (I do yank them immediately off after I finish a pitch).  I find myself using these more than the Skwamas because there is no break-in period required and the sole is more sensitive (but likely not as good edging). They climb well right out of the box. The rubber seams pretty soft (and sticky!) so I don?t know how they will wear. I try to hit the gym for two 3+ hour sessions twice a week, so if I?m allowed, I?ll write a postscript to this review on how they are wearing and performing.  Beware that if you have a narrow foot these shoes may have to be sized differently or may not work for you - there may be too much volume in the shoe for your foot.
reviews.author: Alfred T
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Buy them, perfect bouldering shoe
reviews.text:
I've never written an online review before but I would love for Scarpa to make this shoe until the end of time. I've been climbing for a decade (5.13/v9) and this is the most comfortable shoe i've ever worn and still basically has a good performance as top end shoes like the Solution or Instinct.  It's very soft, probably the softest I've worn, but can still edge , especially on overhangs. The heel is near perfect. The strap doesn't break. The rubber is Scarpa house made, but I think performs nearly as well as XS Grip 2 inside and out and lasts significantly longer. Backcountry often has the shoes for sale for $104! A deal that cannot be beat. 

Your feet wont hurt, performance is top tier. Thats it. Actually, thats not it...the design is very aesthetic as well, they look sleek, simple and well made.  Buy them so Scarpa keeps making them and we can all wear them for forever.

I wear a 40.5 in Solutions, and a 41.5 in other Scarpas and the Veloce is PERFECT at 41 (M9to 9.5 street shoe). Both regular and LV (or women's whatever they call them) of this shoe are the same in my experience, so choose the color for you.

Also, I didn't get anything for this review, but Backcountry does have great customer service and shipping. Maybe send me a special treat Backcountry if this review makes you beaucoups of $$$?

reviews.text: Great helmets got 3 for holidays and the zipper for headphones is awesome
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: High quality lid with great features.
reviews.text: This was a worthwhile upgrade.  I had been using a Bern multisport helmet with a winter liner for snowboarding, and while it worked great with sunglasses and I liked the ability to run it with or without the winter liner, it never fit right with goggles.  The Vantage pairs perfectly with goggles.  The build quality is super nice, the venting is plentiful and very adjustable, and the magnetic clasp is brilliant.  The only surprise was that it actually fits a bit smaller than the sizing would indicate.  It fits me fine, but I'm close to the limit of having the adjuster all the way open, yet my head circumference is at the lower end of the stated range.  If you are closer to the top end of the size range, or want clearance for a thicker balaclava, it might b e worth sizing up.
reviews.author: Ruben A
reviews.familiarity: I've used it several times

reviews.title: Excellent quality
reviews.text: As a long time wearer of a Smith Variance helmet, this Smith Vantage has excellent, even better, quality, venting, and impact protection with MIPS and Koroyd. I personally don't like the added material around the back of the neck with the BOA system integrated into it as it's bulky and makes adjustment trickier with gloved fingers. I've found the extra thickness and firmness of the ear pads make pushing integrated helmet speaker controls more difficult and clumsy to press. It would be nice to see less bulk in the ears and boa system and some brighter colours offered in the next design.
reviews.author: Michael R.

reviews.title: Amazing Updates
reviews.text: I had the original Vantage Helmet that protected my head after being clipped by someone resulting in a fall. So, didn't hesitate to get a new one. Ordered my original size medium. Vantage 2 fits great. It is lighter, but provides for more protection via the Koroyd technology. Seems to let less air escape by the ear pads which is great. Does take getting use to with the new boa system. Like others mentioned, you do need to tighten the helmet w/o gloves. Hopefully, Smith's next update will provide for a large dial. Other than that, it is a great helmet.

reviews.title: LOVE IT!
reviews.text: Had a original Vantage helmet that honest might have saved my life, so when I went for a new one I knew I wanted to go with Smith!   The new helmet is somehow even nicer than the old one!  Love the new vents and is the most comfortable helmet i have ever owned!
reviews.author: Joe G

reviews.title: helmet back too low on nape of  neck
reviews.text: I had the first gen Vantage Mips which I was happy with, it fit ok  but I needed a size large in it where I am a size Medium in Giro helmets.  I went to a Giro Spherical Mips hemet from the 1st gen Vantage Mips. I decided to give Smith another try now that Smith came out with a new 2nd gen Vantage Mips . I am very disappointed in the fit of the new helmet, the soft back part that houses the size dial comes down too low down he nape of my neck putting uncomfortable pressure on the nape of my neck. That was a common problem I encountered when buying my first ski helmet in the mid '00's. I'm disappointed that the new design doesn't work for me. Others here cited the same trouble yet for whatever reason have had their reviews flagged. As to the review complaining about exposed fit tension cords, that is very fixable by removing and repositioning the inside soft black liner which is attached to the helmet via velcro.
reviews.author: marc P
reviews.familiarity: I returned this product before using it

reviews.author: brett

reviews.title: Sadly a step down from the original
reviews.text: Unfortunately, Smith took some bad design cues from the Nexus in designing the Vantage 2, making it a significant step down in comfort from the original Vantage. The head pad does not go far enough down to cover the adjustment straps. As a result, the adjustment straps end up on the inside of your upper ear, cutting right into the skin, just like the Nexus. It’s a very strange design choice considering you only have to put the helmet on to realize the problem. If you end up using one of these get a thin beanie or a balaclava to wear under the helmet. Otherwise it will hurt very quickly. The original vantage provides a much better fit but lacks the fidlock, which is a nice addition.

reviews.title: Nothing but good things to say about this jacket

It performed well on the backpacking trip, kept me dry and comfortable on the 10-mile days as well as the 6-mile days. It's lightweight, making it easy to wear casually or while exercising. It's also a great windbreaker, or even just a lightweight layer. It's easily my most versatile jacket. I got the white and it is so fun and cute, I love wearing it.

reviews.text: I am 5'0" and around 105lbs. After reading reviews, I decided to size down to an XS and overall it's a good fit. I still have room for a warmer layer underneath if warranted. reviews.title: So unbelievably content with this purchase!
reviews.text: So i purchased this jacket based on my significant other's recommendation since we're hiking up Mt. Herard out in Colorado in a few weeks. Needless to say, i'm so happy i bought this ! I'm 5'1 and weigh 110lbs, chest size 32c. i purchased an XS. I was so afraid this jacket was going to be extremely fitted but once it arrived i could immediately tell it wasn't going to be that way at all. i'm petite so it's a tad roomy but i'm fine with that bc now i definitely have the option to layer it when the cooler weather hits but the jacket by itself is still so comfortable and fits so nicely and is so lightweight. The only "dislike" would be the arm length but i have pretty short arms so this tends to be the case with a lot of jackets.... Fortunately the velcro at the wrists of the sleeves fixes that length issue entirely ! (: i also took that custom sizing test to see what i would be and it told me i should get a Small... which would've been massive on me. Glad i listened to my gut and went with the XS ! But overall i highly recommend this product if you want something that's functional/practical for almost anywhere except the extreme cold.

reviews.title: I recommend this jacket to everyone.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First and foremost, the Nuptse delivers exceptional warmth without compromising on comfort. The 700-fill goose down insulation provides superb insulation, keeping you cozy even in the harshest winter conditions. Whether you're braving icy winds on the slopes or navigating city streets in freezing temperatures, the nuptse has you covered. Beyond its warmth, the nuptse boasts a sleek and timeless design that effortlessly transitions from the mountains to the streets. The boxy silhouette and oversized baffles not only add a touch of urban flair but also enhance the jacket's insulation by minimizing heat loss. Available in a variety of colors, there's a nuptse to suit every style preference. Functionality is also a hallmark of the nuptse. Featuring a durable nylon shell with a water-repellent finish, this jacket offers protection against light rain and snow showers. The adjustable hood provides additional coverage when needed, while the zippered hand pockets offer convenient storage for essentials. One of the standout features of the nuptse is its versatility. Whether worn as a standalone piece or layered under a shell for added protection, this jacket adapts to changing conditions with ease. From chilly autumn hikes to frigid winter commutes, the nuptse proves its worth time and time again.

reviews.title: Has a major design flaw.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I am 5'6" or 5'7" and 125lbs. I have multiple North Face jackets. I am a North Face small. At first, the Nuptse jacket seemed like the perfect jacket. Small was the correct size as are all my other jackets. The arm length was correct. The width was just enough to allow to me layer on something else. If I had a medium, I would be swimming in my jacket. The jacket was lightweight, warm, had a packable hood, and I could pack the whole jacket into the pocket. Then, I raised my arm. My arm was only raised to shoulder height and the jacket pulled up above my waist. Am I never supposed to move my arms? I can never shovel snow. Every time I move my arms, I will have 20 degree F wind blowing on my stomach. If I raise my arms all the way up, the jacket exposes my stomach even more. The jacket in neutral position just barely covers my waist. This seems like a major design flaw. I tried on my other North Face jackets and other brand jackets and this is not a problem. I was aware that the Nuptse was "short" because I saw reviews on the internet, but this is a joke. I am shocked that this jacket has such high reviews with such a massive design flaw. If there were another version of the Nuptse that were longer (or just normal sized like every other North Face jacket), I would buy the jacket again.

reviews.title: Yes Yes Yes. But it could be better.
reviews.text: The jacket lives up to all the rage. It's soft and puffy. Being a stand up collar, it does a good job and laying flat which was a big deal for me (short necked). It ended up being warmer than I was expecting. When I'm indoors where it's already warm I have to take it off because I feel my back overheating. The fit from the chest down was amazing too. Normally I have problems with TNF tops because the product gets tight on my hips. Sizing up results in it being too big everywhere else. This is a great fit which is customizable with the bands on the waistline. The jacket lives up to everything you expect it to. But if TNF were to make a bigger badder brother I'd like to see one with a built in hood. The zip out hood didn't cut it for the cold weather and snow where I am. Another alternative to adjusting the wrists would be nice as well. If not then at least more room to make it tighter. I don't have the option to adjust it to how tight I need it so it's loose (though still visually appealing). Finally the zippers. I don't have any problems with it getting stuck, but it would be great if it had a double zipper. Being that a newer version would be more "premium", an upgrade on the zipper pulls wouldn't be a bad idea either. All in all the nuptse is a great jacket. Definately considering getting another.

reviews.title: A long time fan of the Nuptse since 1997.
reviews.text: This is the "go to" jacket whenever I don't know what to wear for a moment. Since I bought my first Nuptse in 1997, I was HOOKED. These jackets are soooo comfortable and will warm you nicely, have a relaxed, wide fit and the Nuptse does not restrict your movements in ANY way. Just perfect! I really HATE those slim-fit thingies. Of course I have down jackets from a wide variety of other manufacturers after more than 20 years, but none comes close to the all-round versatility of the (classic, Retro) Nuptse. The only down side I can find: it is not waterproof. In case you expect rain to fall: choose another jacket. Do yourself a favor and buy the Gotham for those occasions :-)

reviews.title: NYC Film Crew MVP
reviews.text: I tried six coats from various big outdoors brands, including two others from TNF, before finally finding and falling for this one. I work in film and TV in New York, so am often outside for 14+ hours no matter the weather, and was tired of trying to fit tons of layers beneath my Carhartt and still freezing most of the time. The Nuptse is popular with the NYC production crowd; the short length makes it convenient for wearing a walkie or when you need to access your waist bag, etc. I'm petite (5'1, 107 lbs, 32B) with hips and love the boxy coat trend-my body type is one not flattered by the popular long, thin, form-fitting parka look. That being said, most "oversized" or "relaxed fit" coats are way too big on me drafty to the point where they just aren't warm, but not the Nuptse-the Velcro adjustable wrist cuffs and drawstring waist make it easy to trap heat while maintaining the whole puffy look. I tried an on XS and found it uncomfortably snug over the sweatshirt I was wearing, so I ordered a Small because I wanted room for hoodies and jackets beneath, and it fits perfectly, hits right at my hips. It is SO COMFORTABLE. Like wearing a cloud pillow hug. I'm able to wear it in ~35°F with just long a sleeved t-shirt, which was my goal, and layering a mid-weight fleece and a thermal top beneath works well when the temp drops below that. It does pretty well with wind. I wouldn't wear it without a shell in the rain, and even heavy snow is questionable, but I have a waterproof poncho to throw on top in inclement weather. Pockets are super warm; love the stand-up collar when the hood is stuffed inside. The shell is VERY thin and feels fragile, prone to tearing, so I'm careful not to snag it and don't think this jacket would be ideal for hiking/the woods/any sort of sharp or rough environment, but it's perfect for urban use. I always get compliments on the Nuptse because it's such a classic, funky style while also being super warm and practical. I want it in every color!

reviews.title: 3 month update :(
reviews.text: Purchased 3 months ago to be prepared for winter season. I wrote a review describing issues with color discrepancies ( order an all Black shell, get one that's Grey and black. I decided to compromise over the color and keep the product. Went to wash it for the first time the other day and while checking the pockets, I noticed that the seam had split open and the pocket was falling apart. I contacted Customer Service and though the process for warranty returns is to send it back to Quebec so they can decide to repair or replace the item, Simon in customer service suggested that I send in some pics to the Warranty department and maybe they will replace the product and accept the original one back later so Im not without a jacket while waiting for the process to be completed. Simon reminded me that he could make no promises but he was empathetic to my dilemma and wished the best of luck. The "Auto-Reply" I received : Dear The North Face customer, 　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　 We have received your email and are looking forward to handling your request. Our regular turnaround time is of 5 to 10 business days but may be exceeded during peak business periods (August to March). We answer all correspondence in sequential order. 　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　 Thank you for contacting The North Face warranty service The warranty team So at least 3 weeks to get a replacement jacket ( if I'm lucky ) with a good chance that I still have to send it back as requested in the warranty process. Also, this color is no longer available so another compromise has to be made from the customer, sigh ! My experience so far with North Face has been disappointing to say the least. I can't return this item to a "Bricks and Mortar" 40 min away as according to customer service, they will advise me to send the garment back to Quebec. If you want to replace your jacket frequently and don't mind compromising on quality and color, then feel free to keep supporting North Face. I would spend more and buy something that gives you a serviceable life longer than one season or less. "Fashion verses Function" you decide.

I've been very happy with it and would recommend it as use as an outer shell, but not an only layer because it's not very breathable. For me, that's not a big deal. When I'm done wearing, I turn it inside-out to let the interior dry out on the back of a chair. Just know, if you're doing physical activity, and this is the only layer against your skin, the sweat it's not going to wick away or evaporate. PRO's: Great wind and rain protection. Lightweight. Easily packable. Roomy side pockets. Good fit. CON's: Breathability (holds perspiration inside). Pricey.

I like that the side snap button didn't pop once, this was an annoying and constant problem with my previous bib from a different brand. The side cut is high enough to keep the snow out on a pow day and the vents are going to be clutch for sunny spring days. The straps stayed in place and didn't need to be adjusted during the day. The pockets are good too, I would have preferred a zipper on the leg side pocket but the rest of the pockets have zippers so this is minor feedback. reviews.title: Poor Quality and Down/Feather Leakage
reviews.text: I would not recommend purchasing the The North Face Men's Aconcagua 3 Hoodie based on my experience. I bought this jacket brand new, and within just a few days of use, feathers and down started coming out from multiple areas, including the sleeves, body, and pockets. This issue did not improve over time, in fact, it continued for weeks and still happening to date, making the jacket look worn and poorly made. I contacted The North Face customer service, and they advised that this was "normal" and suggested washing the jacket. I followed all care instructions carefully, but the problem persisted. The ongoing loss of down not only affects the appearance but also raises concerns about the jacket's ability to retain warmth over time. What's most disappointing is the lack of support from customer service. Despite clearly explaining the issue, no meaningful resolution was offered. This experience does not reflect the quality or reliability I expected, especially from a brand that promotes durability and a lifetime warranty. I've owned jackets from other brands, even more affordable and cheaper ones, none of them have this issue. Unfortunately, due to both the product quality and the poor and unacceptable customer service experience, I would not consider purchasing from this brand again.

reviews.title: I WILL buy this coat again ... once I wear it ragged!
reviews.text: I picked up the Men's Aconcagua 3 Jacket from The North Face after wearing my last North Face coat completely ragged, and I'm really glad I gave a different style a shot. I'll admit, I was hesitant at first. When you find a jacket you love, switching it up feels risky. But this one won me over fast. It's warm without feeling bulky, lightweight but still does the job on cold days, and easy to layer when the temperature really drops. The fit is clean and modern, not puffy or oversized, which makes it easy to wear pretty much anywhere. Running errands, heading to work, walking outside, or just being out and about, it works for all of it. It looks good enough that you don't feel like you're just wearing a "weather jacket." Best of all, it passed the toughest test. I got full approval from the teens, tweens, and my partner, which honestly says everything. If a jacket can check that many boxes, it's doing something right. If you're looking for a dependable, comfortable jacket that looks good, wears well, and feels like something you'll reach for every day, the Men's Aconcagua 3 is a solid pick. I'd absolutely buy it again.

reviews.title: Soft and warm, my go-to puffer
reviews.text: I'm a 28yo male 5'11" with an athletic build, and I bought this jacket in size M (navy). Overall, this jacket is fantastic, super versatile, and exactly what you'd expect from TNF-reliable quality and performance. In 40-60ºF weather, it keeps me perfectly warm with just a t-shirt underneath. If the temperature drops below that, you'll likely need an extra layer. The insulation does a great job trapping body heat while remaining breathable. It handles light rain (typical Seattle weather) very well, as it's water-resistant but not fully waterproof. A minor downside is that I've noticed a few feathers escaping after a couple of standard washes, but this can happen with down jackets. Regarding pockets: Some reviews were unclear about whether it has an inside pocket, so let me clarify-it doesn't have a classic inner chest pocket. The jacket only includes two zippered side pockets. However, the lining of these side pockets isn't fully stitched at the top on the inside of the jacket. While this technically creates an extra "pocket," it's not designed for use, and you'll feel anything stored there when using the side pockets. Since the product doesn't advertise an inner pocket, this isn't a dealbreaker for me. The jacket performs exactly as promised, so it's still a solid 5 stars.

reviews.title: Bring on Iceland!
reviews.text: As a South Florida resident for the past 48 years, I don't find myself needing a heavy winter coat often. But this year, we were traveling to NY in early February, so my layered sweaters and sweatshirts were not going to cut it. I had an old (15 years,...) winter ski jacket, that must have weighed 20 pounds, not ideal for travel. I asked around and was told Northface is the way to go for a lightweight winter jacket, for extreme temps. I went online, looked at the various styles and colors, and went with the Terra Peak Hoodie. I could not believe how light it was, and could not understand how this could keep me warm. Well, I soon found out what a great purchase I had made. Temperatures were in the 20's with strong winds, and I was toasty as can be. The hood is perfect for keeping the wind out and I quickly realized that I did not need to wear various layers underneath, becasue the jacket kept me warm. Additionally, it is so light and compact for travel, I was able to stick it in my carry-on bag with no problem. We are going to Iceland later in the year, and I am ready!

reviews.title: Great quality, poor design
reviews.text:
I've had the two-man version of this tent for 12 years and it's still going strong. 

I camp at least 45 days a year.  

I loved the two man tent so much that I bought the one man tent for backpacking. 

Here's the good and bad: 

Good: excellent quality as you would expect from a North face product.

Very lightweight for this price point. A 3 lb something ounce tent for under $200 made at this quality can't be found elsewhere. 

Very compact when in the stuff sack. It was the smallest item In my backpack. 

Very quick and easy to set up buy one person. 

Very waterproof. 

Bad:

It does not vent well. The vestibule zips open in a straight line from the Apex of the tent down to the ground.  Even when you try to crack the vestibule open The draft flap keeps the zippered portion closed.  I had a major buildup of condensation on the inside of the tent.  

The tent walls pitch inward as they approach the apex of the tent.  This might not seem like a big deal but when you have condensation on the inside of your fly, it gets your gear wet because you're brushing up against it.  Also the shape of the tent means that when you have the fly open, any moisture rolling off the top of the rain fly falls directly inside your tent since the top of the tent is narrower than the bottom. 

Conclusion:

If this tent had a cross beam on top like the two man does and the walls of the tent pitched straight up instead of inward like a pyramid, this would be the perfect sub $200 backpacking tent. 

Unfortunately I woke up in 26° weather, a soaked down bag and the entire inside of my rainfly frozen with condensation That dripped all over my gear inside the tent as it defrosted. 

I'm looking at the MSR Elixir 1 tent.  It has all of the suggested features above and you only sacrifice about 3/4 of a pound to get it. 

If North face fixes the design on their one-man stormbreak tent, I'll buy it immediately.  

In fact I'm going to retire my 12-year-old two men tent and buy another two-man storm break tent from North face.  Best value in tents that can be found
