reviews.title: Exactly what I needed it to be.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've already got the Stormbreak 2, but I wanted to give the one person tent a go. I purchased the Stormbreak 1, for solo outings where shedding a few pounds in my Terra 65 would be beneficial on longer hikes. I'm a tall guy and at 6'4", I probably max out what length capacity this tent can hold, but I knew this as I'd spent a good bit of time researching reviews already. Setup is quick and easy, literally under 5 minutes. Two pole setup and if you need the rain fly, there is color coding to match it up with the tent itself. Two inside pockets give you room to place a few essentials - flashlight, book, cell phone, charging banks, etc. Provided tent stakes lean a little on the heavy side, if you want to shed more weight, look into some lighter stakes either on this site, or elsewhere. Rain fly keeps the rain out perfectly, as experienced in the rain forests of southeast Alaska. All in all, the Stormbreak 1 was exactly what I needed it to be: a tent option, for when roominess isn't as necessary as being lightweight. Taller humans 6'3" or above might want to make sure they're ok without a lot of interior space, but otherwise, this checks the boxes for lightweight and minimalist in all the ways I needed.

Staking it out, I have no doubt this tent would stand up to bad weather. Getting in and out of the single door is easy and the vestibule provides just enough space to drop your boots, not much else. The not so good. I'm 6 foot, 185 lbs and felt I was sleeping in a coffin! Head to toe, there wasn't much room. My sleeping pad filled the floor space. When laying down, the interior of the tent was pressing/touching my head. My feet were pushing on the other end. Sitting up, I had no head room, just had to push into the interior of the tent. If you're a bit claustrophobic, this may invoke a few emotions! In the end, I was tired enough and just closed my eyes and went to sleep. In short, this is a great tent for shorter people or those that don't mind small spaces.

questions.text: For a minimalist/survival kit, could this be set up using just the poles and tent cover (ie would it be stable without the bug mesh interior)?

answers.text: Absolutely! The North Face Stormbreak 1 Tent can be used in a minimalist setup with just the poles and tent cover, leaving out the bug mesh interior. This configuration, often called 'fastpacking' or 'fly-only pitching,' is perfect for anyone looking for a lightweight shelter option—whether it's for a survival kit or an ultralight backpacking adventure. Just keep in mind that its stability and ability to handle weather will depend on how well the tent cover is secured to both the poles and the ground.

reviews.title: Great Tent, Customer Service Terrible
reviews.text: I purchased the Wawona 6 tent and have had the joy of using it 3 times it is a wonderful tent for my family. The tent pole blew out on our last trip, I opened a case with North Face and it took 3 weeks to get an RMA opened with me constantly pushing on the team to respond. After the case was finally approved I was told it would take 8+ weeks for repair. There are no options to purchase a replacement. Due to an upcoming camping trip I was forced to purchase and build my own replacement pole which cost me significant time, energy, and money. This is a great tent but save your money and time buy from another company who stands behind their products and customers.
reviews.author: Joe

reviews.title: The Right Tent for the Right Kind of Adventure
reviews.text: We're car campers in a Rivian R1S, usually building out a full basecamp with an awning, lounge tent, and kitchen for longer stays. For our shorter trips though-when we just need to roll in, set up, and get some sleep-the North Face Wawona 6 has become the ideal setup. We already love our Gazelle T-Hex Overland, but the Wawona 6 fits perfectly into the "lighter pack-out" side of our system. Setup is straightforward and fast (about ten minutes with two people), and the structure feels more refined than most tents in this size class. It's tall enough to stand in, the ventilation is excellent, and the front vestibule makes the whole footprint feel bigger than it is. We paired ours with the Wawona XL ground tarp, which extends the vestibule into a small outdoor room-great for muddy shoes, dog towels, or a dry coffee spot when the Pacific Northwest drizzle kicks in. On our last trip, we ran it beside the Kammok Crosswing awning off the Rivian, creating a covered path between vehicle and tent. It's a small thing, but it makes camp life smoother. For anyone car camping with dogs or a mix of gear (coolers, chairs, induction cooktop, projector, etc.), this tent strikes that balance between comfort and agility. It feels built for people who want quality and space without dragging along a full expedition rig. In short: well made, thoughtfully designed, and perfectly suited for car campers who build their setups with intention.

reviews.title: Perhaps the perfect family camping tent...
reviews.text: We just took this tent (family of four; two kids under 10) camping for three nights at a National Forest campground high in the Rockies. The layout of the tent is PERFECT for car camping, IMO. The vestibule is a great integrated design that functions so well with two doors. When it rained every afternoon, as it does in the mountains, we could take refuge in the waterproof vestibule and play games with plenty of room for four chairs and a little table. When a neighbor showed up on one side, we just kept one door closed for privacy. The ceiling height inside the tent is great for grown-ups changing and moving around, and plenty of pockets and loops allowed for storage, light sticks, and LED night-lighting options for the evenings. We didn't encounter any severe weather, but the options to guy out the tent are numerous and a few extra guy lines are included. This was important peace-of-mind because our last tent collapsed on us and broke a pole during a 4am gust front from an approaching thunderstorm, with no way to stabilize it. It got fairly warm a couple of the days even at 9,400' elevation, and we employed the multiple venting options to prevent the interior from getting too stuffy so we could go in and change or if a kiddo wanted to relax on the bed or nap. We closed it down when the evenings got cool and it seemed to prevent drafts and did stay a little warmer than the outside, but I doubt it would do too much during cold winds. Another advantage to having the vestibule is that you can have a bucket toilet in there for the evenings when the gals don't want to trudge over to the vault toilet in the dark. Overall I couldn't find much to complain about with this initial outing. We added a tarp for added ground protection, which I think is necessary with rocks and pine cones/needles under there, and I would also add an aluminum sleeve splint for the potential emergency with a snapped aluminum pole.

reviews.title: Stop looking and buy it already
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We purchased this tent for my wife and I and our 3 year old. I think it's perfect size for us and possibly one other child. Three adults would be tight but doable. I'm 6'2 and wanted the height it offers, I can confirm it's excellent. We had two Exped mega mat 10 (long wide) next to each other and could fit one more. Our heads were at the back door and feet towards the vestibule and we had a solid 2 feet of room the whole width of the tent to the door for changing and gear. The vestibule is an absolute game changer. I couldn't imagine not having it now. Fits plenty of gear and even at my height it is awesome. I do have to duck a bit coming into it but it's not a big deal at all. I set the tent up the first time with the help of my toddler and we still managed to do it in about 15 minutes. The main body is pretty simple and the lengths of strap on the eyelets for the poles help out quite a bit when locking the poles in. The rain fly was a bit confusing at first to figure out the orientation but now we got the process down and it's pretty easy to get right. There is plenty of guy line spots and there are extra lines included. All in all I love this tent and highly recommend it. As for the bad so far there really isn't much. The stakes are pretty terrible in anything other than grass but I expected that and brought some large nails to use instead. The few stakes I did use bent badly in packed dirt but I don't really count that against the tent. When tying down the vestibule make sure the door is zipped shut and don't tighten that side up too much as it makes the door hard to re zip when opened. Before you set it up the first time watch a couple YouTube videos because the directions are terrible. The bag is great and you don't have to get to crazy with rolling the tent up to get it back in. As of now I couldn't recommend this tent any more than I already do. I don't regret it at all.

reviews.title: One of the greatest tents ever made
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I can't praise this tent enough. I've used it several times since I bought it but last week I put it to the ultimate test, sleeping through a hurricane and remaining dry. We spent over 12 hours in no less than an inch of standing water around us- combined with the matching footprint, this tent's sturdy floor remained almost completely dry throughout. I did not notice a single drip from the roof, and the floor had mild condensation at worst, which I found amazing given that it had essentially become a waterbed. We left once the sun was shining the next morning, dry and comfortable. I can't say if this tent would be great for high wind but it is very sturdy and has numerous support lines for added tension in the worst case scenarios. Given a big enough group, it could even work for backpacking. Whoever carries it would certainly need to swap out some gear with the rest of thier party (it's 20lbs) but when bundled in 2 sections it is easily packable even on smaller hiking bags.

Tent is very versitle fitting two full sized cots and gear storage with lots of room to spare. Pockets and hanging loops work wonders for lamps and gear storage. Some reviewers said the zippers get caught in the fabric but with a technique of putting your finger inbetween while zipping, no problems even when soaking wet. Pros: Optional vents keep it cool in rainy weather, good amount of windows to open, plenty of interior storage pockets, cords running along the top are great for hanging up damp stuff. Vestibule is roomy enough for a shoe pile, a firewood stack, or a quick meal in rainy weather. Zippers work smoothly. reviews.title: Passed w flying colors - highly recommended!!
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The bar was high. 8 incident free years camping with a pair of REI Basecamp 6 tents. We spend 6-8 days on the Lake Michigan shoreline. We've experienced sustained winds of 30-40 mph and torrential rains. Bad equipment decisions can ruin your week. We introduced the Wawona 6 this year. I'll share some comparative notes... - set up was a breeze - prob 20 minutes to get it staked down - guylines included - tent poles are rigid and more robust than the thinner, REI poles. We never have had an issue with the REI poles but I suspect the TNF poles provide better structural support. - Space; like the Basecamp 6, you will find it cramped to fit 6. 4 is a good number. 2 is great. Now - the BIG difference is the massive vestibule and generous clearance in the Wawona that set this apart from the Basecamp. - Comfort; another positive feature for us is ventilation. The Wawona "breaths" so much better. Single walled and many more vents. - Utility; With the vestibule the TNF tent wins. Both have ample storage pockets within. - Weather resistance; both tents are outstanding. You can't go wrong with a well-made geodesic dome design. We've camped with others who've used top of the line Sierra Designs, Big Agnes and Eureka tents. They look nice but don't hold up the same in in-climate weather. - Overall..we are impressed. This tent delivered on it's first test. We will see if it holds up long term!! Happy camping!!

reviews.title: Definitely not 6 person, 4 at best.
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First time setting up took a bit of time as there are no directions included with the tent, but figured it out after 20+ mins. Like that it is big and tall at the center but even with 2 air mattresses only 4 people fit in it comfortably (not sure how 6 would!) Don't like that the main entrance to the tent on the vestibule side is only mesh and doesn't have a solid door. I don't know how we are going to keep warm in the cold mountains of Colorado with only a mesh door. Love the enclosed vestibule, it for 4 of us in it with our camping chairs (kind of cramped but we made it work) when the wind really picked up and we thought it was going to rain. Needed to add an extra tarp to the floor of the vestibule as the tiny footprint mat wasn't big enough. Overall it's a good tent, just wish some of those other things would get fixed about it to give it a 5 star review.

Very spacious - for someone over 6 feet tall this is very comfortable. Super happy I purchased this and will be taking it all over.

reviews.title: Glamping Fortress
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] A formidable fortress, a roomy abode, and after four decades of searching, my favorite tent. Loved the V1.0 so much I just picked up the newer version. TNF has tamed the difficulties with setting up V1.0 and improved the design by going with a rain fly attached to the vestibule. I'm 6'6" and have easy headroom. I use a queen air bed and there's plenty of extra room. For me the best part, what sets this tent apart, is the front vestibule. It's brilliant, spacious and tall. Shrugged off thunderstorms & snow squalls and kept comfy down to 20F. Love it! O.K. it's huge. Not for everyone. But if a bomber base camp with high comfort is your goal check out this bad boy.
reviews.author: Sleepy Bear

reviews.title: My fiancée and I love this tent
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My fiancée and I have had this tent for a little over a year and have no issues with it. It has kept us dry in the rain, blocked moderate wind and made every camping trip great. The large vestibule is an amazing design (something I was specifically looking for). When it rains, we just put our full size folding table and chairs in the vestibule, listen to some music and have food and drinks laid out on the table. It's done a fantastic job keeping us dry and away from wind every time we used it. The vents at the top keeps us dry when it rains but allows for adequate ventilation and all the storage you can use inside is unmatched. Lastly, it usually takes us between 5-8 minutes to put up but we take our time and it is extremely simple to put up with the color coded sleeves. I would recommend this for anyone camping with a small family. The only "downside" I see with this tent is that it does take 2 people to put it together.

reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Did my research so I knew what would best serve our small families needs and what to expect. Its exactly how I thought it would be minus the the minor shortfall on the vestibule length in front. Very solid and roomy.

reviews.title: Great for weeklong trips
reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We've used this tent for a year now in everything from hot dusty dry, to rainy and windy, from the desert to the mountains, to the lakeshore. It is a great tent with a great amount of space and the vestibule makes for a great versatile area, we've put our bikes in there on mountain biking trips, its great to take off wet clothes out of the rain before climbing in your tent, and its a great place to put a chair and have some sitting room. My only real complaint is that the vestibule walls don't come all the way down to the ground and there is a couple inch gap that wind does find its way under but I haven't really found it to be problematic. Overall a great tent that gets compliments every time we go out.

reviews.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Had one full day where it was heavy rain. Windy at night with 40+mph gust. Tent held up perfect. A few drops of water here and there inside the tent but it probably was condensation. The vestibule was really useful. Only thing I would have liked was if the front door had the option for a full cover instead of just the mesh, it might have helped when it got cold at night to keep some of the cold air out and the warm air from the heater inside.
reviews.author: Wai

reviews.title: Legit Tent
reviews.text: Bought this tent for an annual camping trip to Lake McConnaghey NE.  First night in camp we found out there were TS in the forecast.  We watched storms pass north and south of us in the evening. About midnight, we got hit. 50-60 mph winds and serious rain for over an hour as a big TS passed directly over us.  Several tents in our campground failed outright.  Most of the others leaked severely or floated on the water streaming through the camp.  Our tent flexed and swayed in the wind but remaint solid and dry throughout.  The soil is pretty sandy in that area, so some better spikes might have helped with the water and wind, but the tent held up well. It definitely wasn't part of the plan to ride out a serious thunderstorm, but I was glad I bought a quality tent. (during the storm, the thing running through my mind was the reviews I'd read on this tent).  The rest of the weekend was great.  Lots of room inside, definitely warm inside when it's 100F outside, but a solar fan made it quite comfortable overnight.  Glad I bought this one and would totally recommend it.  If you buy, watch the set up videos, the instructions are accurate but a just pictures.

reviews.title: I would absolutely buy this tent again!!!
reviews.text: I have used this tent for the past three or four years and it is great!! Very roomy, plenty of head space and room for two full size cots. Once I learned to set it up, it's up in less than 15 minutes. The design really helps keep it dry even if am setting it up in the rain as there is no rain fly! The front vestibule is huge and has plenty of room for my two chairs and table...which is where I have the coffee maker for early morning coffee in bed! The back vestibule is great for gear storage or other non necessities. The two drawbacks are that the big side windows open from the outside of the tent and some water has pooled toward the vestibule, causing a drip. I used an extra pole for the latter to keep the material taught allowing the rain to run off. On the former it's just not that big of a deal, as I prop the vents out on top and leave the front vestibule 1/8th of the way open and she has plenty of ventilation. I have also closed the whole thing up and stayed toasty warm! Dr. J. Seriously I have a PhD in Camping!

reviews.title: Terrible fit, but very high quality jacket
reviews.text: I just got this year's version of this jacket as a warranty replacement for the same model from the 2023 season. As you'd expect from a $700 TNF product, the quality and materials and fit and finish are top notch. However, the fit is awful. This jacket seems to be designed for short people with large beer bellies. I'm 6'1", 180 lbs, athletic build, wide shoulders, no belly, 44" chest, and I bought this jacket in size L. It fits quite well in the shoulders and chest (bonus points for the high and tight armpit holes and properly long sleeves), but the sleeves themselves have WAY too much material (the width/diameter is absurd, even with the adjustable velcro cuffs tightened all the way). Additionally, the torso of the jacket (below the chest) has SO much extra fabric - it poofs out and looks like I'm wearing a tent. (I guess if I had a big ol' gut, this extra fabric would be appreciated.) Finally, this jacket isn't long enough for my tastes. It barely comes down far enough to cover my butt, meaning that any movement in my arms or shoulders causes the jacket to ride up much higher than I would like.

I exchanged for a small, and it fit perfectly except for the armpits. Way too tight, felt like I was wearing my wife's tshirt in the armpit area. Really bummed by the fit, because this jacket is great quality and style.

reviews.title: Solid wind/cold performance vs. other jackets; an essential
reviews.text: Have been a Patagonia nano puff jacket wearer for some time and needed a step up in thermal performance. This was definitely it! The fit is similar to a Patagonia nano puff large size, with a little more room in arms and waist. It felt a bit too spacious at first, but with layers it fits nicely. at first wear, I had scraped against a side of a truck while biking and.... NO DAMAGE! great durability test on the jacket day one (also I'm ok no injury). compared to the nano puff, I don't need extra layer to stay warm in Chicago winters. It's help up nicely so far; looks sharp with work clothes or other occasions. I thought it may be too shiny compared to what I was used to wearing, but it's actually pretty great -- not as shiny as others I've seen (e.g. Outdoor Research, etc) Sound: while walking, moving arms, there isn't that dreade "swish-swoosh" sound that you may get from other materials like down jackets. I appreciate down, but it's usually a sound problem like you're wearing a diaper. Not so with this jacket. Also I found TNF down jackets I wear a size up from my regular for best fit. Will see how jacket does for future seasons, I'm happy so far.

reviews.text: These shoes are great. I wear a size 9 in street shoes and initially purchased a size 8, which was way too uncomfortable. However, sizing down half a size to an 8.5 has worked well; they are still very tight, but great for more technical routes. The rubber is super sticky, which works well with smearing. Also, they are easy to put on with two heal tabs and a stretchy upper sole. I mostly climb 5.10-11s and these shoes do everything I need them to.

reviews.title: Style changes 👎
reviews.text:
I've had a couple of pairs of the UpMocc and they've been my favorite shoe. The rubber is the stickiest and most trustworthy I've had, the shoe has proven very comfortable. Now this shoe has been "updated" I ordered my normal size, and they felt a lot narrower. I first thought maybe it was the thicker rubber on the toe cap and rand; not as much give. I exchanged them for half a size up and they were still uncomfortably narrow. I took a measuring tape to compare my old shoe to the new, and at the ball of the foot it's about 1/3in narrower than my old, smaller sized shoe. The inside edge/big toe area is cut straighter instead of the rounded shape on the old shoe, so there's less room for the big toe. I know shoes are very individual because bodies vary so greatly, but these style tweaks have turned what was my favorite shoe into an instant loser. 

When I bought the same model shoe, I expected roughly the same product, but this is a totally different shoe. If it ain't broke, don't fix it. Bring the old Mocc back please 🙏

reviews.title: One Slipper To Rule Them All
reviews.text:
As a self claimed slipper connoisseur, these are just the best. After the OG Five Ten moccs (little red rockets) were changed, I searched far and wide for the next best thing. The Up Mocc is IT. Sized appropriately, these have a fantastic performance aspect to them that a lot of slippers get wrong. The heel will actually hold most heel hooks, unless you really need to crank on a small edge. The toe is much more precise than other slippers and translates well to small edges without sacrificing smearing performance. The toe rubber is an added bonus for toe hooks.

I sized down 1 full size from street and have found them perfect. They are slightly tight to begin with, but stretch nicely. The toe rubber prohibits too much stretching in the upper and keep the shoe performance oriented. A issue I've found with past slippers is that the upper will stretch too much with lots of wear and performance will fade. Time will tell, but so far no concerns with overstretching on the upper due to the added toe rubber. 

BUY THEM NOW!
